regular:0.name: Tacos al Pastor
regular:0.desc: Pork meat marinated in achiote, cooked in vertical spit and served with pineapple and fresh cilantro.
hints: It has roots in Arab immigration to the American continent
It is cooked in a vertical rotating spit, just like the shawarma
The fresh pineapple on top is the differential and secret touch
Born in the night taquerías of the capital of the country
The blue corn tortilla is its most handmade variant

regular:1.name: Mole Poblano
regular:1.desc: Complex dark sauce with more than 20 ingredients: dried chilies, bitter chocolate and spices.
hints: It has more than 20 different ingredients in its preparation
Chocolate or cocoa is one of its most unexpected elements
A city in the center is disputed with Oaxaca the honor of creating it
It may take whole days to prepare for its complexity
Served on turkey or chicken at weddings and important celebrations

regular:2.name: Chiles en Nogada
regular:2.desc: Chile populace stuffed with picadillo with fruit, covered in white walnut, red pomegranate and green parsley.
hints: The three colours of the dish represent the national flag
La nogada is a white salsa made with walnut from Castile
Only prepared in August and September for the pomegranate season
Puebla created it to celebrate the Trigarante Army in 1821
It is one of the most complex and festive dishes in the country

regular:3.name: Pozole Rojo
regular:3.desc: Dense peanut corn soup with pork, guajillo chili and spicy broth.
hints: Peanut corn is its main ingredient
It is decorated with lettuce, radishes, oregano and lemon when serving
It has pre-Hispanic origin and is associated with ancient ceremonies
The state of Guerrero claims it as its emblematic dish
It is consumed especially on September 15th, homeland night

regular:4.name: Cochinita Pibil
regular:4.desc: Pork meat marinated in achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaf and cooked underground.
hints: Pibil means 'cooked underground' in the Yucatecan Mayan language
achiote and sour orange are the flavors that define it
It is accompanied by pickled purple onion and habanero pepper
Yucatan is the region where he was born and where he best prepares
The intense orange red color comes from the natural achiote

regular:5.name: Chilaquiles
regular:5.desc: Maize totopes bathed in red or green sauce with cream, cheese, onion and chicken or egg.
hints: The name comes from the Nahuatl and means 'submerged in chili'
They're Sunday's favorite breakfast all over the country
The sauce can be red or green
They are accompanied by refried beans and avocados almost always
The trick is that totopos absorb the sauce but don't break

regular:6.name: Birria de Res
regular:6.desc: Beef stew in dried chilies and spices broth, native to the state of Jalisco.
hints: Jalisco is the state that claims its origin with greater pride
Served with separate broth to soak the tortilla
The birria tacos are wet in the broth and fried in comal
Cinnamon, clove and cumin are key spices
The original version was made with goat, not beef

regular:7.name: Paella Valenciana
regular:7.desc: Rice cooked in paellera with saffron, chicken, rabbit, green beans and garrofon.
hints: Saffron gives the characteristic golden color to rice
The name comes from the flat pan of two handles where it is cooked
Valencia is the region that created it and defends it with the most passion
The socarrat—roasted rice from the bottom—is the treasure of the dish
Valencians debate whether seafood is valid in the original recipe

regular:8.name: Gazpacho
regular:8.desc: Cold tomato soup, pepper, cucumber, garlic and olive oil, typical of the south in summer.
hints: It is served cold, ideal for the hot summers of the south of the country
Andalusia is the region where this traditional soup was born
Extra virgin olive oil is an essential ingredient
Not cooked: all ingredients go raw to the mixing glass
The salmon is his thickest cousin and also very famous

regular:9.name: Tortilla Española
regular:9.desc: Thick egg and fried potato tortilla, cooked over low heat and served at room temperature.
hints: Its main ingredient is potato, not corn or flour
The eternal debate is whether to bring onion or not to carry it
It is eaten at room temperature, not hot like other eggs
It's the most popular tapeo in bars across the country
The onion version is associated with Galicia and the north of the country

regular:10.name: Pulpo a la Gallega
regular:10.desc: Cooked octopus on potatoes with sweet and spicy paprika, olive oil and thick salt.
hints: Galicia, in the northwest of the country, is the cradle of this dish
The paprika is key in its flavor
Served in round wooden dishes in Galician pulperies
The trick is to cook the octopus well so it's tender
Galician fairs are famous for this dish

regular:11.name: Cocido Madrileño
regular:11.desc: Chicken stew, bacon, morcillo, chorizo, cabbage and potato cooked in pot for hours.
hints: Served in three turns: soup, legume and meat separately
The chickpeas are the main and essential ingredient
Madrid adopted and perfected this dish for centuries
Cooked is eaten on Tuesdays and Thursdays according to tradition
The broth first serves as noodle soup or rice to heat

regular:12.name: Asado Argentino
regular:12.desc: Meat cuts slowly cooked over grilled embers, with chimichurri.
hints: Grill is the sacred instrument of this culinary tradition
Chimichurri — parsley, garlic, vinegar — is the inseparable sauce
Sundays are the traditional day to meet and eat it
The rib and emptiness are the most appreciated cuts
Pampas and their cattle tradition are the reason for this dish

regular:13.name: Empanadas Salteñas
regular:13.desc: Baked empanadas stuffed with knife-cut meat, onion, hard egg and olives.
hints: Salta, in the northwestern Andean region, is the province that created them
The meat is cut by knife — never chopped— for the authentic version
The repellent identifies the filling of each empanada
They carry hard egg and olives
They eat with their hands and never with cutlery according to tradition

regular:14.name: Locro Andino
regular:14.desc: Thick stew of white corn, beans, pumpkin, red chorizo and mondongo, typical of winter.
hints: It is the typical dish of 25 May, festivity homeland Argentina
White corn and pumpkin are its essential ingredients
It cooks for hours over low heat until thickened well
The Andean Northwest is its historic cradle
It is a direct legacy of pre-Columbian indigenous cuisine

regular:15.name: Alfajor Argentino
regular:15.desc: Two tender dough lids with sweet milk, bathed in chocolate or white frosting.
hints: The sweet milk is the essential filling of the classic version
Córdoba and Mar del Plata compete for the best in the country

regular:84.name: Empanada Criolla Uruguaya
regular:84.desc: Baked empanada or fried stuffed with meat, olives, hard egg and onion.
hints: Uruguay adopted them from the Argentine tradition with small variations
They can be baked or fried depending on the preference
The filling carries minced meat, onion, hard egg and black olives
They are eaten as an entrance before the child or as a snack
Bakeries make them fresh twice a day in Montevideo

regular:85.name: Huevos Rancheros
regular:85.desc: Fried eggs on corn tortillas bathed in tomato ranchera sauce and serrano pepper.
hints: Ranchera sauce with tomato, serrano pepper and onion
Served on lightly fried corn tortillas
They are the classic Sunday breakfast of Mexican ranches
They are accompanied by refried beans and sliced avocados
The name comes from ranches in the north of the country

regular:86.name: Elote en Vaso
regular:86.desc: Grenade corn cooked with mayonnaise, cotija cheese, piquín pepper and lemon in disposable glass.
hints: Sold in street stalls in disposable glasses
Dry and salty cotija cheese is essential in the recipe
Piquin pepper and lemon give it the spicy and acidic touch
It is an evolution of the corn in cob with the same ingredients
Mexico City and Guadalajara have the best positions

regular:87.name: Torta Ahogada
regular:87.desc: Salted birot stuffed with carnitas drowned in spicy tree chili sauce.
hints: The birote is a hard, crispy bread from Guadalajara alone
Suffocates —sumerge— completely in chili pepper sauce
Guadalajara, in Jalisco, is the only city where she was born
The average version — medium submerged — is for the less daring
It's so spicy that many tourists can't finish it

regular:88.name: Marquesitas
regular:88.desc: Crispy crepe stuffed with edam ball cheese and cajeta or nutella, typical of Yucatán.
hints: Dutch ball cheese edam is the original and classic filling
The card — goat’s caramel— is the sweetest combination
They roll in a cylinder and eat hot with their hands
Merida sells them at night stalls in the park
They are the most popular nocturnal craving in the entire Yucatan Peninsula

regular:89.name: Caldo Tlalpeño
regular:89.desc: Chicken broth with chickpeas, chipotle smoked chili, epazote and fresh avocado.
hints: chipotle smoked is the element that defines its deep taste
Chickpeas are rare in Mexican cuisine but here they are key
epazote is the essential aromatic herb of this soup
Born in the town of Tlalpan, south of Mexico City
Served with fresh avocado and lemon when eating

regular:90.name: Coctel de Camarón
regular:90.desc: Shrimp in clamato sauce, tomato, cucumber, onion, cilantro and lemon served in glass.
hints: The cry is the base of the salsa, different from ceviche Ecuadorian
Served in high glass with corn toast on one side
Valentina or Huichol sauce adds itchy to everyone’s taste
Veracruz and the Pacific coast are its source areas
It's eaten as a snack in seafood all over the country

regular:91.name: Flautas de Pollo
regular:91.desc: Corn tortillas stuffed with chicken and rolled in cylinder, fried until crispy.
hints: Roll in flute form before frying in hot oil
Served with cream, guacamole, lettuce and cheese crumbled on top
The difference with taquitos is that flutes are longer
Mexico City has them in virtually all markets
They are also made of potato with chorizo or cheese in some regions

regular:92.name: Pescado a la Veracruzana
regular:92.desc: Huachinango fillet in tomato sauce, olives, capers, chilies and Mediterranean spices.
hints: The salsa mixes Mexican tomato with European olives and capers
The huachinango (red snapper) is the most commonly used fish in the recipe
Veracruz, port of the Gulf of Mexico, is its historic cradle
The Spanish influence on the ingredients is very evident in this salsa
It is the most representative dish of the summer cuisine of the Gulf

regular:93.name: Albóndigas en Chipotle
regular:93.desc: Ground beef balls with rice and mint in chipotle broth and tomato.
hints: chipotle smoked gives the characteristic flavor to broth
The mint inside the meat is the differential aromatic touch
Served in abundant broth with vegetables such as zucchini and carrot
It is one of the most common stews in homes in the center of the country
The recipe goes from generation to generation in Mexican families

regular:94.name: Gorditas de Chicharrón
regular:94.desc: Mass of coarse corn cooked in griddle filled with chicharrón pressed with green sauce.
hints: The dough is thicker than the tortilla and opens in half
The pressed chicharrón is already cooked in its own fat
They open on one side like a pocket to put the stuffing
Central Mexico markets sell them early
They are also filled with beans, rajas, tinga or stew of the day

regular:95.name: Pan Dulce
regular:95.desc: Variety of sweet breads — shells, horns, dust— that are eaten at breakfast with coffee.
hints: The shell with its round sugar cover is the most iconic
They are bought in bakeries that bake twice a day
Hot chocolate or pot coffee are your natural companions
Mexico has more than 2000 distinct varieties of sweet bread documented
On Sundays families go to the bakery to choose their assortment

regular:96.name: Gazpacho Manchego
regular:96.desc: Hunting meat stew with unleavened bread cakes, mushrooms and field vegetables in La Mancha.
hints: It has nothing to do with the cold Andalusian tomato gazpacho
It is a hot hunting dish that mixes hare, partridge or rabbit
The cakes of unleavened bread are thrown into the stew at the end
La Mancha, the dry land of the centre, is its only region of origin
It has centuries of history linked to the Manchego shepherds

regular:97.name: Migas Extremeñas
regular:97.desc: Hard bread shredded and fried with chorizo, peppers and garlic, the shepherd's breakfast.
hints: The bread must be hard and dry, never fresh or soft
Sprinkle with water before frying to make it spongy inside
The chorizo and the peppers give it red color and smoky flavor
Extremadura and Castilla claim them as their own dish of the countryside
They are eaten at breakfast, especially in the months of intense cold

regular:98.name: Salmorejo
regular:98.desc: Cold and thick cream of ripe tomato, bread, garlic and olive oil, decorated with ham and egg.
hints: It's thicker and creamier than the gazpacho for the bread it carries
The mature Andalusian summer tomato is the key ingredient
Córdoba is the city that claims it as its emblem dish
Garnished with diced ham Iberian and grated hard egg
It is served cold, ideal for the hot summer of the south of the country

regular:99.name: Bacalao a la Vizcaína
regular:99.desc: Cod desalted in red sauce of choriceros, onion, tomato and olive oil of the Basque Country.
hints: The Basque Country and Navarre compete the most authentic version
Dry chorizero peppers are the most important ingredient
Cod must be desalted for 48 hours before cooking
It is the star dish of Easter in all northern Spain
Txangurro and cod are the kings of Basque marine cuisine

regular:100.name: Pisto con Huevo
regular:100.desc: Sofrito slow tomato, pepper, zucchini and onion with poached egg on top.
hints: It is the simplest and most common dish in Manchega cuisine
The egg can be poached, fried or scrambled above sofrito
Eating with village bread to soak in the sauce and egg
La Mancha and Murcia are the regions where you cook most daily
It is also accompanied with diced ham or fried chorizo

regular:101.name: Tarta de Santiago
regular:101.desc: Moist almond cake ground with sugar, egg and cinnamon, with the Cruz de Santiago powder.
hints: The ground almond completely replaces the wheat flour
It is gluten-free completely natural for its ingredients
The Cross of Santiago decorated with icing sugar is its visual signature
Santiago de Compostela and all Galicia claim it as their own
It is eaten all year but especially on the Camino de Santiago

regular:102.name: Arroz Negro
regular:102.desc: Rice cooked in squid ink with squid, prawns and golden alioli above.
hints: Squid ink gives you the intense black color and marine flavor
It is finished with alioli — garlic and oil — served separately to mix
Valencia and Catalonia have the most recognized versions of the country
sofrito onion and tomato is the essential aromatic base
It is always eaten fresh, never overheated the next day

regular:103.name: Chistorra con Huevo
regular:103.desc: Fine pork sausage spicy with paprika from Navarre, fried and served with egg.
hints: The chistorra is a fine cured sausage typical of Navarre
The red paprika gives you the color and flavor smoked so intense
Fries in its own fat until slightly crispy
It is the most popular pintxo —tapa— in the bars of the Basque Country and Navarre
It is eaten as breakfast or appetizer with bread and young red wine

regular:104.name: Carne Asada Colombiana
regular:104.desc: Beef marinated in beer, garlic and cumin, grilled on the grill with hogao and potatoes creole.
hints: Hogao — sofrito tomatoes and onions — is the key accompaniment
Small yellow creole potatoes are irreplaceable on the plate
Beer in marinade softens meat and gives it special flavor
Weekends are the classic time for family roasting
Bogotá and the Cafetero Axis have the country’s most deeply rooted tradition

regular:105.name: Mazamorra Colombiana
regular:105.desc: Thick corn drink breast cooked in milk with panela, cinnamon and clove of smell.
hints: Peto corn — broken corn — is the basis of this dense drink
The panela — unrefined cane sugar — gives you the special sweetness
It is the most popular dessert and snack in the coffee region
Medellín and the Cafetero Axis sell it in street stalls
It is accompanied with guava sandwich to wet according to tradition

regular:106.name: Sobrebarriga Bogotana
regular:106.desc: Skirt of beef cooked slowly in vegetable broth and then baked with hogao until browned.
hints: The overt belly is the most popular beef skirt cut in the country
It cooks first in pot and then bakes to brown the surface
The hogao —tomato with onion— is placed on top before baking
It is the Sunday dish par excellence in Bogotá and the savannah
Served with rice, potato creole and tomato salad

regular:107.name: Chicharrones de Cerdo
regular:107.desc: Cuts of skin and pork fried until completely crispy, with lemon.
hints: They fry in the pork fat itself without extra oil
The lemon squeezed on top of serving is the indispensable touch
They are the classic accompaniment of the regional country tray
Medellin sells them in street fritangas from very early
The single-skinned version —curito— is the most crispy and appreciated

regular:108.name: Caldo de Costilla
regular:108.desc: Broth of beef rib with potato, onion, cilantro and guascas, the classic Bogotan breakfast.
hints: It is the most emblematic and popular breakfast in Bogotá in the morning
The guasca —herba— gives it the flavor that differentiates it from other broths
Served with whole yellow potato and fresh cilantro chopped on top
The restaurants of Bogotá serve it from 6 in the morning
They say it cures hangovers better than any pharmaceutical remedy

regular:109.name: Patacón con Todo
regular:109.desc: Crushed and fried green banana, covered in hogao, meat, cheese and avocado.
hints: The patacón is fried twice—just like the Puerto Rican tostón—
'With everything' means that it carries all the toppings available on top
The Colombian Caribbean coast is where the most consumed and celebrated
Tomato and onion hogao is the basis of ingredients on top
It's a complete meal on its own that doesn't need an escort

regular:110.name: Bollo de Mazorca
regular:110.desc: Mushroom of tender corn with salt and coastal cheese, wrapped in cob leaf and steamed.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the base dough of the bun
The leaf of the same cob serves as a natural wrap
Salty coastal cheese contrasts with the sweetness of tender corn
The Colombian Caribbean coast is its region of historical origin
Sold on the streets early as a cheap breakfast

regular:111.name: Asopado de Pollo
regular:111.desc: Rice cooked in chicken broth with vegetables, criollo dressing and Venezuelan spices.
hints: The rice is cooked directly in the broth, not apart as always
Creole dressing carries sweet pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro and paprika
It is the dish of convalescence and healing of Venezuela
Every home has its own version that goes from generation to generation
Served in hot deep dish with a repeat next to it

regular:112.name: Pisillo de Chigüire
regular:112.desc: Chigüire (capibara) dried and fried meat with onion, garlic and sweet chili.
hints: Chigüire is the world's largest rodent, abundant in the plains
Its meat is consumed especially in Easter as a tradition
The Venezuelan plains—Apure, Barinas—are its natural territory
The meat melts finely after cooking and drying
It is similar to wicked meat but with a wilder flavor

regular:113.name: Mandocas
regular:113.desc: Maize with ripe banana and white cheese, fried and served at breakfast.
hints: The dough mixes precooked corn flour with ripe banana puree
White cheese is mixed into the dough before molding
They are molded in the form of a small slang before frying
They are the regional breakfast of western Venezuela — Zulia and Mérida —
They eat hot with more white cheese grated on top

regular:114.name: Tumbarrancho
regular:114.desc: Sweet potato dough stuffed with spicy ground meat fried in oil, from Zulia.
hints: It is the most popular street food in Zulia state in the West
The corn dough is thinner than arepa and filled before frying
The filling carries ground meat very well seasoned with spices
Maracaibo is the city where it is sold in every corner of downtown
It is different from the zulian empanada in shape and texture of dough

regular:115.name: Cazuela de Vacuno
regular:115.desc: Bovine broth with potato, pumpkin, choclo, green porotos and rice.
hints: The pumpkin gives the orange color and the sweetness to the broth
Always carry a large piece of meat with bone to give flavor
Green beans and choclo are the most important vegetables
It is the family lunch of cold and rainy days in the south
It is eaten with kneaded bread or brownie to wet in the broth

regular:116.name: Porotos Granados
regular:116.desc: Fresh beans stew with choclo, pumpkin, basil and pork.
hints: Pomegranate beans are fresh — not dry — seasonal beans
choclo — corn — and pumpkin are irreplaceable in the recipe
The fresh basil at the end gives it the scent that sets it apart
It's the Chilean summer dish when the beans are fresh
It is eaten alone or accompanied by a chicken or roast pork prey

regular:117.name: Charquicán
regular:117.desc: charqui stew — dried meat — with potatoes, pumpkin, choclo and crushed peas.
hints: charqui is dried beef in the sun or smoked and salted
Everything is crushed by the end to achieve the rustic texture
It is a dish of pre-Hispanic origin adapted with Spanish meat
Served with a fried egg on top and salad aside
The south and north of the country have slightly different versions

regular:118.name: Mote con Huesillos
regular:118.desc: Cold drink of mote wheat and peach ears in syrup with cinnamon.
hints: Bones are dried peaches — ores — in syrup
The mote is cooked peeled wheat that is soft and chewable
Serve cold in a tall glass with plenty of cinnamon sweet syrup
It is the most traditional and iconic summer drink in the whole country
Sold in street carts for more than a century

regular:119.name: Prietas Chilenas
regular:119.desc: Pig blood sausages with onion, rice and spices, steamed or grilled.
hints: Prietas are the Chilean version of the rice sausage inside
The rice makes them denser and fluffy than the Spanish sausage
They are cooked steamed or grilled at the barbecue on the weekend
They are insurmountable in the Chilean barbecue next to the longanizas
They are served with pebre — cilantro sauce and pepper — to accompany

regular:120.name: Humitas Chilenas
regular:120.desc: Mass of choclo grated with basil and cheese or sugar, wrapped in leaves of choclo steamed.
hints: The choclo is grated raw and mixed with chopped fresh basil
Wrapped in the leaves of choclo itself and tied
The sweet version carries sugar and the salty one has cheese inside
They're tamal South — unlike tamal Northern Dry Corn —
Fresh basil is the ingredient that makes them unique

regular:121.name: Ropa Vieja Canaria
regular:121.desc: Chickpeas with shredded pork, chorizo, pepper and cumin from the Canary Islands.
hints: The Canary Islands have its own version different from that of Cuba
Cumin and paprika are the spices that define it in the islands
The chickpeas are the basis that the difference of the Cuban
It is the most consumed dish in Canarian homes during winter
Served with wrinkled potatoes — cooked sea salt papas — next door

regular:122.name: Papas Arrugadas
regular:122.desc: Small potatoes cooked in water with a lot of sea salt until wrinkled, with red or green mojo.
hints: They cook with so much salt that the water almost crystallizes at the end
The skin wrinkles and covers salt when the water evaporates completely
The Canary Islands are their only place of origin and production
The spicy red mojo is the most traditional accompaniment
The small Canarian potato variety is irreplaceable in the recipe

regular:123.name: Gofio Canario
regular:123.desc: Roasted cereal flour — wheat or millet — used in pouters, scaldons and desserts.
hints: Gofio is cereal flour or roasted legumes before grinding
It is the base food of the Guanche diet—canarian indigenous—for centuries
It is mixed with milk, broth or water to make the scald
The Canary Islands have been exporting it to all Latin America for centuries
It is so versatile that it enters soups, desserts, smoothies and breads

regular:124.name: Rondón Caribeño
regular:124.desc: Soup of fish and seafood in coconut milk with cassava, banana and ball of dough, from the Caribbean.
hints: It is the most representative dish of the root community of San Andrés
Coconut milk is the liquid base that differentiates it from other broths
The baked banana dough ball gives you the characteristic texture
San Andrés and Providencia, islands in the Colombian Caribbean, are their cradle
The Afro-Caribbean and English influence is evident in its ingredients

regular:125.name: Mamona Llanera
regular:125.desc: Young calf roasted whole in rod to wood fire for hours in the eastern plains.
hints: Mamone is beef under one year of age raised in pasture
Tears into wooden sticks around a wood fire
The eastern plains—Meta and Casanare—are their natural territory
It is the festive dish of herd farmers of the Llanera tradition
Served with cooked cassava and hot pepper on the side

regular:126.name: Pepitoria de Gallina
regular:126.desc: Hen in a sauce thickened with egg yolks, almonds, saffron and dry sherry.
hints: It is one of the oldest dishes in medieval Castilian cuisine
Egg yolks and thick almonds sauce naturally
The saffron gives the intense golden color and floral aroma
Dry sherry wine brings acidity and body to the sauce
Appears in the Quijote de Cervantes as a celebration dish

regular:127.name: Cochinillo Asado
regular:127.desc: Lechón less than 21 days roasted in wood oven until it is completely crispy skin.
hints: The piglet must weigh less than 5 kilos for the tender version
The skin should be so crispy that it is cut with the edge of a plate
Segovia and Arévalo are the world capitals of this iconic dish
Roast in wood oven for two hours with only water and salt
Cándido de Segovia inn made it popular internationally

regular:128.name: Caldereta de Cordero
regular:128.desc: Milk lamb stew with pepper, tomato, garlic and white wine from Extremadura and Castile.
hints: The milk lamb is less than 35 days old and only fed with milk
Extremadura and La Mancha are the regions where it is best prepared
It cooks slowly for hours in heavy clay pot
The dried chorizero pepper gives depth and color to the broth
It is the star dish of village slaughters and festivals

regular:129.name: Empanada Gallega
regular:129.desc: Large baking of bread dough stuffed with tuna, sardines or cod with peppers.
hints: It is a large pie that is cut into portions, not individual
The dough is of bread, thicker and fluffy than that of fine wheat
Galicia is the region where he was born and where he best prepares
Tuna or sardine are the most traditional and popular fillers
You eat cold or warm, never hot fresh out of the oven

regular:130.name: Arroz con Leche Español
regular:130.desc: Rice cooked in milk with cinnamon, lemon peel and sugar, served cold with cinnamon above.
hints: It differs from Peruvian by lemon peel in cooking
The powdered cinnamon on top is your visual signature
Asturias boasts the creamiest and most traditional version
It is eaten cold as dessert in weddings, baptisms and communions
The secret is to cook the rice very slowly stirring non-stop

regular:131.name: Sopa de Mariscos
regular:131.desc: Rich broth of prawns, clams and mussels with tomato, saffron and bell pepper.
hints: The saffron gives it the golden color and aroma so characteristic
It is made with the broth to cook the heads and shells of seafood
Galicia, the Basque Country and Catalonia are its most famous regions
The fried bread or the picatotes are placed on top when serving
It is the first star dish of Christmas in all Spain

regular:132.name: Torrejas Españolas
regular:132.desc: Brioche bread soaked in milk with cinnamon and beaten egg, fried and bathed in honey or syrup.
hints: They are the torrijas—not turrets—in their most formal Spanish name
Especially prepared during Holy Week as a religious tradition
The bread must be from the day before so that it absorbs milk well
They bathe in honey, cinnamon syrup or icing sugar when serving
They are the most popular dessert of Lent in all Spain

regular:133.name: Cuy a la Brasa
regular:133.desc: Cobayo roasted whole in coal with chili pepper, cumin, achiote and Andean herbs.
hints: The guinea pig is a farm animal bred in the Andes for centuries
It roasts whole, without tearing, turning on the embers
It is the most important festive dish in Peruvian Andean cuisine
Cusco, Arequipa and Cajamarca are the cities where it is best prepared
Served with native potatoes and peanut sauce or ají amarillo

regular:134.name: Sopa Seca de Fideos
regular:134.desc: Noodles cooked in chicharrón sauce, tomato and ají panca until absorbing all the liquid.
hints: Dry soup is not a soup — noodle absorbs all the broth
The pork chicharrón gives the dish a deep fat flavor
It is the fusion of Italian pasta with Peruvian Andean ingredients
Lima adopted it as a dish of neighborhood and anticucherias
It is cooked in a single large skillet and served directly to the table

regular:135.name: Ocopa Arequipeña
regular:135.desc: Potatoes with ají mirasol sauce, peanuts, huacatay and fresh cheese, typical of Arequipa.
hints: The huacatay – black Andean grass – gives it the dark green color
The ají mirasol dry is different from the ají amarillo and more smoked
Arequipa, the white city of the south, claims it as its own
It differs from potato to huancaine by the huacatay sauce
Cold served on lettuce leaves with olive on top

regular:136.name: Tacu Tacu
regular:136.desc: White rice tortilla and fried beans crushed and golden in skillet, with jumping on top.
hints: Born as a dish to make use of leftovers of rice and beans
It is crushed in the pan until it becomes crispy on the outside and soft inside
It has Afro-Peruvian influence on its colonial historical origin
Served with salted loin, squid or seafood on top
It is the most popular dish in Lima Creole cuisine of African heritage

regular:137.name: Butifarras Limeñas
regular:137.desc: French bread stuffed with ham of the country, onion creole sauce with lemon and ají amarillo.
hints: The ham of the country is a cooked sausage different to Iberian ham
Creole sauce is purple onion in juliana with lemon and cilantro
Peruvian French bread is crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside
It is the most popular street sandwich in historic Lima
It is sold in hot springs and huariques of downtown Lima

regular:138.name: Chicha Morada
regular:138.desc: Cold drink of purple corn cooked with pineapple, quince, cinnamon, clove and sugar.
hints: The Andean purple corn gives it the intense violet color so striking
Pineapple and quince are cooked next to corn for acidity
It is the most consumed non-alcoholic national drink in the country
It is accompanied by purple dungeon to make the classic combined
It has natural antioxidants of purple corn that make it healthy

regular:139.name: Arroz con Gandules Boricua
regular:139.desc: Yellow rice with gandules, sofrito, careo, seasoning and bacon, the island's Christmas dish.
hints: The gandules — guandu — are small green legumes of the Caribbean
The sofrito with careo and sweet aji is the irreplaceable aromatic base
The achiote seasoning gives the yellow color and unique taste
It's Christmas rice and patron saintly parties all over the island
It is cooked in aluminium cauldron to form the glue of the bottom

regular:140.name: Tembleque
regular:140.desc: Coconut milk flan with cornstarch, sugar and cinnamon, served cold with cinnamon powder.
hints: It is made only with coconut milk, cornstarch, sugar and cinnamon
The name comes from the tremor made by gelatin when moving it
It is the most traditional holiday and Christmas dessert on the island
Refrigerate several hours before demolishing on the plate
It is gluten-free naturally and suitable for many special diets

regular:141.name: Carne Guisada Boricua
regular:141.desc: Beef in sofrito sauce, tomato, olives and potatoes, slowly stewed.
hints: The sofrito boricua with caero and sweet aji is the basis of everything
The olives and capers give you the salty touch and briny
It is served on white rice with toast or yellow next to it
It is the most cooked stew in Puerto Rican homes in the world
The pressure cooker speeds it up but the slow version has more flavor

regular:142.name: Pastelón de Plátano
regular:142.desc: Layers of sweet ripe plantain, minced meat and sofrito, topped with melted cheese and baked.
hints: Fried ripe plantain replaces the pasta sheets used in Italian lasagne.
The filling is minced meat cooked with Puerto Rican sofrito.
A layer of grated yellow cheese tops the dish and browns in the oven.
It is a popular home-cooked dish for informal celebrations.
It bakes until the plantain caramelises and the cheese bubbles.

regular:143.name: Arroz Mamposteado
regular:143.desc: White rice scrambled with pink beans, sofrito and bacon, comforting food.
hints: It is made with white rice already cooked mixed with beans
Smashing means mixing in the cauldron stirring everything together
It's the leftover dish that becomes something richer
It is the most comforting and economical homemade food on the whole island
Served as a main dish or as a side dish with roasted meat

regular:144.name: Chicha de Jora
regular:144.desc: Fermented drink of dried jora corn with chancaca and spices, the millenary Andean beer.
hints: Jora maize is germinated and sun-dried before fermenting
It originates in the Inca civilization where it was ritual sacred drink
Chancaca—panel—gives sweetness and accelerates fermentation
Cusco and the central Andes are where the most is still produced
You can consume young — sweet — or fermented — with alcohol

regular:145.name: Locro de Papa
regular:145.desc: Thick potato soup with avocado, fresh cheese, cilantro and milk from the Andean highlands.
hints: The potato cooks until it gets rid of and thickens the broth naturally
Avocado and fresh cheese are put on when serving
Quito and the northern mountains are the areas where it is consumed the most
It is the most comforting soup of the Ecuadorian highlands in winter
It differs from ajiaco Colombians for not carrying guacas or chicken

regular:146.name: Caldo de Patas
regular:146.desc: Breed leg broth with mote, peanuts, milk and spices, the Andean reconstituent.
hints: The leg of beef is cooked for hours until the broth gelatinizes
The ground peanut is mixed in the broth to give it special creaminess
It is served with white mote (cooked corn) and paired pepper to chop
It is consumed especially in the markets of the mountains from early
They say it has restorative properties for the tired body

regular:147.name: Guatita Ecuatoriana
regular:147.desc: Beef calluses in peanut sauce with potato, onion and achiote, the dish of the serrano markets.
hints: The guata is the beef belly clean and cooked for many hours
The ground roasted peanut sauce gives you the unique texture and flavor
Served with white rice, avocado and onion pickle
The markets of Quito, Ambato and Riobamba are the most famous for it
It is the economic and powerful lunch of the Andean markets

regular:148.name: Choclo con Queso
regular:148.desc: Mazorca of Andean corn cooked in water with salt served with fresh cheese from Cajamarca.
hints: The choclo Peruvian has large and soft grains, different from the American
Cajamarca's fresh cheese is the most appreciated to accompany you
Sold in street stalls throughout the day in Lima
The cob is peeled and served hot with cheese next to it
It is the simplest and most popular street snack on the Peruvian coast

regular:149.name: Champús
regular:149.desc: A thick drink of fermented corn with lulo, panela, pineapple, cinnamon and clove, from the suroccident.
hints: The corn is fermented briefly to give it the special acid touch
The lulo — tropical fruit— gives you the typical citrus acidity
Nariño and Valle del Cauca are its historical regions
It is consumed especially in Easter and Christmas by tradition
You drink hot or warm, never cold, and always very thick

regular:150.name: Aborrajados de Plátano
regular:150.desc: Mature banana slices stuffed with peasant cheese, battered in dough and fried.
hints: The banana should be well ripe and sweet for the right recipe
The salty peasant cheese contrasts with the sweetness of the banana
Swallow in a dough of wheat flour before frying
They are the most popular parade of meetings in Valle del Cauca
Cali and the Cafetero Axis are the areas where they consume the most

regular:151.name: Sopa de Tortilla
regular:151.desc: Chicken broth with epazote, roasted tomato and fried tortilla strips with cream and cheese.
hints: The tortilla strips are fried separately and put in the broth at the end
The tomato is roasted before blending to give depth to the broth
The epazote gives you the scent that makes it completely different
It is the first dish of many traditional Mexican restaurants
Crowned with cream, fresh cheese, avocado and fried pasilla pepper

regular:152.name: Tlayuda Oaxaqueña
regular:152.desc: Giant and toasted corn tortilla with seat, black beans, tasejo and Oaxacan cheese.
hints: The tlayuda is a giant tortilla of more than 30 centimeters
Tasejo is dried beef and marinated meat typical of Oaxaca
Quesillo is the yarn cheese produced only in Oaxaca
The seat — chicharrón grease — is smeared as a base on the tortilla
It is the most representative dish of Southern Oaxacan cuisine

regular:153.name: Enchiladas Mineras
regular:153.desc: Tortillas stuffed with potato and carrot bathed in chili guajillo with carrot and lettuce on top.
hints: They are the typical dish of the state of Guanajuato in central Bajío
The filling of potato with carrot is simple but very tasty
The guajillo sauce gives them intense red color and soft itching
Crowned with pickled carrot, onion and chopped lettuce
They're different from other enchiladas because of the vegetable filling

regular:154.name: Aguachile Verde
regular:154.desc: Raw shrimp marinated in cucumber juice, serrano pepper, lemon and cilantro, from the Pacific.
hints: The aquachile is the ' ceviche end' for the most intense itching
The blended cucumber with chili and lemon is the green sauce that defines it
Sinaloa and Sonora, in the northwest of the Pacific, are their historic cradle
Shrimp go completely raw, only marinated in the juice
The red version has red chili instead of green serrano

regular:155.name: Caldo de Pescado
regular:155.desc: Fish broth with carrot, chayote, tomato, pasilla pepper and epazote.
hints: The epazote is the indispensable herb that gives the special aroma
The dried pasilla pepper gives depth and a slight itching to the broth
Served with lemon, onion and chopped serrano pepper apart
The coastal states of the Pacific and Gulf are the ones that prepare it the most
It is the traditional cure of flus and cold days on the coasts

regular:156.name: Pachamanca
regular:156.desc: Meats, potatoes and humitas cooked underground among hot stones with Andean herbs.
hints: Pacha means land and manca means pot in Quechua
The stones are hot red hot and buried with food
Huatia and pachamanca are the two ways to cook underground
It's an Inca millenary tradition that is celebrated in festivities
Ayacucho, Cusco and Huancayo have the most ceremonial versions

regular:157.name: Sopa de Maní
regular:157.desc: Chicken broth with ground peanuts, potato, noodles, rice and vegetables, the Bolivian national dish.
hints: Ground peanut is the ingredient that makes it completely unique
Bring peanuts, potatoes, noodles and rice all together in the same broth
It is considered the most beloved unofficial national dish in the country
Sucre and Cochabamba presume to have the best documented version
Served with a chicken prey and white rice next door always

regular:158.name: Silpancho Cochabambino
regular:158.desc: Fillet of crushed meat and fried empanado on rice, potato and fried egg with salad.
hints: Silpancho is a very thin and large beef fillet empanado
Cochabamba is the most famous gastronomic city in Bolivia
Served on a bed of rice and potato cooked on the plate
The fried egg goes over everything, like a plate crown
The tomato salad and onion with locoto goes separately to accompany

regular:159.name: Tucumanas
regular:159.desc: Fried empanadas stuffed with chicken, cooked potato, egg and spices, from Cochabamba.
hints: They're smaller than the Salta and they fry instead of baking
The filler carries chicken shredded with potato and hard egg
Cochabamba and Santa Cruz are the most sold cities
They are eaten at breakfast or as a snack with madoto sauce
The dough is thinner and crisper than that of the baked saltine

regular:160.name: Sancochado Limeño
regular:160.desc: Cooked meat —res, chicken, cecina — with cassava, sweet potato, choclo, carrot and cabbage.
hints: It is the Madrid cooked adapted to American ingredients
Yucca, sweet potato and choclo replace European chickpeas
Lima adopted it as a Sunday dish in the colonial century
Served with Creole sauce, ají amarillo and rocoto apart
Cooked broth is first served as noodle soup

regular:161.name: Pollo a la Brasa
regular:161.desc: Grilled chicken in soy, ají panca and spices, roasted in rotary oven with fries.
hints: Peru invented the rotary oven to roast grilled chicken in the 1950s
The marinade carries soy, ají panca, cumin, garlic and black beer
Served with fries, salad and the three sauces: green, yellow and red
Lima has more chickens — chicken restaurants — than any other city
It is the most daily dish consumed by Peruvians worldwide

regular:162.name: Champurrado
regular:162.desc: Atole thick corn with bitter chocolate, cinnamon and piloncillo, hot winter drink.
hints: Atole is a corn drink and adding chocolate is called champurrado
The little piloncillo — unrefined brown sugar — gives the smoked sweetness
Mexican chocolate —Granuelita or Ibarra — gives it the special flavor
It is especially drunk on Day of the Dead and Christmas with tamales
It is the best-selling street drink in Mexican winter markets

regular:163.name: Tostada de Ceviche
regular:163.desc: Toast fried corn covered with ceviche shrimp, avocado, onion and lemon.
hints: The toast must be completely crisp to hold the ceviche
ceviche Mexicans wear tomato and Clamato, different from Peruvian
The chopped avocado or the guacamole go over the ceviche on top
It is eaten in a single large bite so as not to lose the creak
Seafood stalls in the Pacific sell them early

regular:164.name: Pozole Verde
regular:164.desc: Coconut corn soup with chicken in tomatillo green sauce, serrano pepper and nuggets.
hints: The green sauce carries tomatillo, serrano pepper, nuggets and epazote
The toasted nuggets give thick and nutty flavor to the salsa
Guerrero, on the Pacific coast, claims this green version
It is decorated as red: lettuce, radishes, oregano and lemon
It is less spicy and more herbaceous than the classic red version

regular:165.name: Sopa Paraguaya de Carne
regular:165.desc: Soup beef with noodles, tomato, onion, paprika and fresh herbs.
hints: Paraguay has its own noodle soup very different from others
The paprika gives red color and sweet flavor to the broth
Served as a first course at family lunches at midday
It's different from the sopa paraguaya solid—which is actually a bread—
Noodles are thick and absorb well the flavor of meat broth

regular:166.name: Asado Uruguayo a la Cruz
regular:166.desc: Lamb or beef roasted on cross of vertical iron over embers of firewood for hours.
hints: The iron cross holds the flesh vertically in front of fire
The lamb on the stick is the most traditional and festive version of the country
Cooks for 4 to 6 hours without rush, with total patience
Montevideo and the cattle ranching interior have the most deeply rooted culture
The meat only carries thick salt, nothing else is needed in the recipe

regular:167.name: Milanesa al Limón
regular:167.desc: Fillet of baked and fried beef, served with plenty of lemon and mixed salad.
hints: The lemon squeezed generously on top is the Uruguayan touch
It differs from Argentina in that it is always served with lemon
Montevideo has rotiserías in every neighborhood specialized in Milanese
The Champignon version carries mushroom sauce on top
It is the most ordered dish in Montevideo homes on Sundays

regular:168.name: Churrasco Uruguayo
regular:168.desc: Fine fillet of grilled beef with chimichurri, tomato, lettuce and crumb bread.
hints: The Uruguayan churrasco is a sandwich, not just grilled meat
Soft white crumb bread is the classic sandwich bread
Parsley and garlic chimichurri is the infallible seasoning
Montevideo has 24-hour barbershops open for nightstanders
It's the night sandwich, the most ordered after midnight

regular:169.name: Flan de Coco Brasileño
regular:169.desc: Creamy flan of condensed milk and coconut milk with dark caramel above.
hints: Coconut milk gives you the creaminess and special tropical flavor
The caramel is made first in the mold before adding the mixture
It is the most popular birthday dessert in the northeast states
Bahia and Pernambuco are the states where they consume most and celebrate
It melts cold and the caramel falls on the flan forming a sauce

regular:170.name: Vatapá Baiano
regular:170.desc: Dense bread paste, dried shrimp, peanuts, coconut milk and Northeastern palm oil.
hints: Dendê oil —palma— gives it the orange color and African flavor
Dried ground shrimps are the protein that gives the marine flavor
It is served inside the carajé — bean bun — in Bahia
It has strong influence from the African Yoruba cuisine of slaves
Salvador de Bahia is the city where you best prepare and eat more

regular:171.name: Acarajé Baiano
regular:171.desc: White bean dough fritter fried in palm oil, filled with vatapa and shrimp.
hints: The dough is made from white beans —feijão fradinho — ground raw
It is fried exclusively in dendê oil that gives it the orange color
Inside goes the vatapa, the dry shrimp and the fresh shrimp salad
Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil formally recognized
The Baianas sell it in Salvador street stalls wearing white

regular:172.name: Feijão Tropeiro
regular:172.desc: Beans with cassava flour, bacon, egg, cabbage and onion from Minas Gerais.
hints: The tripiro is the carrier who carried it on the roads
Manioc flour — farofa — is the most defined ingredient
Minas Gerais is the state that created it to feed travelers
Fried chopped cabbage is the vegetable that gives it a fresh and green touch
Served with rice, roast meat and salad in the mineira food

regular:173.name: Quibe Frito
regular:173.desc: Croquette of ground meat with bulgur wheat, onion and mint, Lebanese Arab heritage.
hints: Came with Lebanese and Syrian immigration to Brazil in the 19th century
Fine ground bulgur wheat is mixed with raw beef
The fresh minty chopped gives it the characteristic Arabic aroma
São Paulo and Rio have the best versions of the Arab diaspora
It's the salt —fried mouth— most consumed in velories and parties

regular:174.name: Pabellón con Barandas
regular:174.desc: Creole Pavilion with extra slices of fried ripe banana and fried egg on top.
hints: The handrails are the banana slices that surround the plate
The fried egg above is the protein supplement added to the base pavilion
It is the most complete and forceful version of the Venezuelan national dish
Some call him a horse pavilion by the egg on top as a rider
It is the most sought after lunch in Venezuelan Creole restaurants

regular:175.name: Chupe de Camarones
regular:175.desc: Creamy soup of shrimps with potato, choclo, rice, egg and ají amarillo from Arequipa.
hints: The river shrimps of Arequipa are the most appreciated in the country
Arequipa is the city where it originated and where it is best prepared
Milk and fresh cheese give you the creaminess that distinguishes it
The ají amarillo gives you the color and itching that makes it unique
It is the Sunday dish in the restaurants of Arequipa

regular:176.name: Locro Ecuatoriano
regular:176.desc: Thick potato soup with milk, fresh cheese, avocado and pork leather, from the saw.
hints: The cooked pork leather gives you completely unique texture and flavor
The potato is undone in the broth to thicken it naturally
Fresh avocado and cheese are added when served over hot soup
Quito claims it as part of its serranian culinary identity
It's different from the locro Argentine because it doesn't carry corn but only potatoes

regular:177.name: Mofongo Relleno
regular:177.desc: Pilón of mofongo filled shrimp to the garlic or meat in creole sauce with a lot of broth.
hints: The mofongo base is fried green banana with garlic and chicharrón
The hot broth is served separately to pour into the pylon
Grilled shrimps are the most popular filling in restaurants
San Juan has restaurants where mofongo is the only dish on the menu
The version with shrimp in its garlic and butter sauce is the star

regular:178.name: Tostones con Salmón
regular:178.desc: Crispy green banana toast with smoked salmon, cream and capers.
hints: This fusion version was born in modern restaurants in Panama City
Smoked salmon and capers give you international elegance
Toas are the crispy base that holds all the ingredients on top
Panama City has the most diverse fusion cuisine in Central America
The canal and geographical position explain the global gastronomic influence

regular:179.name: Bollo de Yuca
regular:179.desc: Mass of yucca grated with salt and white cheese cooked in steamed bijao leaf.
hints: The bijao leaf is a tropical plant that wraps and gives flavor
Raw grated cassava forms the dough without having to cook before
White cheese or chicharrón are the most popular fillings
Veraguas and Azuero are the provinces where it is consumed the most
Served as a breakfast or snack in local rural markets

regular:180.name: Caldo de Pollo Guatemalteco
regular:180.desc: Chicken broth with güisquil, ejotes, corn, mint and rice, the Mayan reconstituter.
hints: Güisquil — chayote — is the most characteristic vegetable of broth
Fresh peppermint at the end is the scent that distinguishes it
Served with freshly made corn tortillas in hot griddle
It is the most prescribed remedy for any disease in the country
Guatemalan grandmothers consider it superior to any medicine

regular:181.name: Ponche Navideño
regular:181.desc: Hot drink of seasonal fruits — tejocote, guava, cane — with tamarindo and piloncillo.
hints: Tejocote (Mexican fruit) is the ingredient that cannot be lacking
The pilloncillo gives the dark sweetness and smoked to the punch
It is specially prepared in December for Christmas inns
The sugarcane in pieces gets whole inside the pot
Served hot in mud jar with cooked fruits inside

regular:182.name: Nopales con Huevo
regular:182.desc: Nopal tender cooked in its juice with scrambled egg, onion, serrano pepper and tomato.
hints: Nopal is the most consumed cactus as vegetables in the country
Cleans from thorns and cuts into cubes before cooking
The drool of the nopal disappears when cooked over live fire with salt
It is the healthiest and cheapest breakfast in traditional Mexican cuisine
Mexico is the only country in the world that consumes nopal as a daily vegetable

regular:183.name: Enchiladas Suizas
regular:183.desc: Corn tortillas stuffed with chicken bathed in cream and green sauce, gratinated with cheese.
hints: The Swiss name comes from the cheese and cream that is used generously
Bake until the cheese bubbles and browns on top
The green salsa of tomatillo is the base that gives them the characteristic flavor
They're different from normal green enchiladas by the gratinate
The Sanborns restaurant in Mexico City popularized them in the 1950s

regular:184.name: Mole Negro
regular:184.desc: Dark Oaxacan sauce with black chilies, bitter chocolate, male banana and more than 30 ingredients.
hints: It is the mole most complex and darkest of Oaxaca's seven moles
The roasted black chilhuacle gives it the color completely black
You can bring more than 30 different ingredients in your preparation
Oaxaca is the city that claims it most as part of its identity
It cooks for days and is the dish of great family celebrations

regular:185.name: Sopa de Lima
regular:185.desc: Chicken broth with Yucatecan sour lime, tomato, xcatic chili and fried tortilla.
hints: Yucateca sour lime is a different citrus to the common lemon
The xcatic pepper is yellow and soft, typical of the Yucatan Peninsula
Crowned with crispy fried tortilla strips when serving
Mérida claims it as her most emblematic and identity soup
It is completely different from lemon in aroma and floral flavor

regular:186.name: Queso Fundido
regular:186.desc: Oaxaca cheese melted in clay pan with Mexican chorizo or poblano pepper slices.
hints: Hebra Oaxaca cheese is the only one that melts correctly for this dish
It is served bobbing in the clay pan directly to the table
Mexican chorizo—uncured—be fried before adding cheese
It is eaten spooning with corn tortillas freshly made in griddle
It is the most demanded entrance in the restaurants of antojitos of the country

regular:187.name: Barbacoa de Borrego
regular:187.desc: Borrego wrapped in maguey pencas cooked in earth hole throughout the night.
hints: It wraps in maguey pencas that transfer its smoky flavor
Cooks buried for 8 to 12 hours in the morning
The state of Hidalgo and the area of the Mosque Valley are its cradle
Served on Sundays in tacos with drunk sauce and consommé apart
The consommé of the cooking is the most tasty broth in the Mexican world

regular:188.name: Menudo Rojo
regular:188.desc: Panty broth and leg of beef with chili guajillo, hominy and oregano, the remedy of hangovers.
hints: The hominy — cacahuazintle corn — is the ingredient next to the belly
The guajillo chili and the width give it red color and deep flavor
It is said to cure hangovers better than any pharmaceutical medicine
Sundays are served very early in the markets and fondas of the country
Garnished with onion, oregano, tree chili and lemon when served

regular:189.name: Esquites
regular:189.desc: Grenade corn cooked in epazote broth with mayonnaise, chili, lemon and cotija cheese.
hints: The epazote aromatic is cooked with corn to give it the base flavor
Served in a cup with spoon and eaten hot or cold
It is the cup version of the corn in cob with the same ingredients
The night stalls in Mexico City sell them all the time
Mayonnaise, piquín pepper and lemon are the classic dressing

regular:190.name: Coctel de Ostión
regular:190.desc: Fresh oysters in your shell with lemon, valentine sauce, chili and onion in your juice.
hints: The oysters are served in their own shell with all their juices
Valentina or Huichol sauce is the classic spicy seasoning
Veracruz and the Pacific coast have the best oysters in the country
They open at the moment and are served completely raw with lemon
It is the most popular seafood aperitif of Mexican coastal bars

regular:191.name: Atole Blanco
regular:191.desc: Warm and thick corn drink massed with milk, cinnamon, vanilla and sugar.
hints: The mass of maize dissolved in water and milk is the basis of the white atole
Cinnamon sliced and vanilla give you the most characteristic aromas
It is drunk in clay jars in the markets from very early
It is the classic accompaniment drink of the tamales all over the country
Day of the Dead and Christmas Inns are your most consumed moments

regular:192.name: Costillas en Salsa
regular:192.desc: Pork ribs stewed in tomato sauce, chipotle, garlic and spices over low heat.
hints: The ribs are browned first before stewing in the sauce
The chipotle smoked gives depth and itching to the tomato broth
It is one of the most common stews in homes in the center of the country
Served with red rice, beans and hot corn tortillas
The recipe varies by region but chipotle is always present

regular:193.name: Leche Frita
regular:193.desc: Milk pastry cream, maizena and lemon fried in oil with sugar and cinnamon above.
hints: The pastry cream is solidified in a refrigerator before cutting and frying
The exterior is crispy and the interior creamy and soft at the same time
Galicia and Northern Spain have the oldest documented versions
Sprinkle in flour and egg before frying in hot oil
It is the best-selling dessert at popular fairs and vervains in the north

regular:194.name: Espinacas con Garbanzos
regular:194.desc: Chickpeas cooked with fresh spinach, garlic, cumin, paprika and fried bread in olive oil.
hints: It is the typical dish of Sevillian Holy Week par excellence
Fried bread crushed in thick mortar sauce naturally
Seville claims it as its most emblematic Lent dish
The cumin and the smoked paprika give it the characteristic Moorish flavor
It is eaten as a vegetarian main dish with village bread to wet

regular:195.name: Berberechos al Vapor
regular:195.desc: Roasted Galician beans cooked with white wine, garlic and parsley, served in their juice.
hints: The cockles of Galician rivers are the most appreciated in the world
They open only with the steam of white wine without water
The broth they release when opened is the most marine flavor imaginable
Galicia exports them in canned to all the world for decades
They eat with toothpick and dip bread in the bottom broth

regular:196.name: Pimientos de Padrón
regular:196.desc: Small green peppers fried in olive oil and sprinkled with sea salt.
hints: The village of Padrón, in Galicia, gives name to this small pepper
Some people bite and some don't—you never know which one will touch you until you bite it
Fry whole in very hot olive oil until crushed
Sea salt is the only necessary seasoning in the recipe
They are the most popular tapas in summer bars throughout Spain

regular:197.name: Caldo Verde
regular:197.desc: Galician cabbage green soup with potato and chorizo, the Spanish version of Portuguese green broth.
hints: Shear — Galician cabbage — cut into very fine julian for soup
Galicia prepares it with the local cabbage different from the Portuguese version
The Galician smoked chorizo gives the flavor and color to the broth
It is eaten in the cold months as a comforting spoon dish
The Portuguese version is couve-galega and is practically the same

regular:198.name: Mantecados
regular:198.desc: Demenuzable cookie of lard, flour, sugar and cinnamon, the Christmas candy.
hints: Pork butter — not butter — is the essential fatty ingredient
They crumble when they eat leaving an inevitable trail of crumbs
Stepa, in Seville, produces 80% of the butters from Spain
Sold wrapped in individual silk paper in Christmas lots
Cinnamon is the aroma that most characterizes them next to butter

regular:199.name: Roscos de Vino
regular:199.desc: Rings of fried dough with sweet wine, olive oil and sesame, sprinkled with sugar.
hints: Sweet wine — Moscatel or Pedro Ximénez — gives it the special flavor
They are fried in olive oil and sprinkled with sugar on their way out
Andalusia and Extremadura have the oldest and most famous versions
They are the sweet typical of Easter next to the torrijas and pestiños
The sesame sesame is mixed in the dough before frying

regular:200.name: Pestiños
regular:200.desc: Fry flour dough with wine, anise and orange zest, bathed in orange blossom honey.
hints: Anise and orange give you the medieval Arab aroma that defines them
They fry in olive oil and bathe in hot honey when taken out
They are the most popular Easter sweet in all of Andalusia
Its Andalusian Arab origin is evident in aromas and technique
Seville and Cadiz have the oldest and most appreciated recipes

regular:201.name: Bienmesabe Andaluz
regular:201.desc: Almond cream ground with sugar, egg, cinnamon and lemon zest of the Axarquia.
hints: It's different from the Venezuelan bienmesabe that is coconut
The toasted ground almond is the basis of this sweet cream
The Malaga Axarquía is the region where this cream originated
It is used as a filling of cakes, cakes and bread spreads
The name literally means that it tastes very good to the palate

regular:202.name: Olla Podrida
regular:202.desc: Medieval stew of beans, sausage, chorizo, bacon, hen and morcillo de Burgos.
hints: It is one of the oldest dishes in Spanish cuisine documented
The name doesn't mean it's bad but it's a powerful stew
Burgos and Castilla la Vieja are its region of medieval historical origin
Served in two turns like the cooked Madrid but more forceful
It appears mentioned in the Quijote as a dish of stately celebration

regular:203.name: Paella de Mariscos
regular:203.desc: Rice with saffron, prawns, clams, mussels and squid without meat or chicken.
hints: It's the marine version of paella, no meat of any kind
Fumet —fish broth — replaces meat broth in cooking
The Mediterranean coast area adopted it as its star version
The crispy socarrat of the background is as appreciated as in Valencian
Garnished with whole prawns and lemon before serving on the table

regular:204.name: Arroz a Banda
regular:204.desc: Rice cooked in fish fumet and saffron, served with alioli, Alicante sailor dish.
hints: A band means separate — rice and fish are served separately —
Fish and seafood fumet is the key to intense marine flavor
Alicante and the Valencian Costa Blanca are its place of historical origin
Alioli — garlic with oil — is the indispensable accompaniment on the table
It is made with the leftover broth to cook the fish that is served separately

regular:205.name: Carne con Papas Cubana
regular:205.desc: Beef in tomato creole sauce with potatoes and peppers, slowly stewed.
hints: It is the most daily meat stew consumed in Cuban households
Creole sauce carries tomato, pepper, onion, garlic and cumin
Potatoes are added in the middle of cooking so they don't melt
Served on white rice with black beans always next door
It is the dish that Cubans remember most of their mothers' cooking

regular:206.name: Fricase de Pollo Cubano
regular:206.desc: Chicken in dried wine sauce, olives, capers and potatoes, stewed over low heat.
hints: Cuban dry wine gives acidity and the body that distinguishes it
Olives and capers give it the salty and Mediterranean flavor
It's different from European African because it carries potatoes inside the stew
Served on major family days and gatherings
The recipe came with French and Spanish influence to the Cuban Caribbean

regular:207.name: Congris Oriental
regular:207.desc: Rice cooked with red beans, bacon, peppers and spices from the east of the island.
hints: Red beans differentiate it from Moors and Christians of black beans
It is the typical rice of the eastern region — Santiago, Holguin, Bayamo —
Smoked bacon gives the rice a deep fat flavor
It's called congrí all over the island but with red beans in the east
Bacon fat is used to fry sofrito before rice

regular:208.name: Picadillo a la Habanera
regular:208.desc: Ground beef with olives, capers, raisins and tomato creole sauce.
hints: Sweet raisins contrast with salty olives in a unique way
It is the filling of Cuban pastries and empanadas par excellence
Havana adopted it as a daily stew for family lunch
Served on white rice with fried ripe bananas next door
The Cuban picadillo is sweeter than those of other Caribbean countries

regular:209.name: Yuca con Mojo
regular:209.desc: Boiled cassava with garlic mojo, sour orange, onion and hot olive oil.
hints: The sour orange and garlic creole mojo is the soul of the dish
Cuban sour orange is more acidic than common sweet orange
The cassava must be well cooked but not undone by dressing it
It is the most popular Cuban food garrison on the whole island
It can be made with fried cassava also for a crisper version

regular:210.name: Buñuelos Cubanos
regular:210.desc: Eight-shaped cassava and malanga fritters, fried and bathed in cane honey.
hints: Mature cassava and malanga form the mass of these special fritters
They are formed in figure of eight which is their most visual characteristic
Cane honey — mellao — bathes them generously as they come out of the oil
They are the most traditional Christmas dessert on the island of Cuba
They are served hot and honey penetrates into the holes of eight

regular:211.name: Tamal en Cazuela
regular:211.desc: Mass of tender corn with pork, sofrito creole and spices, cooked in leafless pot.
hints: It's the tamal unwrapped — that's why in casserole— easier to make
The tender corn dough is cooked directly in the sofrito Creole
The pork in small pieces is mixed into the dough when cooking
It is the Cuban Creole version of tamal Central American and Mexican
Served with a large spoon directly from the saucepan to the dishes

regular:212.name: Churrasco Brasileño
regular:212.desc: Roasted meats in rotating spets served in the Rodízio system of meats without stopping.
hints: The Rodízio is the system where waiters take the spetons to the table
The picanha is the most appreciated and requested cut of the Rodízio
The green tablet turns—it continues to serve—or red—no longer—
São Paulo and Porto Alegre are the capitals of churrasco in the country
The rotating sprocket is the most characteristic tool of this method

regular:213.name: Moqueca Capixaba
regular:213.desc: Fish stew in tomato sauce, onion and urucum without coconut milk or dendê.
hints: Uricum — achiote — replaces palm oil in this version
It does not carry coconut milk or dendê, which makes it lighter
Holy Spirit is the state that created this version different from the Baian
It is cooked in a special clay pan called panelinha
The dispute between capixaba and baiana is one of the most famous in the country

regular:214.name: Baião de Dois
regular:214.desc: Rice and string beans cooked together with queijo coalho, dried meat and butter.
hints: Rope beans — feijão-de-corda — are the legume of the northeast
Grilled queijo gives it the characteristic milky and salty flavor
Smoky dried meat provides protein and smoky flavor
Ceará and the Brazilian Northeast are its region of historical origin
The name baião comes from a North American musical rhythm of the 19th century

regular:215.name: Pamonha
regular:215.desc: Sweet corn paste with coconut milk or cheese, cooked inside the corn leaf.
hints: The tender corn is grated raw and mixed with coconut milk or cheese
Wrapped in the leaf of the corn cob itself to cook
The sweet version carries coconut and the salty version carries coalho queijo
Goiás and the Centre-West are the regions where the most is consumed
It is sold at road stalls especially during the time of June

regular:216.name: Canjica
regular:216.desc: Dessert of white corn grains cooked in milk with grated coconut, cinnamon and sugar.
hints: White corn—canjica—is different from ordinary yellow maize
It is cooked in milk until the grains are very soft and creamy
The grated coconut and cinnamon are the aromas that identify it
It's the star dessert of June Junina Festas all over the country
Served hot on the cool nights of the São João holidays

regular:217.name: Picanha Grelhada
regular:217.desc: Cut of rump with fat covered in salt grossa, roasted whole and cut on the table.
hints: The picanha is the cut between the loin and the fat-covered rump
Fat is not removed — it's the secret of intense roasting
Roast whole and cut into thick strips directly on the diner table
It is the most requested and appreciated cut in all the churrascos of the country
Thick salt is the only necessary seasoning in the recipe

regular:218.name: Caldinho de Feijão
regular:218.desc: Thick broth of blended black beans with bacon, sausage and spices, served in glass.
hints: The beans are completely blended to make the ultra creamy broth
It is served in small glass as an entrance or appetizer in the churrascos
Bacon and linguiça — sausage — give it the fatty and smoked flavor
São Paulo popularized it as a bottle snack — informal bar—
It is served very hot with croutons or crunchy towers on top

regular:219.name: Arroz Carreteiro
regular:219.desc: Rice with defied dried meat, onion and garlic, the South Gaucho dish.
hints: Dried meat — pond — is desalted and defiled before cooking
The name reel comes from the reels that cooked it en route
Rio Grande do Sul and the gaucho south are its territory of historical origin
It is the most elegant rice of southern cuisine
It cooks everything together in the same pot so that rice absorbs the flavor

regular:220.name: Suco de Açaí
regular:220.desc: Thick açaí amazonic pulp juice beaten with guarana and served in bowl or glass.
hints: Açaí is a fruit of an Amazonian palm with a very intense purple colour
In Belém del Pará it is taken with tapioca and fish at breakfast
In the south and southeast you eat sweet smoothie with granola and banana
The palmeira açaizeiro grows only in the dense Amazon rainforest
Its consumption spread to the entire world as superfood in the 2000s

regular:221.name: Empadão Brasileiro
regular:221.desc: Flour dough cake filled with chicken, palmito, corn and cream, very creamy.
hints: Palm-heart palm is the most Brazilian ingredient in filling
The dough carries egg yolk and is very short and demenuzable
It's different from Latin American pie for being a big baked cake
Eating at celebrations, birthdays and family reunions
São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul have the most elaborate versions of the country

regular:222.name: Arroz con Pollo Venezolano
regular:222.desc: Rice cooked with chicken, criollo dressing, olives, capers and Venezuelan saffron.
hints: The Venezuelan criollo dressing carries sweet pepper, onion, garlic and cilantro
The olives and capers give the Mediterranean salty touch
The yellow color comes from the onyte — achiote — or turmeric
It is the most cooked festive dish in Venezuelan homes in the country
It differs from Colombian by olives and capers inside

regular:223.name: Papas Rellenas Venezolanas
regular:223.desc: Potato puree molded in ball filled with ground meat with olives and egg, fried.
hints: The mashed potato flattens in the hand, fills and closes in ball
Straw in flour and fry until golden and crispy
The ground meat with olives and hard egg is the classic filling
They are the most popular quick dinner of Venezuelan homes in the country
They are served with cabbage salad or guacaca — Venezuelan guacamole—

regular:224.name: Mandoca Zuliana
regular:224.desc: Argolla corn dough with ripe banana and fried white cheese, breakfast of Zulia.
hints: The dough mixes precooked corn flour with well-mature banana puree
The white cheese is mixed into the dough before shaping it
They are molded in small slang and fried until golden
Maracaibo and the state Zulia are their only place of documented origin
They eat hot with more white cheese grated above always

regular:225.name: Hervido de Pollo
regular:225.desc: Chicken broth with cob, yucca, potato, green banana and Venezuelan criollo dressing.
hints: Creole dressing is the mixture of sweet pepper, onion, garlic and cilantro
It is the sancocho Venezuelan even if it is called boiled in local jargon
It is served very hot with arepita and avocado to the side always
It is the most prescribed remedy for flus and colds in the country
Each region has its version with different local tubers

regular:226.name: Pasticho
regular:226.desc: Venezuelan pasta lasagna with ground meat, bechamel, cheese and tomato sauce.
hints: Pasticho is the Venezuelan lasagna adopted from Italian cuisine
It differs by the name—never say lasagna in Venezuela—
The bechamel is more abundant and creamy than in the Italian version
It is the most popular party and birthday dish in homes
Caracas has bakeries that sell it for portions every day

regular:227.name: Asado Negro
regular:227.desc: Round beef caramelized on paper and cooked in dark sauce with spices.
hints: The caramelized paper gives the sauce the intense black color
The meat is completely browned on the paper before adding liquids
It is the star dish of Caraqueña Creole cuisine since the 19th century
Served in slices on white rice with black broth next to it
It is the Christmas dish and important celebrations of Venezuela

regular:228.name: Empanada de Cazón
regular:228.desc: Fry corn dough empanada stuffed with pot — young shark — stewed.
hints: The bowl is the young shark whose meat is white and soft when cooked
The dough is precooked corn, different from wheat flour
The saucepan is cooked with onion, sweet pepper, tomato and creole cilantro
The Venezuelan coast produces the best bowl in the country for this filling
It is the most typical empanada of coastal states like Sucre and Anzoátegui

regular:229.name: Huevos Pericos
regular:229.desc: Eggs scrambled with tomato, onion and cilantro, Colombia's most popular breakfast.
hints: Finely chopped tomato and onion are inseparable ingredients
The chopped fresh cilantro is added at the end as an aromatic touch
They are the most consumed scrambled eggs in Colombian households
Served with arepa, fruit juice and coffee with milk at breakfast
Each region calls them different but the basic recipe is the same

regular:230.name: Frijoles Charros
regular:230.desc: Pot beans with chorizo, bacon, jalapeno pepper, tomato and cilantro.
hints: The chorizo and the bacon give it the flavor smoked and fat so special
The beans are cooked whole in clay pot for several hours
The jalapeño in slices gives you the itch that distinguishes them from normal beans
They are the inseparable accompaniment of roast meat from northern Mexico
The fresh cilantro and tomato are added at the end without cooking more

regular:231.name: Tostadas de Frijoles
regular:231.desc: Crunchy corn toast spread with black beans, chirmol, dry cheese and cream.
hints: Chirmol is the roasted tomato sauce with onion and chili guajillo
The dry, hard and salty cheese grates generously above
Guatemalan toast is thicker than Mexican toast
It is the most popular snack on markets across the country
It is eaten at any time of the day as a cheap and tasty snack

regular:232.name: Rellenitos de Plátano
regular:232.desc: Mature banana pellets stuffed with sweet black beans and fried in oil.
hints: The ripe banana is crushed to make a moldable dough
Black beans are sweetened with sugar or piloncillo for filling
They form in oval and fry until completely browned on the outside
They are the best-selling street dessert in the country's markets
Sprinkle with sugar when coming out of the oil to finish sweetening

regular:233.name: Jojotos
regular:233.desc: Sweet corn cobs cooked in salted water, served with butter and white cheese.
hints: The jojoto is the Venezuelan name for the tender corn cob
Cook in salted water until the grains are completely tender
The butter melts on the hot cob before serving
The grated white cheese is generously sprinkled above
Sold in street carts all year round in the country

regular:234.name: Cachito de Jamón
regular:234.desc: Horn-shaped bread stuffed with smoked leg ham and dough of sweet bread.
hints: It's the best-selling bread in Venezuelan bakeries every morning
Smoked leg ham is the only filling of the original straw
The dough becomes slightly sweet which contrasts with the ham
You eat hot fresh out of the oven with black coffee or malt
Caracas has bakeries open since 5am that bake them fresh

regular:235.name: Sopa Teologa
regular:235.desc: Noodle soup with chicken, mint, potato and hard egg, the dish of convents.
hints: Born in the colonial convents of Arequipa as a fasting dish
Fresh mint is the scent that differentiates from other noodles
The hard egg split in half is placed inside when serving on the plate
Arequipa claims it as part of its historic conventual cuisine
The thick noodles absorb the broth and are very tasty

regular:236.name: Pepián de Tostadas
regular:236.desc: Toast corn with pumpkin seeds dense sauce, tomato and chili on chicken.
hints: The pumpkin seeds toasts form the base of the thick sauce
It's different from pot cucumber — served on crispy toast —
Antigua Guatemala and the capital are the cities where it is most prepared
The toast must be very crisp to hold the dense sauce
It is a pre-Columbian dish that has remained almost the same since Mayan times

regular:237.name: Cocido de Puchero
regular:237.desc: Chickpea stew with chorizo, sausage, rib, pumpkin and potatoes in abundant broth.
hints: It is the Argentinian adaptation of Spanish cooked with local ingredients
The zapallo — calabaza— gives the color and sweetness to the broth of the stew
The Argentinean red chorizo is smoked and very different from Spanish
It is served in two dishes: first broth and then meats and vegetables
The Pampean interior has the most traditional documented versions

regular:238.name: Reviro Paraguayo
regular:238.desc: Mass of wheat flour with water and salt fried in pieces, the peasant breakfast.
hints: The dough is fried into irregular pieces in hot pork oil or fat
It is the most rustic and humble breakfast of Paraguayan peasants
It is eaten with cooked mate or hot milk in cold mornings
It doesn't carry yeast or sugar — it's just flour, water and salt —
The rural interior of Paraguay consumes it daily as breakfast

regular:239.name: Sopa de Albóndigas
regular:239.desc: Tomato broth with meatballs of beef and rice, mint and vegetables.
hints: The minced herb inside the meat is the most aromatic touch
Raw rice is mixed into meat before forming balls
Meatballs are added raw directly to the boiling broth
It's the most beloved granny dish in every home downtown
The roasted tomato gives depth to the broth different from raw tomatoes

regular:240.name: Caldo de Res Mexicano
regular:240.desc: Rib broth with ejotes, chayote, carrot, corn, potato and fresh coriander.
hints: The rib of beef with bone gives the most gelatinous and tasty broth
The chayote — guaisquil— gives it a soft texture and a special neutral flavor
The fresh cilantro is added only when serving to avoid cooking in the broth
It is the most comforting broth of Mexican family Sundays
Served with lemon and chopped serrano pepper separately for everyone

regular:241.name: Sopas de Lima
regular:241.desc: Sour lime broth with tortilla, shredded chicken and Yucatan habanero pepper.
hints: Yucatecan sour lime gives you completely unique citric acidity
The habanero pepper gives the intense and fruity itching that differentiates
The tortillas are fried separately and put on the time to serve
It's different from the basic lime soup by the habanero and chicken
Merida and the entire Yucatan Peninsula consider it their emblem soup

regular:242.name: Nieve de Limón
regular:242.desc: Natural lemon sorbet with water, sugar and salt, made in metal cylinder with ice.
hints: It is made of metal cylinders rotated in ice and salt to freeze
The only ingredient that gives it the flavor is freshly squeezed lemon
Snowfalls in Mexican parks sell them in cones or spoons
Oaxaca and Michoacán have the most famous and ancient snowfalls in the country
The red tuna and tamarind versions are the most popular of summer

regular:243.name: Arroz con Leche Venezolano
regular:243.desc: Rice cooked in milk with cinnamon, lemon peel and paper instead of white sugar.
hints: The paper—panel—gives a different smoky and dark taste to sugar
The lemon peel is cooked with rice to give citrus aroma
Cold served with powdered cinnamon generously sprinkled on top
It is the most cooked dessert in Venezuelan homes after hallaca
Venezuelan consistency is thicker and creamier than Spanish

regular:244.name: Papas Chorreadas
regular:244.desc: Criollas potatoes cooked with creamy tomato hogao, onion and melted peasant cheese.
