hints: The small and yellow creole potatoes are the irreplaceable ones of the dish
Hogao is prepared with slowly cooked tomato and long onion
The peasant cheese melts on the hot hogao for more creaminess
It is the most demanded garrison in the restaurants of the Andean highlands
Bogotá and the Cundiboyacense region eat them with all kinds of dishes

regular:245.name: Sudado de Pescado
regular:245.desc: Fish stewed in tomato sauce, aji, onion and cilantro in their own steam.
hints: The sweaty name comes from the fish cooking in its own steam
Red snapper and catfish are the most commonly used fish in the recipe
The sauce is made with tomato, onion, chili and lots of fresh cilantro
The Pacific and Caribbean coast have the most tasty versions of the country
Served with rice with coconut or white rice and patacones next to it

regular:246.name: Envueltos de Mazorca
regular:246.desc: Sweet corn dough with sugar and cheese wrapped in cob leaf and steamed.
hints: The tender corn grates raw to make the sweet dough of the wrapper
The cob leaf serves as a natural wrap and gives flavor
The peasant cheese in the center contrasts with the sweetness of the dough
They're different than tamales because the dough is sweet and meatless
The Valle del Cauca and the Cafetero Axis are its regions of origin

regular:247.name: Frijoles Colombianos
regular:247.desc: Red beans or cargomanto cooked with hogao, ribs, chorizo and green banana.
hints: Cargomanto beans are the largest and creamiest in Colombia
Tomato and onion hogao is the aromatic basis of the recipe
The rib and chorizo give the meaty flavor to the thick broth
The green banana in pieces is cooked with beans to give them body
Antioquia and the Cafetero Axis have the most famous and appreciated version

regular:248.name: Torta de Plátano
regular:248.desc: Mature banana moist cake with panela, cheese and tropical spices.
hints: Mature crushed banana substitutes for some flour in the dough
The panela —cane sugar— gives you the dark, smoked sweetness
The salty peasant cheese inside contrasts with the sweetness of the banana
Every Colombian home has its own secret recipe for this cake
Served as dessert or snack with coffee or hot chocolate

regular:249.name: Mondongo Venezolano
regular:249.desc: Soup of corned beef with chickpeas, potato, yucca, sweet pepper and criollo dressing.
hints: The calluses are cooked for hours until completely tender
The chickpeas and cassava give it the thick consistency that characterizes it
The Venezuelan criollo dressing gives the taste different from that of other countries
It is the dish of weekends and Sunday hangovers
Caracas and Valencia have the most famous and frequented mondongos

regular:250.name: Cocoa Venezolana
regular:250.desc: Heavy hot chocolate pure Venezuelan cocoa with milk, sugar and cinnamon.
hints: Venezuela produces the best aroma-fine cocoa in the world
Venezuelan Criollo cocoa is the most aromatic and globally appreciated
The cocoa is ground with sugar and diluted in hot, thick milk
It is the most refined breakfast drink in Venezuelan homes
Chuao and Ocumare are the Venezuelan valleys with the most famous cocoa

regular:251.name: Salchipapas
regular:251.desc: Fried potatoes with sliced sausages, mustard, ketchup and ají amarillo cream.
hints: It is the most popular and cheap street food in Lima par excellence
Sausages are fried in slices next to potatoes cut into strips
The ají amarillo in cream is the Peruvian touch that makes a difference
They are sold in kiosks and stalls all over Lima at any time of the day
Colombia and other countries adopted it but the original Peruvian is the father

regular:252.name: Caldo de Mote
regular:252.desc: Pork broth with cooked white mote, cilantro, onion and Andean spices.
hints: The mote is the peeled and cooked Andean corn that is very soft
The leg and pork rib give the most gelatinous and rich broth
Fresh cilantro and aji tree are added when serving on the table
It is the most popular breakfast of the Ecuadorian Sierra markets
It is especially eaten on weekends as a recovery dish

regular:253.name: Hayaca de Pollo
regular:253.desc: Maize with chicken stew, olives and capers wrapped in banana leaf.
hints: It's the hallaca version of chicken instead of meat mix
It is prepared as an alternative for those who do not eat beef
The stew carries the same olives and capers as the original hallaca
It is the most cooked variant by families with dietary preferences
Each family calls it hallaca chicken but the recipe varies by home

regular:254.name: Mazorca Asada
regular:254.desc: Roast corn cob with butter, salt and grated coastal cheese.
hints: The cob roasts directly on the embers and turns it constantly
Melted butter and coarse salt are the base of the dressing
Grilled and dry coastal cheese is sprinkled at the hot end
Sold in street stalls of Colombian cities at sunset
The version with hogao and peasant cheese is the most typical of the interior

regular:255.name: Chicha de Maíz
regular:255.desc: Fermented drink of purple corn with panela and Andean spices, slightly alcoholic.
hints: Maize chews and spits to start ancestral fermentation
Natural fermentation with saliva yeast is the original technique
It is the oldest sacred drink of the Andean cultures of the continent
Indigenous communities continue to prepare it by hand
Inti Raymi feasts are consumed in large ceremonial quantities

regular:256.name: Tamale de Rajas
regular:256.desc: Tamales corn dough stuffed with rajas of poblano pepper with cheese and cream.
hints: Rajas are strips of roasted and peeled poblano pepper
The melted Oaxaca cheese is mixed with rajas for filling
It is the most popular vegetarian version of the tamales Mexicans
Wrapped in corn leaf and steamed for one hour
Mexico City sells them in tamale shops early on

regular:257.name: Arroz Aguado
regular:257.desc: Rice cooked in abundant chicken broth until creamy as Ecuadorian risotto.
hints: The rice is cooked with more water than usual until it is almost undone
The shredded chicken is mixed into the rice at the end of cooking
The cilantro —ancholine— gives it the special Ecuadorian aroma
It is the most prescribed convalescence and healing food in homes
It is served with lemon and table aji so that everyone condiments

regular:258.name: Pastel de Yuca
regular:258.desc: Mass of yucca cooked with butter stuffed with chicken or meat, baked until browned.
hints: The cassava is cooked and made puree with butter before molding
The filling can be chicken stewed with vegetables or ground meat
Bake in rectangular mold until the cassava on top
It's different from the cause because it uses yucca instead of yellow potato
Lima serves it in Creole restaurants as entrance or main course

regular:259.name: Humitas de Sal
regular:259.desc: Mass of choclo grated with cheese, basil and onion wrapped in steamed choclo leaf.
hints: The choclo tender is grated raw and mixed with cheese and basil
Argentina’s salty version carries cheese and onion — not sugar —
They tie themselves with strips of the own choclo leaf before cooking
The Andean Northwest — Salta, Jujuy, Tucumán — is its original area of origin
They are similar to humitas Chileans but with more cheese and no sweet

regular:260.name: Tarta de Ricota
regular:260.desc: Broken dough cake stuffed with ricotta, sugar, lemon and orange zest.
hints: The ricotta — fresh Italian cheese — came with the Italian immigrants
The lemon and orange zest give the citrus freshness to the filling
Buenos Aires has italo-argentina pastry shops in every historic neighborhood
It differs from American cheesecake by ricotta instead of cream
It is the dessert of tea time in Buenos Aires' Buenos Aires homes

regular:261.name: Pascualina
regular:261.desc: Pastry cake stuffed with spinach, ricotta, whole egg and parmesan cheese.
hints: The whole egg hidden inside is the surprise when cutting the cake
Spinach sauté and drain well before mixing with ricotta
The crispy pastry dough contrasts with the creamy and soft filling
Uruguay adopted it from 19th century Genoese Italian cuisine
It's the most traditional Easter and party cake in homes

regular:262.name: Canja de Galinha
regular:262.desc: Field chicken broth with rice, onion, herbs and lemon, the Brazilian reconstituted.
hints: The field hen gives a broth much richer than the farm chicken
The rice is cooked directly in the broth to absorb the flavor
The squeezed lemon at the end gives it the acidity that refreshes it
It is the most universal remedy for any disease in Brazil
Brazilian grandmothers prepare it since the family member gets sick

regular:263.name: Vatapá de Camarão
regular:263.desc: Dense pasta of fresh shrimps with bread, peanuts, coconut milk and dendê.
hints: Fresh shrimps are added in addition to dried shrimps for more flavor
Mold bread without thick bark pasta next to ground peanut
Dendê oil gives you the orange color and special African aroma
It is served with white rice or inside the plier as main filling
Salvador de Bahia is the city where this recipe is best prepared

regular:264.name: Xinxim de Galinha
regular:264.desc: Chicken in dried shrimp sauce, peanuts, coconut milk and Bahia palm oil.
hints: The dried shrimp ground is the most characteristic ingredient of the salsa
The dendê — palm oil— gives it the orange color and African flavor
It is the most representative dish of Afro-Babyan cuisine in the northeast
Served on white rice or with farofa manioc next to it
The name comes from the African Yoruba dialect brought by slaves

regular:265.name: Quibebe
regular:265.desc: Rustic pumpkin puree — abobora — with coconut milk, sugar and cinnamon from the northeast.
hints: The pumpkin — abobora — is cooked to the ground in puree
Coconut milk gives you the tropical creaminess that makes it different
It is the classic accompaniment of dried meat and Northeastern churrasco
Pernambuco and Bahia are the states where it is consumed the most daily
It can be eaten only as dessert or as a side dish of roasted meat

regular:266.name: Pão de Mel
regular:266.desc: Soft honey biscuit and spices covered in black chocolate, the Brazilian lebkuchen.
hints: Spices include cinnamon, ginger, clove and nutmeg
Honey gives you moisture and sweetness that keeps you soft for days
It is completely covered in black chocolate or milk at the end
He arrived with German immigrants south of Brazil in the 19th century
São Paulo popularized it as a gift and souvenir of pastry shops

regular:267.name: Pamonha de Milho Verde
regular:267.desc: Sweet corn paste with milk and salt wrapped in corn leaf, salty version.
hints: The tender corn grinds completely until a liquid paste is made
The salty version carries only salt and milk without any added sweets
Maize leaf is used as a natural wrapper in all cases
Goiás and Minas Gerais have the most famous pamonherias in the country
Purchased at roadside stalls all year round indoors

regular:268.name: Arroz de Cuxá
regular:268.desc: Rice with vinegar —acid plant — dried shrimp and peanut toasted, from Maranhão.
hints: Vinaigreira is an acidic plant that gives the taste completely unique
Maranhão is the most gastronomically unknown state of the country
Dried ground shrimps give the sea flavor to red rice
It is one of the most authentic and inimitable dishes of Brazilian cuisine
São Luís, capital of Marbella, is where this recipe is best prepared

regular:269.name: Caruru
regular:269.desc: Okra —quiabo — stewed with dried shrimp, dendê and peanuts, Afro-Baaian ritual dish.
hints: The chiabo (okra) is the main vegetable that gives it the viscous texture
It is a ritual dish of the Candomblé religion dedicated to orixas
It is prepared at the Cosme e Damião holidays in September
Salvador de Bahia consumes it in both religious and lay contexts
The viscosity of the chiabo is the texture that makes it unique and inimitable

regular:270.name: Mee Goreng Latinoamericano
regular:270.desc: Chifa-style noodles with soy, vegetables, scrambled meat and egg.
hints: Chifa is the fusion of Chinese Cantonese cuisine with Peruvian cuisine
Noodles are skipped in wok with very high fire Asian style
Soybean—sillao—and kion — ginger—are the basic condiments
Lima has more chifa restaurants than any other Latin American country
It is the clearest proof of Chinese influence in Peruvian cuisine

regular:271.name: Mondongo Boliviano
regular:271.desc: Soup of beef corns with mote corn, potato, chuño and hot locote lajua.
hints: The chuño – dehydrated andine papa – is the most Andean ingredient of the dish
The white corn mote is added next to the potato and chuño
Spicy locote lajua is served separately for everyone to regulate
Cochabamba and Sucre have the most famous mondongo soups in the country
Specially eaten on weekends as a dining dish

regular:272.name: Leche Asada
regular:272.desc: Flan of whole milk, eggs and sugar baked in oven to the Maria bath, Chilean dessert.
hints: Bake in bath pot so that the cream is not cut during cooking
He doesn't have candy on the bottom—he differs from the flan for this—
The texture is firmer than the French flan by egg ratio
It is the most cooked Sunday dessert in Chilean homes in the country
It is served cold directly from the mold or deflated in a fountain

regular:273.name: Mote Pillo
regular:273.desc: White mote sautéed with scrambled egg, onion, garlic and milk, Cuenca breakfast.
hints: The mote is the peeled and cooked Andean corn that is very soft
Sauté with onion and garlic before adding the beaten egg
The milk is added at the end to give creaminess to the whole
Cuenca, the colonial city of the south, claims it as its emblem breakfast
It's different from broth — it eats dry and sautéed —

regular:274.name: Tacacho con Cecina
regular:274.desc: Green banana roasted and crushed with butter, served with cecina — smoked meat — Amazonian.
hints: The tacacho is the Amazon version of the mofongo Caribbean
The green banana is roasted in the embers before being crushed with butter
Cecina is pork or smoked beef and grilled salt
Iquitos and the entire Peruvian Amazon consume it as a main dish
It is the most representative dish of Peruvian Amazonian cuisine in the country

regular:275.name: Juane de Arroz
regular:275.desc: Rice ball cooked with chicken, olives and egg wrapped in steamed bijao leaf.
hints: The Amazonian bijao leaf transfers its green aroma during cooking
It is especially celebrated at the feast of San Juan on June 24
Rice cooked with turmeric gives it the characteristic intense yellow color
Iquitos, Tarapoto and the whole Amazon consume it at the feast of San Juan
The name comes from John, John, which is celebrated in June

regular:276.name: Inchicapi
regular:276.desc: Amazonic chicken broth with corn, ground peanuts and cilantro, thick and aromatic.
hints: The ground corn and the ground peanut thickens the broth naturally
It is the most representative dish of Peruvian Amazonian cuisine in the jungle
The broad-leaf cilantro gives you the special green scent
Loreto and the entire Amazonian department consume it daily
Served with cooked cassava and ají charapita — small and very spicy —

regular:277.name: Causa de Cangrejo
regular:277.desc: Causa limeña filled with river crab with mayonnaise, palm and ají amarillo.
hints: The shredded river crab replaces the tuna or chicken in this version
The base cause of yellow potato with lemon and chili pepper is the same as always
It is presented in the shape of a tower molded on the plate for more elegance
Novoandina cuisine restaurants serve as a luxury entrance
The crab version is the most appreciated at special events

regular:278.name: Adobo Arequipeño
regular:278.desc: Pork rib macerated in chicha jora, ají panca and spices, cooked the next day.
hints: It macerates all night before cooking the next day
chicha jora — fermented corn — is the most special ingredient
The ají panca gives it the dark red color and characteristic taste
Arequipa eats it especially on Sunday after Saturday night
The Arequipa peppers open only for Sunday lunch

regular:279.name: Sopa de Quinua
regular:279.desc: Chicken broth with white quinoa, potato, chuño and puna Andean vegetables.
hints: Quinoa is the Andean superfood grown since Inca times
The chuño — dehydrated dad — gives the earthy taste so Andean
The puna—altiplano over 3800 meters—is where quinoa is grown
It is the most nutritious and energetic soup of the entire Bolivian Andean diet
Bolivia produces 40% of all quinoa consumed in the world

regular:280.name: Silpancho de Huevo
regular:280.desc: Base silpango with double fried egg on top and tomato and locoto creole salad.
hints: It is the strongest version of the silpancho with extra egg on top
Cochabamba is the most proud gastronomic city of this recipe
The madoto—andean pepper—in the salad gives him the special Andean itching
Served in huge dishes covering the entire restaurant table
Tourists are always surprised by the size of the dish

regular:281.name: Plato Paceño
regular:281.desc: Cooked potato, choclo beans and fresh cheese from La Paz, the simplest and most tasty dish.
hints: It is the simplest dish in Bolivian cuisine—only four ingredients—
The Pope imilla of the valleys is the most appreciated of the whole
Cooked green beans and choclo are served at natural temperature
La Paz's fresh cheese melts slightly over the ingredients
It is the dish that people eat on Sundays in local markets

regular:282.name: Arroz con Camarones
regular:282.desc: Creamy rice cooked with fresh shrimp, onion, pepper and coconut milk.
hints: Fresh shrimps on the Ecuadorian coast are the largest in the world
Coconut milk gives you the tropical creaminess that makes it special
Pepper and onion form the base refrito of the coastal recipe
Guayaquil and the entire peaceful coast are its area of historical origin
It is the most sought after dish in the marshes of Guayaquil

regular:283.name: Papas con Cuero
regular:283.desc: Potatoes cooked with pork leather in peanut sauce, onion and achiote Andean.
hints: Clean pork leather cooks until completely gelatinous
The ground roasted peanut sauce is the thick base that gives it body
The achiote — onoto— gives it the orange color characteristic of the salsa
The Ecuadorian Andean mountain range is where the most consumed and celebrated
Served with white rice and onion tanned and tomato next to it

regular:284.name: Sopa de Lentejas
regular:284.desc: Thick lentil cream with onion, garlic, cumin, cilantro and fried ripe banana.
hints: Lentils are cooked until completely disposed of in dense cream
The fried ripe banana next door is the most classic accompaniment
Cumin and coriander are the most characteristic aromas of the dish
It is the most cooked soup in Ecuadorian homes during the year
Served with white rice and sliced avocado next to the plate

regular:285.name: Ceviche de Pulpo
regular:285.desc: Cooked octopus marinated in lemon with ají limo, purple onion and fresh cilantro.
hints: The octopus is cooked before marinating, unlike the ceviche fish
The ají limo gives you the most intense and fruity itching of all the ajies
Garnished with canchita —roasted corn— and choclo Peruvian white
Lima Vieja and the districts of Callao are where best prepared
It is the ceviche premium that is requested in Lima luxury cevicherías

regular:286.name: Arroz con Leche Cubano
regular:286.desc: Rice cooked in milk with lemon peel, cinnamon and sugar, the most loved dessert.
hints: It differs from Spanish because it is more liquid and less compact
The cinnamon powder is generously sprinkled on top of serving
The lemon peel is cooked with rice and removed at the end
It is the most cooked dessert in all Cuban homes in the world
You eat cold or at room temperature never fresh out of the fire

regular:287.name: Sopa de Mondongo
regular:287.desc: Soup of corned beef with chickpeas, banana, yucca, potato and creole spices.
hints: The calluses are cleaned and cooked for hours until tender
The chickpeas and cassava give it the thick texture that characterizes it
It is the dish of Sundays and large family celebrations
Santiago and Santo Domingo have the most famous restaurants in the country
Served with banana toast or ripe avocado next door always

regular:288.name: Pollo Guisado Dominicano
regular:288.desc: Chicken in sofrito creole sauce, tomato, olives and seasoning, slowly stewed.
hints: The sofrito Dominicans bring chií cubanela, tomato, garlic, onion and cilantro
The olives stuffed with pepper give the special salty touch
The achiote seasoning gives you the golden color and Caribbean flavor
It is the most cooked lunch dish in Dominican homes
Served with white rice, beans and salad always

regular:289.name: Quipes
regular:289.desc: Croquettes of ground meat with bulgur wheat and mint, the island's Arab quibe.
hints: They came with 19th-century Lebanese and Syrian Arab immigration
Fine bulgur wheat is mixed with raw ground beef
The minty fresh chopped gives it the Arab aroma that differentiates them
They are the most popular fry in Dominican celebrations and festivals
They eat cold or hot with chili pepper sauce next door

regular:290.name: Habichuelas con Dulce
regular:290.desc: Sweet cream of red beans with coconut milk, raisins, cinnamon and sweet potatoes, Easter dessert.
hints: It is the only vegetable dessert in the world — beans are cooked sweets —
It is eaten exclusively during Holy Week by religious tradition
Sweet potatoes — sweet potatoes — give you the sweetness and soft texture at the end
Coconut milk makes the cream very aromatic and tropical to the palate
Dominicans share it with neighbors door to door on Easter

regular:291.name: Sopón de Pollo
regular:291.desc: Hard chicken soup with thick noodles, chickpeas, potato and sofrito boricua.
hints: The sofrito with careo and sweet chili gives the unmistakable boricua flavor
The chickpeas give you the protein and texture that make it very forceful
The thick noodles absorb the broth and are very tasty when eating
It is the soup of Sundays and rainy days throughout the island
Grandma is the most authorized person to prepare the best sopon

regular:292.name: Caldo Santo
regular:292.desc: Cod soup desalted with potato, green plantain and sofrito Easter Boricua.
hints: Prepared exclusively on Good Friday as a religious tradition
Cod desalted 48 hours earlier is the only valid fish
Green banana and potato give the body and consistency to broth
It is the dish most remembered by Puerto Ricans of their religious childhood
Every grandmother has her secret recipe that she doesn't share with anyone

regular:293.name: Pionono
regular:293.desc: Fried ripe banana roll stuffed with ground meat with sofrito, fried and baked.
hints: The ripe banana is flattened in strips before rolling with the filling
Ground meat with sofrito boricua is the most traditional filling
Fry first and then bake briefly to caramelize the banana
It is the most popular appetizer in Puerto Rican parties everywhere
It is always accompanied with ketchup — tomato sauce— in Puerto Rico

regular:294.name: Pernil de Puerco
regular:294.desc: Pernil pork marinated in Creole season, sour orange and garlic, roasted in oven.
hints: Sour orange gives you the acidity that penetrates the meat when marinating
Dominican Creole Season Is Different From Other Caribbean Countries
It marinates at least 24 hours before for the flavor to penetrate well
It is the most cooked Christmas Eve and New Year dish in the country
The crispy skin —curito— is the most contested part in serving

regular:295.name: Nacatamales Hondureños
regular:295.desc: Mass of corn with chicken, olives, rice and raisins wrapped in banana leaf, the tamal large.
hints: It is the tamal largest in all Central America — it can weigh a kilo—
It is wrapped in banana leaf that transfers its vegetable flavor
Olives, raisins and rice differentiate it from another tamales
Fridays are prepared for Saturday breakfast by tradition
Tegucigalpa has the most famous tamaleras in Honduras

regular:296.name: Catrachitas
regular:296.desc: Toast corn with refried beans, grated dry cheese and on top cabbage and cream.
hints: The cabbage in thin strips and the acidic cream are the classic toppings
The dried cheese hard and very salty is grated on top of the beans
Honduran toast is smaller and rounder than Mexican toast
They are the most popular snack in the markets and stadiums of the country
The name comes from a loving kindness for Hondurans

regular:297.name: Tajadas con Queso
regular:297.desc: Mature banana fried in long slices with melted white cheese and cabbage on top.
hints: Cuts are fried in hot oil until caramelized from the outside
The white cheese is put on the hot slices to melt
The cabbage in thin strips with lemon is put on top at the cool end
It is the most popular garrison of Honduran lunches in the country
It is accompanied with any kind of grilled meat or fried next to it

regular:298.name: Caldo de Res Guatemalteco
regular:298.desc: Broth of beef ribs with corn, güisquil, ejotes, potato and fresh mint.
hints: Güisquil — chayote — is the most Guatemalan vegetable in the stock
Fresh peppermint at the end is the scent that distinguishes it from others
The rib with bone gives the gelatinous base of the broth so special
It is the most traditional Sunday lunch of Guatemalan families
Served with freshly made corn tortillas in hot griddle

regular:299.name: Garnachas
regular:299.desc: Small corn tortillas with beef, pickled cabbage and tomato sauce.
hints: Grenaches are thick tortillas and small fried in butter
The shredded beef is put on the hot tortilla
The pickled cabbage in vinegar gives acidity and crunchy
They are the most popular street snack on Guatemalan markets
Huehuetenango and Quetzaltenango have the best in the West

regular:300.name: Jocón de Pollo
regular:300.desc: Chicken in intense green sauce of tomatillo, chili, coriander and pumpkin seeds.
hints: The green sauce comes from tomatillo — miltomate — and the dried chili
The pumpkin seeds toasts give the thickness and flavor to walnut
It is one of the eight national dishes recognized by the Guatemalan State
The indigenous West —Huehuetenango, San Marcos — has been cooking it for centuries
The name is Tzeltal and means green chicken in that Mayan language

regular:301.name: Sopa de Pan
regular:301.desc: Cobán holiday soup with French bread, chicken broth, vegetables, capers and raisins.
hints: Cobán, in the northern verapaces, is the only place where it is made
Prepares only for the All Saints celebrations in November
French bread soaked in chicken broth gives you the special texture
Capers and raisins give you the salty and sweet contrast together
It is one of the most unknown and unique dishes in all Guatemala

regular:302.name: Champurradas
regular:302.desc: Big and crunchy cookies of anise and sesame, the Guatemalan Christmas bread.
hints: Anise and sesame are the aromas that identify them
They're bigger than normal biscuits—the size of the hand—
Dried in black coffee or hot chocolate before eating them
They are typical Christmas bread and inns throughout Guatemala
Bakeries bake them especially in December and January

regular:303.name: Sopa de Frijoles
regular:303.desc: Thick cream of red beans with parrot, hard cheese grated and acidic cream.
hints: The parrot is a Salvadoran edible flower with a very special aroma
Salvadoran red bean blends to make the cream thick
The hard cheese grated and dried is generously sprinkled on top
It is the most daily and consumed soup in all Salvadoran homes
Served with freshly made corn tortillas to soak in the cream

regular:304.name: Yuca Frita con Chicharrón
regular:304.desc: Boiled casserole and then fried with crispy chicharrón and cabbage salad with lemon.
hints: The cassava is boiled first and then fried for the crispy exterior
The chicharrón Salvadoran pig skin is very crispy and dry
The cabbage salad with lemon and tomato balances the fat of the dish
It is the most popular street snack in El Salvador
Served with homemade tomato sauce or fermented cabbage tanned

regular:305.name: Riguas
regular:305.desc: Thick corn cakes roasted in griddle, accompanied by cream and cheese.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the dough without any flour
They are cooked directly in the griddle without oil until golden on the outside
Cream and hard cheese are the only classic accompaniments
They are the whim of season when the corn is at its tender point
Salvadoran markets sell them especially from July to September

regular:306.name: Güirilas
regular:306.desc: Thick and sweet corn tortillas cooked in comal, with cream and cheese.
hints: Sweet tender corn makes the tortilla taste natural
They are thicker and sweeter than Salvadoran or Guatemalan tortillas
Acid cream and grated dry cheese are your classic accompaniments
They are breakfast and seasonal snack when tender corn is available
Nicaragua sells them on the markets all year round

regular:307.name: Vigorón
regular:307.desc: Yucca cooked with crispy chicharrón and cabbage tanned served on banana leaf.
hints: Served on banana leaf instead of dish — the classic presentation—
Sour cabbage tanning contrasts with chicharrón fat
Granada, colonial city of the lake, is where the vigorón originated
Sold in street stalls and markets throughout Nicaragua
The name vigorón comes from the advertising of a 19th century medicine

regular:308.name: Indio Viejo
regular:308.desc: Thick stew of corn dough with shredded beef, tomato, achiote and mint.
hints: The corn dough dissolves in the broth and thickens the stew completely
The fresh mint inside is the scent that makes it completely unique
It is one of the oldest and most pre-Columbian dishes in Nicaragua
Served with white rice and corn tortillas as an accompaniment
Managua’s restaurants serve it as a typical dish of national cuisine

regular:309.name: Rondon de San Andrés
regular:309.desc: Soup of fish and seafood in coconut milk with yam, yucca and banana dough.
hints: San Andrés and Providencia are the Colombian Caribbean islands of origin
Coconut milk is the completely tropical liquid base of broth
Yams and yucca are the Caribbean tubers irreplaceable in soup
The Afro-Caribbean and English root influence is evident in the recipe
It is one of the most exotic and unknown dishes in Colombian cuisine

regular:310.name: Tamal de Pipián
regular:310.desc: Tamal dough of corn with pickle — turkey — wrapped in maxan leaf.
hints: The maxan leaf —heliconia— is the traditional Guatemalan wrapper
Choppy pepián is the turkey nuggets sauce that fills tamal
Prepares for weddings and the most important celebrations of the year
The indigenous regions of the country prepare it as a festive ceremonial dish
It's bigger and ceremonial than the country's daily tamales

regular:311.name: Seco de Carne
regular:311.desc: Steak stew in black beer sauce, tomato, onion, cumin and naranjilla.
hints: Black beer gives the bitter and caramelized flavor to the sauce
naranjilla — lulo — provides characteristic tropical citrus acidity
Served with white rice, beans and sliced avocado next door
It is the most requested dry in restaurants of the Ecuadorian mountains
It differs from seco de pollo by being darker and more res

regular:312.name: Encebollado
regular:312.desc: Albacore broth — tuna — with cassava, pickled onion in lemon and cilantro, the Costa Rican breakfast.
hints: Ezebollado is eaten as breakfast on the Ecuadorian coast
The albacore — shortfin tuna — is the only authentic fish on the plate
Onion pickled in lemon is the ingredient that gives it its name
It is eaten with banana chifles, canguil and yucca bread next to it
Guayaquil declares it gastronomic heritage of the coastal city

regular:313.name: Ayampaco
regular:313.desc: Palmito with tilapia meat or chicken wrapped in bijao leaf and grilled in embers.
hints: The bijao leaf wraps the filling and cooks directly in the embers
Palm-heart palm is the most valued Amazonian ingredient
It is the most representative dish of Ecuadorian Amazonian cuisine
Pastaza, Orellana and Sucumbíos are the Amazonian provinces of origin
Kichwas communities cook it as a festive ceremonial dish

regular:314.name: Sancocho de Gallina
regular:314.desc: Yucca chicken broth, banana, sweet chili, cilantro and spices.
hints: The patio hen — not the farm chicken — is the only one valid for broth
The cassava and the green banana are the food that makes it so strong
The sweet pepper — a bell pepper— gives the broth the sweetness
Specially eaten on weekends as a celebration dish
Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula have the most recognized versions of the country

regular:315.name: Tamales Costeños
regular:315.desc: Tamales rice with pork, olives and chiltoma from the Nicaraguan Caribbean.
hints: Nicaragua’s Caribbean Coast Uses Rice Instead of Maize
Chiltoma—sweet pepper—gives the tropical flavor different to the interior
Olives and pork are the most typical fillers of the coastal version
Totally different from nacatamal Pacific corn mass
Bluefields and the Caribbean Coast are cities of historical origin of the dish

regular:316.name: Arroz con Leche de Coco
regular:316.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with cinnamon, sugar and raisins, afroantillano dessert.
hints: Coconut milk completely replaces cow's milk in the recipe
Sweet raisins give you the fruity touch and different texture
The cinnamon powder is generously sprinkled on top when serving cold
Jamaican Afro-Antillean influence is evident in Panamanian recipe
Columbus and the Caribbean area are where this tropical dessert is consumed the most

regular:317.name: Tamales Oaxaqueños
regular:317.desc: Tamal wrapped in mole black and chicken banana leaf, typical of Oaxaca.
hints: It is wrapped in banana leaf, not corn, unlike another tamales in the country
The mole black Oaxacan is the filling that makes it unique
Oaxaca is the southern state where this variant originated
Steamed for more than an hour
Typical of Day of the Dead celebrations in the region

regular:318.name: Esquites con Chile Piquín
regular:318.desc: A variant of skis with extra ground chili pepper and powdered cotija cheese.
hints: It is a more spicy variant of the classic squite in glass
Pichin pepper is ground dry and sprinkled generously
The dry cotija cheese gives you the final salty touch
It is sold in the same street stalls as the corn
It is very popular in the north of the country for its intense itching

regular:319.name: Fabada Asturiana
regular:319.desc: White beans stew with chorizo, sausage and bacon, insignia dish of Asturias.
hints: Fabes — large white beans— are irreplaceable in this recipe
Asturias, in the green north of the country, is its region of origin
It carries compango: chorizo, sausage and smoked bacon
It is cooked over very slow heat for several hours
It is the most representative spoon dish in northern Spain

regular:320.name: Esgarraet
regular:320.desc: Valencian salad of roasted red pepper, demigrated cod, garlic and olive oil.
hints: The pepper is roasted whole until the skin can be removed easily
Cod demiga raw, already desaladado, without cooking more
Valencia is the Mediterranean region where this salad was born
Served cold as an entrance or tapas in the bars of Levante
The name literally means 'teared' in Valencian

regular:321.name: Provoleta
regular:321.desc: Grilled provolone cheese thick round with oregano and olive oil.
hints: The provolone cheese is roasted directly on the hot grill
Sprinkled dry oregano is the classic seasoning
Served as entrance before main roast
The golden and crispy bark contrasts with the melted interior
It is an infallible in any Argentine barbecue weekend

regular:322.name: Choripán
regular:322.desc: Grilled chorizo served on bread with chimichurri, the most popular street sandwich.
hints: The chorizo opens in the middle before roasting so that it cooks faster
Chimichurri is the salsa that never fails on top
Sold in football games and street grills
It is the fastest appetizer of any Argentine roast
The bread of crumbs or French bread are the most used

regular:323.name: Causa Limeña
regular:323.desc: Layers of yellow potato pressed with lemon and ají amarillo, stuffed with chicken or tuna.
hints: The yellow potato is seasoned with lemon and ají amarillo before pressing
Cast in layers like a cold cake, without the need for oven
The most classic filling is chicken or tuna with mayonnaise
It is a cold dish, perfect for the warmth of the coast
The ají amarillo gives it the golden color so characteristic

regular:324.name: Rocoto Relleno
regular:324.desc: Rocoto spicy stuffed with ground meat and cheese, baked and very spicy, from Arequipa.
hints: The rocoto is a very spicy and fleshy chili from the Peruvian Andes
Arequipa is the city where this traditional dish originated
It is emptied and boiled before filling to soften the itching
The filling of ground meat with cheese is baked gratina
It is one of the most spicy dishes in Peruvian gastronomy

regular:325.name: Patacones con Hogao
regular:325.desc: Green banana toast covered in tomato and onion hogao, typical garnish.
hints: The green banana is fried and crushed twice, just like the classic patacón
Tomato and onion hogao is slowly cooked apart
It is the most popular garrison on the Colombian Caribbean coast
Served hot, freshly fried, next to any main course
The creaking of the patacón contrasts with the softness of the hogao

regular:326.name: Changua
regular:326.desc: Milk soup with water, cilantro, poached onion and egg, typical Bogotan breakfast.
hints: Milk and water are boiled together as the basis of this soup
The egg is poached directly into the hot liquid
Bogotá and the cundiboyacense savanna consume it as cold breakfast
The chopped fresh cilantro is added just before serving
It is accompanied with bread or draught — soaked bread — to wet

regular:327.name: Pernil Venezolano
regular:327.desc: Pork leg marinated in creole spices and baked, Venezuelan Christmas dish.
hints: It marinates with garlic, cumin, oregano and sour orange for hours
It is the center dish of Christmas Eve dinner in the country
The skin is crispy after hours of slow oven
Served next to the hallaca and hambread in December
Each family has its own secret marinate recipe

regular:328.name: Pan de Jamón
regular:328.desc: Sweet bread rolled with ham, bacon and raisins, infallible at the Christmas table.
hints: It rolls like a gypsy arm stuffed with ham and bacon
The raisins and green olives are part of the classic filling
It is exclusive to the season decembrina all over the country
The dough is slightly sweet, similar to a brioche bread
Caracas has bakeries that bake it only in December

regular:329.name: Curanto
regular:329.desc: Cooking seafood, meat and potatoes underground with hot stones, typical of Chiloé.
hints: It is cooked in a hole in the ground with stones heated to bright red
Chiloé, the southern island of Chile, is its ancestral cradle
Bring seafood, pork, chicken, chapalles and milcaos all together
The nalca leaves cover the hole to retain steam
It is a cooking technique of Huilliche indigenous origin

regular:330.name: Sopaipillas Chilenas
regular:330.desc: Sausage fries with zapallo, served sweets with chancaca or salted with chili pepper.
hints: The zapallo — calabaza— is incorporated into the dough before frying
Rainy days are sold on the streets across the country
The sweet version is bathed in chancaca, hot cane honey
The salty version is accompanied by pebre or chili pepper
They are a very popular snack in the cold months of the year

regular:331.name: Tostones Cubanos
regular:331.desc: Green banana rolls fried and crushed, golden and crunchy, classic garnish.
hints: The green banana is fried, crushed and fryed again
They are the most popular garrison of all Cuban food
Served with garlic mojo to wet each piece
The crispy texture on the outside and soft inside is key
They accompany almost any dish of meat on the island

regular:332.name: Vaca Frita
regular:332.desc: Boiled beef, frayed and then fried with onion until crispy.
hints: The meat boils first until it becomes very tender to melt
Then fry in hot oil until browning the edges
The onion in juliana is fried separately and mixed at the end
The touch of sour lemon is added just before serving
It is a very popular dish in the Criollos restaurants of Miami and Cuba

regular:333.name: Tigrillo Ecuatoriano
regular:333.desc: Gentle green banana with scrambled egg and cheese, breakfast typical of the southern mountain range.
hints: The cooked green plantain is crushed until it becomes thick as puree
The scrambled egg is mixed directly with the hot banana
Loja and the southern mountain range of the country are its area of origin
Fresh grated cheese is added at the end of sautéing
Served with coffee or laundry as a hearty breakfast

regular:334.name: Morocho Ecuatoriano
regular:334.desc: Thick drink of broken corn cooked in milk with cinnamon, nail and panela.
hints: Morocho corn — split and white — is cooked to a great extent
Milk and panela give you creaminess and sweetness
Cinnamon in crack and clove of smell are its characteristic aromas
It sells hot in the cold mornings of the Ecuadorian mountains
It is similar to the dungeon but with white corn, not purple

regular:335.name: Pique Macho
regular:335.desc: Pieces of meat and sausage on fried potatoes with onion, tomato and spicy locoto.
hints: Served on a large tray to share among several people
Meat and sausage are sautéed with onion and tomato together
The spicy locoto is spread over the whole dish
Cochabamba is the Bolivian city where this dish originated
Fries make the basis for all the mixture on top

regular:336.name: Chairo Paceño
regular:336.desc: Lamb soup with chuño, potato, wheat and Andean vegetables, typical of La Paz.
hints: The chuño — dehydrated dada — is one of its most Andean ingredients
The peeled wheat gives you a very particular thick texture
La Paz, the highest city in the country, is its place of origin
It is slowly cooked with lamb or puddle of beef
It is a very strong soup, ideal for the cold of the highlands

regular:337.name: Mbeju Paraguayo
regular:337.desc: Crusher cake of cassava starch and cheese, cooked in unleavened skillet.
hints: Manioc starch is the base, without any wheat flour
It does not carry yeast, so it is fine and crispy
Paraguayan cheese is mixed directly into the dough
Cooked in skillet until golden on both sides
It is gluten-free naturally because of its ingredients

regular:338.name: Bori Bori
regular:338.desc: Chicken soup with corn balls and Paraguayan cheese, traditional homemade dish.
hints: Balls are made with mixed corn flour and Paraguayan cheese
Cook directly inside the hot chicken stock
It is one of the most homemade and beloved dishes in the country
The broth is enriched with vegetables and fresh herbs
Balls absorb the flavor of broth while cooking

regular:339.name: Torta Frita Uruguaya
regular:339.desc: Flat, crispy fried dough, typical of rainy days, served with sugar or sweet milk.
hints: Fry in hot oil until browned and very crispy
It's tradition to eat them just on rainy days in the country
He gets a cut in the center for a couple to cook
Sprinkled sugar or sweet milk are the companions
Montevideo smells like fried cakes every time it rains hard

regular:340.name: Pamonha Doce
regular:340.desc: Sweet corn paste tender with coconut and sugar, wrapped in steamed corn leaf.
hints: The tender corn grinds to form a creamy and sweet pasta
The grated coconut is mixed inside to give more tropical flavor
Wrapped in the corn leaf itself before steaming
It is very popular at June Juninas Festas throughout Brazil
Goiás and Minas Gerais have the most famous versions of the country

regular:341.name: Casabe Dominicano
regular:341.desc: Flat and crispy cake of grated yucca, unleavened, Tain indigenous heritage.
hints: The bravaded yucca grated and pressed is the only base of this cake
No yeast or egg, only cassava and a little salt
It is the direct inheritance of Taín peoples before colonization
It is cooked in a large budare until it becomes thin and crispy
You eat alone or with stews as if it were bread

regular:342.name: Locrio Dominicano
regular:342.desc: Rice cooked with chicken, longaniza or fish, sofrito and spices, Dominican holiday rice.
hints: It is Dominican rice cooked in a single pot with protein
May be chicken, longaniza, salami or fish depending on region
The sofrito tomato, garlic and onion gives the base flavor
It is the most prepared dish in family celebrations of the country
It differs from rice with chicken by sofrito and its own spices

regular:343.name: Asopao Boricua
regular:343.desc: Broth rice with chicken or seafood, sofrito and achiote, more liquid than normal rice.
hints: It's hotter than normal rice, almost like a thick soup
The sofrito boricua with recao is the aromatic base of the dish
It is served very hot, ideal for tropical rainy days
It can be chicken or seafood according to the family recipe
It is one of the most beloved spoon dishes on the island

regular:344.name: Yuca al Mojo Puertorriqueño
regular:344.desc: Boiled cassava bathed in garlic mojo and hot olive oil, classic garnish.
hints: The cassava is boiled until tender but not undone
Garlic mojo heats in oil before pouring it over
It is the most common garrison of piglets and roasted meats
The chopped garlic browns slightly to soften its strong flavor
It accompanies almost any festive food on the island

regular:345.name: Tamal Pisque
regular:345.desc: Tamal corn dough with ayote pepper, wrapped in maxan leaf or banana.
hints: Ayote Pepitoria are roasted and ground pumpkin seeds
It's a tamal single, meatless, heavily consumed weekdays
The eastern regions of the country frequently prepare it
Wrapped in maxan or banana leaf depending on the area
It has a softer flavor than other tamales holidays in the country

regular:346.name: Yuca con Chicharrón Hondureña
regular:346.desc: Fried Yuca with crispy chicharrón and cabbage tanned, popular street dish.
hints: The cassava is boiled and then fried until browned on the outside
The Honduran chicharrón is very crispy and served in pieces
Cabbage tanning with vinegar balances the fat on the plate
It's one of the best-selling street dishes on weekends
Tegucigalpa has stalls dedicated only to this dish

regular:347.name: Tamal Pisque Nicaragüense
regular:347.desc: Tamal corn dough with ground beans, wrapped in banana leaf, simple and homemade.
hints: The ground beans are mixed directly into the corn dough
It's a tamal simpler than the nacatamal, without so much filling
Wrapped in banana leaf and steamed
It is very common as daily food in Nicaraguan homes
Managua and the country’s Pacific often consume it

regular:348.name: Birria Tatemada
regular:348.desc: Variant of birria with chile betamodo direct to the comal, more smoked and dark.
hints: The chili is roasted directly in a dry griddle before being ground
Jalisco also claims this darker and smoked version
Serves just like the classic birria, with its separate consommé
Tatemado intensifies the smoky taste of stew
It is popular at night stalls in Guadalajara

regular:349.name: Sope Mexicano
regular:349.desc: Thick base of corn dough with edge, covered with beans, meat, lettuce and cheese.
hints: The dough is molded with a high edge to hold the filling
Fry lightly before filling with the ingredients
Refried beans are the first layer always
It's thicker than a toast or a tlayuda
It is sold in markets throughout the center of the country

regular:350.name: Conchas de Chocolate
regular:350.desc: Sweet bread with crispy chocolate cover in the shape of seashell.
hints: The cover is made separately and marked with shell type lines
The chocolate version is the favorite next to the vanilla version
Bake twice a day in the country’s bakeries
They are accompanied by hot chocolate or pot coffee
Mexico has more than two thousand varieties of sweet bread, this is one of the most sold

regular:351.name: Cocido Andaluz
regular:351.desc: Chickpea stew with vegetables and meat, Andalusian version of the Spanish cooked.
hints: Bring pumpkin and green beans, more vegetables than the cooked Madrid
Andalusia has its own lighter version of cooking
It is served equally in two turns: soup and then solids
The Andalusian paprika gives a different touch to the broth
It's a typical southern winter spoon dish

regular:352.name: Marmitako
regular:352.desc: Nice Basque stew with potato, pepper and onion, typical of fishermen.
hints: Born in the Basque fishing boats of the Cantabrian
The northern bonito is the main fish of the recipe
Potatoes are cracked, not cut, so they release starch
It is cooked in a single pot, easy to make on the high seas
The Basque Country considers it one of its most unique dishes

regular:353.name: Vacío a la Parrilla
regular:353.desc: Cut lean and tasty beef, roasted slowly over embers.
hints: It is one of the most juicy cuts for Argentine roasting
It is cooked with bone or without bone according to the butchery
Thick salt is the only seasoning you need
Livestock pampas produce the most appreciated meat from cutting
Served whole and cut on the table in front of the diner

regular:354.name: Torta Frita Argentina
regular:354.desc: Flat fried dough served with sugar, tradition of rainy days.
hints: A cut is made in the center for a couple to cook
It's customary to prepare them just when it rains
Sprinkled sugar is the most common accompaniment
Served hot fresh out of oil
Argentina’s countryside considers them an essential snack

regular:355.name: Papa a la Huancaína
regular:355.desc: Cooked potatoes bathed in creamy ají amarillo sauce, fresh cheese and cookie.
hints: The sauce is blended with ají amarillo, fresh cheese and soda cookie
Huancayo, in the central mountain range, gives this dish its name
Cold served on slices of cooked yellow potato
Brings black olive and hard egg as classic decoration
It is one of the most ordered tickets in Peruvian restaurants

regular:356.name: Arroz con Pato
regular:356.desc: Green rice cooked with duck, cilantro, black beer and ají amarillo, Northern dish.
hints: The blended cilantro gives the rice the intense green color
The north coast of the country is where this dish originated
Black beer softens duck meat when cooking
The ají amarillo is incorporated directly in the sofrito
Lambayeque is the most famous region for this recipe

regular:357.name: Empanadas de Pino
regular:357.desc: Chilean empanada filled with minced meat, onion, hard egg, olive and raisins.
hints: The pine is prepared well in advance so that the onion is well cooked
The raisins are optional but very traditional in the recipe
They bake to brown, never fry in the classic version
It is the most representative empanada in the whole country
Juicy filling is the sign of a good pine empanada

regular:358.name: Sancocho de Gallina Colombiano
regular:358.desc: Creole hen thick soup with yucca, banana and cob, festive version of sancocho.
hints: The Creole hen gives a broth more concentrated than the common chicken
It cooks for hours until the meat is undone alone
Yucca, plantain and cob are the unstoppable companions
It's a family Sunday dish in much of the country
The coriander and the yellow color of saffron decorate it when serving

regular:359.name: Buñuelos Colombianos
regular:359.desc: Fried peas made of coastal cheese and cassava starch, golden and fluffy inside.
hints: The coastal cheese is mixed directly into the dough before frying
They're unstoppable at Christmas dinner by the natilla
They fry until they're golden and inflated like a ball
Yucca starch gives you the elastic texture inside
December is the month in which most are consumed throughout the country

regular:360.name: Reina Pepiada
regular:360.desc: Filling of arepa with chicken scraped, avocado and mayonnaise, the most famous in the country.
hints: It bears the name of a Venezuelan beauty queen from the 1950s
Avocado and shredded chicken are mixed with mayonnaise
It's the most ordered arepa filling in any arepera
It can be eaten in arepa, on bread or as a salad alone
Caracas has arepers dedicated almost exclusively to this filling

regular:361.name: Dominó Venezolano
regular:361.desc: arepa filling with black caraotas and grated white cheese, simple and popular.
hints: The name comes from black and white colors, like domino tiles
Black caraotas are beans cooked with paper and onoto
It is one of the most economical and consumed arepa fillings
The grated white cheese is mixed with the hot caraotas
Served in any country arepera at any time

regular:362.name: Sopaipillas Pasadas
regular:362.desc: Sopaipillas bathed in hot chancaca with orange and cinnamon, winter dessert.
hints: The chanca is boiled with orange and cinnamon until thickened
The sopaipillas are completely immersed in the hot syrup
It is the dessert of cold and rainy days in the south of the country
The contrast between fried and sweet makes them very popular
Served hot, freshly bathed in dark honey

regular:363.name: Natilla Colombiana
regular:363.desc: Creamy dessert of corn, milk and panela curdled in pictures, infallible at Christmas.
hints: It is curdled when cooled until cut into firm frames
The panela gives you the color and sweet smoky taste
It eats next to the fritters at Christmas Eve dinner
Cinnamon in splinter is cooked next to milk
It is one of the most anticipated Christmas desserts in the country

regular:364.name: Tequeños de Plátano
regular:364.desc: Variant of the tequeño stuffed with ripe banana instead of cheese, sweet and salty at the same time.
hints: Replace classic cheese with ripe banana inside the dough
It fryes just like the traditional Tequeño until golden
It's a sweeter version, popular at children's parties
Some combine it with cheese and banana together
Serves hot, freshly fried, as a raspberry

regular:365.name: Cau Cau Limeño
regular:365.desc: mondongo stew with potato, ají amarillo and mint, Limo creole dish.
hints: The mondongo — beef bread — cooks until very tender
The herb is the scent that differentiates it from other stews
ají amarillo and turmeric give it intense yellow color
It is a dish of the criolla cuisine very popular during week
Served with white rice as a classic accompaniment

regular:366.name: Escabeche de Pescado
regular:366.desc: Fried fish in onion bittersweet sauce, ají panca and vinegar, coastal dish.
hints: The vinegar and the ají panca give the characteristic bittersweet touch
The fish is fried whole before bathing in the sauce
The onion is cooked until translucent and soft
It is typical of the Peruvian coast since colonial times
Serves cold or warm, never fresh and hot

regular:367.name: Tallarín Verde Peruano
regular:367.desc: Pasta with basil sauce, spinach and cheese, served with steak or chicken.
hints: The basil and spinach licuadas give it the intense green color
It is the most beloved Italian fusion of Peruvian Creole cuisine
It is always served accompanied by a steak or a breaded chicken
Parmesan or fresh cheese thicken the sauce to licuar
It is one of the most popular menu dishes in Lima

regular:368.name: Anticuchos de Pollo
regular:368.desc: Chicken skewers marinated in ají panca, grilled to the embers, variant of the anchovies.
hints: It's the chicken version of the traditional heart-of-res anticucho
ají panca and cumin are the base of the marinade
They roast to the embers just like the classic version
They are sold in the same night street stalls
It's softer than the heart version but just as popular

regular:369.name: Tres Leches Hondureño
regular:369.desc: Biscocho soaked in three milks with cinnamon and whipped cream, Honduran festive dessert.
hints: The three milks — evaporated, condensed and creamed — soak it completely
It is the obligatory dessert on birthdays and weddings of the country
The cinnamon sprinkled on top is the classic final touch
Serves cold after hours in the refrigerator
Central America whole disputes the exact origin of this dessert

regular:370.name: Carne Asada Costarricense
regular:370.desc: Roast beef served with gallo pinto, ripe banana and salad, typical dish tico.
hints: It is always accompanied with gallo pinto, rice with beans of the country
Mature fried banana is a fixed part of the complete dish
Lizano sauce is used to season meat on the table
It is the most traditional Sunday lunch in many homes
Served with freshly cooked hot corn tortillas

regular:371.name: Picadillo de Res Salvadoreño
regular:371.desc: Ground beef with potato, carrot and spices, Salvadoran homemade stew.
hints: Potato and carrot in small cubes are the basis of stew
It is one of the most affordable and home-made dishes in the country
Served with white rice and freshly made corn tortillas
Cumin and achiote give it the typical color and aroma
It's everyday food in many Salvadoran homes

regular:372.name: Ropa Vieja Panameña
regular:372.desc: Chilted beef in tomato and pepper sauce, Panamanian version of the classic Caribbean.
hints: The meat is cooked until melted with a fork
The sofrito tomato and pepper is the base of the sauce
Served with white rice and patacones as an accompaniment
It's a very widespread dish throughout the Caribbean region
Panama City has its own variant with cilantro

regular:373.name: Empanadas Argentinas de Humita
regular:373.desc: Filled empanadas of choclo creamy, onion and cheese, sweet and soft version of the north.
hints: The choclo grated is cooked with onion until thickened
They are typical of northwestern Argentina, just like the Saltañas
The cheese is added to give creaminess to the filling
Bake until browning the dough on the outside
They taste sweeter than meat pies

regular:374.name: Tamal Chileno
regular:374.desc: Tamal corn dough with meat and olive, wrapped in leaf of choclo, similar to humita salt.
hints: It differs from the humita by carrying meat filling inside
The dough is made with choclo ground and a little butter
Wrapped in the own choclo leaf before cooking
It's typical of summer when the choclo is at its best
Southern Chile has the most traditional versions

regular:375.name: Pastel en Hoja Guatemalteco
regular:375.desc: Tamal sweet rice with raisins, wrapped in banana leaf, Guatemalan festive dessert.
hints: Rice is cooked in milk with sugar before wrapping
The raisins give the sweet and festive touch to the filling
Wrapped in banana leaf like the tamales salted
It is typical of the patron fiestas in various regions
It differs from the tamales salted as a dessert

regular:376.name: Empanada de Queso Paraguaya
regular:376.desc: Fry empanada stuffed with melted Paraguayan cheese, simple and very popular.
hints: Fresh Paraguayan cheese melts inside when the pie is fried
It is one of the simplest and fastest to prepare at home
Served as a snack with terreré or cooked mate
The dough is thin to cool quickly and become crispy
It's very common in the country's fast food stalls

regular:377.name: Cazuela de Ave Uruguaya
regular:377.desc: Chicken stew with vegetables and rice, home dish typical of Uruguayan homes.
hints: The chicken is slowly cooked next to zapallo and carrot
It is one of the most homemade and economical stews in the country
The rice is added towards the end so that it does not melt
It is served very hot on the cold days of Montevideo
Each Uruguayan family has its own variant of this recipe

regular:378.name: Brigadeiro Branco
regular:378.desc: White brigadeiro variant made with condensed milk and coconut, without cocoa.
hints: It differs from the classic brigadeiro by not carrying cocoa
The grated coconut replaces the chocolate granillo on the outside
It's just as popular on Brazilian children's birthdays
Condensed milk and butter are the basis for both
It rolls in balls just like the chocolate version

regular:379.name: Pão de Açúcar Mineiro
regular:379.desc: Sweet bread from Minas Gerais with cheese and sugar, similar to the pão de queijo but sweeter.
hints: Minas Gerais is also famous for this sweeter bread
He carries cheese mines just like the classic cheese pão
The cassava starch gives the same elastic texture
Bake until browned on the outside and become soft inside
It's typical of coffee-side mining snacks

regular:380.name: Empanada de Cambray
regular:380.desc: Fried cake stuffed with guava or cheese, sweet very popular in Cuban bakeries.
hints: Filled with sweet guava or cream cheese, sometimes both
Fry in hot oil until golden browned dough
It is one of the best selling sweets in Cuban bakeries
Sprinkle with icing sugar when taken out of oil
It is typical breakfast with Cuban coffee and one of these cupcakes

regular:381.name: Tinga Poblana
regular:381.desc: Beef or chicken shredded in tomato sauce with chipotle and onion, homemade poblano stew.
hints: The chipotle smoked gives the most characteristic flavor of stew
The onion is fried in slices before adding the sauce
Puebla is the state where this so popular stew originated
Served on toast, tacos or cake filling
It is one of the most widely reproduced stews in the whole country

regular:382.name: Arroz Rojo Mexicano
regular:382.desc: Rice cooked in sofrito tomato, garlic and onion with chicken broth.
hints: The tomato blended and fried is the base that gives it the red color
Fry raw rice in oil before adding liquid
Chicken broth gives it more flavor than simple water
It is the accompaniment of virtually any Mexican food
It is decorated with peas, carrots and jalapeño pepper sometimes

regular:383.name: Frijoles de Olla
regular:383.desc: Black beans or berries cooked in clay pot with epazote and salt, Mexican basic recipe.
hints: The epazote is the grass that gives it the most authentic aroma
They cook slowly for hours until very soft
The clay pot is the traditional container to prepare them
They are the base of refried, cooled beans and many other dishes
They are accompanied by corn tortillas freshly made in comal

regular:384.name: Guacamole
regular:384.desc: Avocado sauce crushed with tomato, onion, serrano pepper, cilantro and lemon.
hints: Hass avocado is the most used for its perfect creamy texture
It is crushed with fork or molcajete, never in blender
Lemon prevents it from rusting and gives it the necessary acidity
The serrano pepper gives it the fresh itching that characterizes it
Served with corn totopos as a snack or accompaniment

regular:385.name: Carnitas Michoacanas
regular:385.desc: Pork meat cooked in its own fat with orange, milk and spices, typical of Michoacán.
hints: Michoacán is the state that claims the best version of the country
All pork is cooked in a single large copper pot
Orange and milk give you the final golden caramelization
Served in tacos with green sauce, cilantro and onion
The process lasts hours over very slow heat to make it soft

regular:386.name: Camarones a la Diabla
regular:386.desc: Shrimp in very spicy sauce of tree chili and tomato, intense coastal dish.
hints: Dry tree chili gives you the most intense itching of salsa
The bright red color comes from the chili and tomato together
Shrimp are skipped briefly to avoid overcooked
The Pacific and Gulf States consume it the most
Served with white rice and toast to lower the itching

regular:387.name: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo
regular:387.desc: Shrimp sautéed in abundant garlic fried in butter and olive oil.
hints: The garlic is fried in butter until golden and crispy
Shrimp are cooked briefly over high heat so that they do not harden
Served on white rice or with bread to wet in the mojo
It is one of the most ordered seafood dishes in coastal restaurants
The lemon is squeezed at the end to give the final acid touch

regular:388.name: Mojarra Frita
regular:388.desc: Whole fried fish until crispy, served with lemon and green sauce.
hints: The fish is fried whole, with diagonal cuts in the body
The diagonal cut allows it to cool better and more even
Served in seafood stalls by rivers and coasts
Lemon and green sauce are inseparable accompaniments
Veracruz and the southern states are the ones that consume it the most

regular:389.name: Huaraches con Nopales
regular:389.desc: Mass of corn in elongated form of huarache, with beans, nopales and salsa.
hints: The elongated form similar to a sandal gives it the name
Refried beans spread over the cooked dough
Clean and roasted nopals are the typical green garnish
Sold on popular markets in Mexico City
They are covered with crumbling cheese and red or green sauce

regular:390.name: Tlacoyos de Frijol
regular:390.desc: Mass of blue corn filled with beans and cooked in comal, ancient prehispanic preparation.
hints: The blue corn dough is the most traditional to make them
The ground beans are put into the dough before closing it
They cook in a dry griddle, without oil, like the tortilla
They are accompanied by cactus, cheese and green or red sauce
They are part of the oldest street food in the central region

regular:391.name: Tasajo Oaxaqueño
regular:391.desc: Salted beef, flattened and dried in the sun or smoked, typical of Oaxaca.
hints: Meat is salted and allowed to dry in the sun for days
Cut into long, thin blankets to make it dry better
Oaxaca serves it in tlayudas, tacos and memelas
Roast to the embers just before serving on the table
It's different than cecina because it's made of beef, not pork

regular:392.name: Rajas con Crema
regular:392.desc: Popular chili strips roasted with cream, corn and melted Oaxaca cheese.
hints: The poblano pepper is roasted and peeled before being cut into strips
The acidic cream gives you the softness that balances the itching
The corn in grains is added by its natural sweetness
The Oaxaca yarn cheese melts over everything else
Served in tacos, quesadillas or as garnish

regular:393.name: Machaca Norteña
regular:393.desc: Shewed and dried beef, scrambled with egg, tomato, onion and chili.
hints: The machaca is dried and crushed meat from the north of the country
Sonora and Chihuahua are the most famous states for preparing it
It is mixed with scrambled egg for Northern breakfast
Tomato, onion and serrano pepper complete the stew
It is served in flour tacos, which are typical of the north

regular:394.name: Tepache de Piña
regular:394.desc: Fermented drink of pineapple peels with piloncillo and cinnamon, refreshing and slightly alcoholic.
hints: It is made with the peel and heart of pineapple, not pulp
The piloncillo gives the dark sweetness and accelerates fermentation
Cinnamon and clove are the scents that characterize it
Fermented between 2 and 3 days at room temperature
Sold in street markets as fresh summer drink

regular:395.name: Café de Olla
regular:395.desc: Black coffee boiled in clay pot with piloncillo and cinnamon, traditional drink.
hints: The piloncillo is the traditional sweetener, never white sugar
The cinnamon sliced is boiled together with the coffee ground
The clay pot transfers a special flavor to the coffee
It's the cold morning drink in the Mexican countryside
Served in mud jars to keep the heat warm

regular:396.name: Pipián Verde
regular:396.desc: pumpkin seeds thick sauce, green chili, tomatillo and epazote on meat.
hints: The pumpkin seeds toasts are the thickening base of the sauce
tomatillo green gives acidity and color to pipián
The epazote is the aromatic herb indispensable in the recipe
Puebla and the central region claim older versions
Served on chicken, pork or enchiladas depending on region

regular:397.name: Enfrijoladas
regular:397.desc: Tortillas bathed in blended black bean sauce with pasilla pepper and cheese on top.
hints: The salsa is made by blending beans cooked with pasilla pepper
The tortillas bathe completely in the dark sauce
They are covered with crushed fresh cheese and sour cream
They are similar to enchiladas but with bean sauce
It is one of the fastest and cheapest breakfasts in the country

regular:398.name: Entomatadas
regular:398.desc: Tortillas bathed in red tomato sauce with pasilla pepper, stuffed with cheese.
hints: The salsa is made with roasted tomato and pasilla pepper or width
They are the tomato version of enchiladas or cooled
Fresh cheese or cheese is the most classic filling
Cover with cream, onion and cilantro when serving
They are a very popular breakfast dish in the center of the country

regular:399.name: Chile Pasilla Relleno
regular:399.desc: Chile pasilla stuffed with picadillo or cheese, caped in egg and fried in oil.
hints: The pasilla pepper is dry and has a more smoked flavor than the poblano
hydrates in hot water before filling
It is capped just like the chilies in walnut with beaten egg
Oaxaca and Mexico City consume it the most
The tomato sauce where they are served gives them the necessary acidity

regular:400.name: Crema de Chile Poblano
regular:400.desc: Creamy soup of poblano pepper with cream, corn and melted cheese.
hints: Poblano pepper gives the green color and soft smoky flavor
Blended with milk cream to achieve silky texture
The granulated corn is added as a floating garnish
Served as a first course in Mexican cuisine restaurants
Panela cheese or Oaxaca is added in pieces when serving hot

regular:401.name: Cabrito al Horno
regular:401.desc: Lechal goat marinated in garlic, oregano and lemon, roasted in the oven slowly.
hints: The kid is the goat under four months old
Nuevo León, in the north, is the most famous state for this dish
Sail with garlic, cumin and oregano before roasting
Served whole or in pieces with flour tortillas and salsa
Sundays are the traditional day of eating kids as a family

regular:402.name: Molotes Oaxaqueños
regular:402.desc: Fries of corn dough stuffed with black beans and Oaxacan chorizo.
hints: The corn dough is filled and shaped in oval before frying
The Oaxacan chorizo is different from the red of the center of the country
Fry in plenty of oil until golden brown
Oaxaca sells them in markets early as breakfast
Served with green sauce and cream on top at once

regular:403.name: Agua de Horchata
regular:403.desc: Drink of ground rice with cinnamon, sugar and evaporated milk, served very cold.
hints: The rice is ground with cinnamon and let to rest in water
Sweeten with sugar and add evaporated milk at the end
It is the most consumed fresh water next to that of Jamaica
Served in large glasses with ice and sprinkled cinnamon
It has Arabic origin and arrived with the Spanish colonizers

regular:404.name: Atole de Guayaba
regular:404.desc: Hot thick corn dough drink with guava puree, cinnamon and sugar.
hints: The guava gives it the pink color and acid fruity flavor
The dough of corn dissolved in water gives it the thickness
Cinnamon and sugar complement the taste of fruit
Hot sale on popular markets in winter
It is the most fruity variant of traditional atols

regular:405.name: Sopa de Flor de Calabaza
regular:405.desc: Chicken broth with pumpkin flower, corn, poblano pepper and epazote fresh.
hints: Pumpkin flower is the most delicate ingredient of soup
You only get fresh in the summer rain months
The fresh epazote gives it the scent that distinguishes it
It is accompanied with freshly made corn tortillas
It is a light soup highly valued in modern Mexican cuisine

regular:406.name: Cecina con Tostadas
regular:406.desc: Pork meat enchilada and dried served on toast with avocado and cheese.
hints: Yecapixtla's cecina in Morelos is the most famous in the country
The meat is cut into very thin slices before enchilating
The ancho pepper gives it the dark red color and smoked flavor
Roast in griddle or grill just before serving
Morelos serves it in tlayudas, tacos and memelas as well

regular:407.name: Verdolagas con Cerdo
regular:407.desc: Vegetable stew — wild plant — cooked with pork and green sauce.
hints: Vegetables are very nutritious edible wild plants
They are cooked in tomatillo green sauce and serrano pepper
The pork in pieces is fried before adding the sauce
It is a very popular stew in Mexico City and downtown
Vegetables provide a slightly acidic flavor to the stew

regular:408.name: Tamales de Elote
regular:408.desc: Tamales sweets of tender corn ground with sugar, cinnamon and cheese, without extra filling.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the sweet dough
Cinnamon and sugar are the only flavorings added
They don't carry meat stuffing, just sweet corn dough
Steamed on corn leaves like all tamales
They are the dessert of Christmas tamales in many families

regular:409.name: Cabeza de Res Taquera
regular:409.desc: Taco of tacked meat, tongue or beef brains steamed, special taquería.
hints: The beef slap is the softest and most juicy
It is steamed for hours until it melts itself
Head tacos are sold in specialized taquerías
The cilantro, onion and green sauce are the companions
Mexico City has taquerías open early in the morning for these tacos

regular:410.name: Agua de Tamarindo
regular:410.desc: Refreshing drink of tamarind pod dissolved in water with sugar.
hints: The tamarind is undone in hot water and strained
Sweetness and acidity balance with sugar to taste
It is one of the most popular fresh waters in the country next to lemon
It is served very cold with ice in large market glasses
The tamarind pulp contains the most intense acidic flavor

regular:411.name: Pozole de Mariscos
regular:411.desc: pozole coastal variant with shrimp, octopus and seafood in corn broth.
hints: It is the marine version of the traditional pozole saw
Peanut corn remains the base of broth
The Pacific coastal states invented this variant
It is decorated as the classic with lettuce, radish and oregano
The broth is lighter than the pork version

regular:412.name: Tamal Veracruzano
regular:412.desc: Tamal corn dough with mole and chicken, wrapped in banana leaf, typical of Veracruz.
hints: The banana leaf is the classic Veracruz wrapper, not the corn wrapper
The mole thick red with chicken is the most traditional filling
Veracruz, in the Gulf of Mexico, has rich fusion cuisine
It is steamed like the tamales corn leaf
They're bigger and heavier than the tamales in the center of the country

regular:413.name: Boquerones en Vinagre
regular:413.desc: Fresh anchovies macerated in vinegar and olive oil with garlic and parsley, very popular lid.
hints: Fresh anchovies marinate in vinegar for hours without cooking
The acid of vinegar heals the fish naturally
Fine chopped garlic and fresh parsley are added at the end
It is the most classic tapas of bars on the Mediterranean coast
Cold served directly from the fridge with toasted bread

regular:414.name: Croquetas de Jamón
regular:414.desc: Thick bechamel croquettes with chopped Iberian ham, empanadas and fried.
hints: The very thick bechamel is the base that keeps them creamy
Iberian ham gives you the salty and smoked flavor that distinguishes them
They empanate twice so that the outside is crispy
They are the most popular tapas in bars all over Spain
The best ones are sold in the taverns of Madrid and San Sebastián

regular:415.name: Pan con Tomate Catalán
regular:415.desc: Roast bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, seasoned with olive oil and salt.
hints: The bread is roasted first and then rubbed with raw garlic
The mature tomato split is rubbed directly on the bread
Catalonia is the region that created and exported this simple breakfast
Extra virgin olive oil pours generously on top
It is the most common breakfast in any Catalan home or bar

regular:416.name: Escalivada Catalana
regular:416.desc: Red peppers and aubergines roasted at fire, peeled and seasoned with olive oil.
hints: Vegetables are roasted whole on fire or under the grill of the oven
The skin is removed while they are still warm and release it better
Extra virgin olive oil and salt are the only dressing
Catalonia serves as a garrison or cold entrance
It is accompanied with bread of pagès and anchovies in some versions

regular:417.name: Crema Catalana
regular:417.desc: Egg yolk creams with milk, lemon and cinnamon, with scab of sugar burned on top.
hints: The sugar scab is burned with blowtorch or hot paddle just before serving
It is the Spanish equivalent of French crème brûlée, but earlier
Catalonia claims the oldest documented invention of this dessert
Milk is flavoured with cinnamon and lemon bark before cooking
Served in individual clay cazuelita directly to the table

regular:418.name: Fideuà Valenciana
regular:418.desc: Short noodles cooked in paellera with seafood, fish broth and saffron.
hints: Noodles are roasted first in oil before adding broth
Fish broth is the key to intense marine flavor
It is made in paellera just like paella, but with noodles instead of rice
Gandía, on the Valencian coast, claims the invention of the dish
The socarrat of crispy noodles in the background is just as appreciated

regular:419.name: Arroz al Horno Valenciano
regular:419.desc: Rice with chickpeas, rib, sausage and tomato, baked in clay casserole.
hints: Bake in clay casserole at high temperature until grating
The chickpeas and ribs give the bottom of the broth
The onion sausage gives it the dark and spicy flavor
Valencia cooks it on Sundays with the leftovers of cooking
It is distinguished from paella by making it in oven, not fire

regular:420.name: Lechazo Asado
regular:420.desc: Pork lamb roasted in wood oven only with water, salt and butter, in clay casserole.
hints: The milk lamb is less than 35 days old and only feeds on milk
Castilla y León, especially Aranda de Duero, is its historical cradle
Just bring water, salt and some lard as ingredients
Roast in low temperature clay casserole for two hours
The skin should be so crispy that it breaks with a spoonful

regular:421.name: Cocido Montañés
regular:421.desc: White beans stew with beers, chorizo and sausage, typical of Cantabria.
hints: Berry — green cabbage — is the differentiating ingredient of cantabra cooked
Cantabria, in the rainy north, is its region of historical origin
White beans replace chickpeas from the cooked Madrid
The chorizo and the sausage cantabra give you the deep smoky flavor
It is a winter dish that warms well in the northern cold

regular:422.name: Porrusalda Vasca
regular:422.desc: Leek soup, potato and carrot in broth, with or without cod, from the Basque Country.
hints: Leek is the most abundant ingredient and protagonist
It cooks very slowly until the potato almost melts
The version with desalado cod is the most consumed in Easter
The Basque Country considers it one of its most traditional soups
It is a very simple dish that stands out for the quality of leek

regular:423.name: Lacón con Grelos
regular:423.desc: Cured pork duck cooked with bitter greens, potato and chorizo, Galician winter dish.
hints: Lacon is the front leg of salt-cured pork
The greens are the tender shoots of turnips, bitter and nutritious
Galicia consumes it especially in winter and Carnival
Everything is cooked together in water for hours
It is considered the most representative dish of Galician winter cuisine

regular:424.name: Filloas Gallegas
regular:424.desc: Very fine crepes of flour, milk, egg and sometimes broth, typical of the Galician Carnival.
hints: They're thinner than French crepes and less sweet
The pork broth version is the oldest and most traditional
Made in the hot stones of traditional Galician fires
Galicia prepares them especially in Carnival and Easter
Filled with cream, honey or eaten alone sprinkled with sugar

regular:425.name: Morcilla de Burgos
regular:425.desc: Pig blood sausage with rice, onion and spices, in natural gut.
hints: Rice makes it different from other sausages that carry onion alone
Burgos, in Castile, produces the most famous and exported variant
It eats fried, roasted or cooked depending on the recipe
It is the favorite sausage for eggs with breakfast pudding
Sweet paprika and oregano are its characteristic spices

regular:426.name: Patatas a la Riojana
regular:426.desc: Potatoes with chorizo riojano, pepper choricero and paprika, casserole stew and tasty.
hints: The chorizo riojano gives it the red color and smoked flavor
The potatoes are cracked, not cut, to thicken the broth
