Rioja, a wine country of the north, is its region of origin
The dried choricero pepper is used to deepen the taste
It is an economic stew and very popular throughout the Spanish Plateau

regular:427.name: Chilindrón Aragonés
regular:427.desc: Chicken or lamb stewed with red pepper, tomato, onion and ham in sauce.
hints: Roast red pepper is the basis of thick stew sauce
Aragon, in the northeast, is the region that created and claims the dish
The serrano ham in pieces gives the salty and smoked touch
It can be made with chicken, rabbit or lamb according to preference
It is the dish of summer festivals in Aragonese villages

regular:428.name: Rancho Canario
regular:428.desc: Chickpea stew with noodles, pork and vegetables, dish of the Canary Islands.
hints: The Canary Islands have their own African and Peninsular cuisine
The chickpeas and noodles are cooked together in the same broth
Pork and seasonal vegetables vary according to island
It is the dish of cold days of winter canary
It differs from fabada and cooked by its Canarian ingredients

regular:429.name: Frangollo Canario
regular:429.desc: Gofio dessert or corn flour cooked with milk, sugar, lemon and almonds.
hints: Gofio or coarse corn flour is the thickening base
The Canary Islands have consumed it as dessert since Guanches times
Hot milk is poured over the gophie stirring non-stop
The toasted almonds and lemon bark aromatize it
Serve cold in individual molds or in a large fountain

regular:430.name: Porra Antequerana
regular:430.desc: Thick tomato, bread, garlic, pepper and olive oil cream, similar to salmon, but denser.
hints: It is thicker than the salmon because it carries more bread in the mixture
Antequera, in Malaga, is the city that created it and defends it
Crowned with canned tuna and chopped hard egg
The olive oil is added in fine thread to the liqueur to emulsify
It is served cold as a first dish in the intense summer months

regular:431.name: Flamenquín Cordobés
regular:431.desc: Pork loin fillet rolled with ham, empanado and fried, from Cordoba.
hints: The pork loin rolls over a slice of serrano ham
Dried in egg and breadcrumbs before frying in oil
Córdoba claims it as its most famous and unique appetizer
Serves cut into slices as a ration or snack
The juicy interior contrasts with the very crispy exterior

regular:432.name: Remojón Granadino
regular:432.desc: Orange salad with demigrated cod, black olives and onion in Granada.
hints: Fresh orange in slices is the basis of this winter salad
Unbleached and shredded cod is distributed over the fruit
Granada, in deep Andalusia, is its city of origin
Virgin olive oil and sherry vinegar season it
It is typical of Easter and the cold months of the year

regular:433.name: Turrón de Jijona
regular:433.desc: Sweet almond soft ground with honey, sugar and egg white, the Christmas soft nougat.
hints: Jijona, in the province of Alicante, produces 90% of the soft nougat
Valencian almond is ground to form an unctuous paste
Honey and sugar cook together before mixing pasta
It comes as a tablet and has a texture that breaks down when eating
It's the best selling Christmas candy on the Spanish market next to the hard one

regular:434.name: Buñuelos de Viento Madrileños
regular:434.desc: Very light fried dough balls stuffed with cream or cream, typical of All Saints Day.
hints: The dough carries flour, egg, butter and boiled water together
They fry in very hot oil until inflated by steam
On November 1, they eat with hot chocolate in Madrid
They are lighter than the classic fritter for poached dough
Filled with pastry cream or eaten alone with icing sugar

regular:435.name: Gambas al Ajillo
regular:435.desc: Sautéed prawns in very hot olive oil with garlic and guindilla, classic tapas.
hints: The oil must be very hot for the shrimps to squirt
Garlic in foils is fried first until lightly browned
The pepper gives it the spicy touch without mastering the flavor of seafood
They are served in clay casserole squirting on the table
They are the most ordered seafood tapas in bars all over Spain

regular:436.name: Menestra de Verduras
regular:436.desc: Seasonal vegetable stew — artichokes, peas, asparagus — in light broth.
hints: Navarra and La Rioja compete for the best version of the country
The vegetables are cooked each separate so that they are at their point
Artichoke, pea and asparagus are the most valued
Add Iberian ham in tacos to give the flavor background
It is one of the most elegant vegetable dishes in Spanish cuisine

regular:437.name: Polvorones de Estepa
regular:437.desc: Very demenuzable cookie of toasted flour, lard, sugar and cinnamon.
hints: The flour is roasted in a frying pan before mixing with butter
Steppe, in Seville, produces the most famous in the world
Pork butter is the secret ingredient of its unique texture
They're the best-selling Christmas candy next to buttered
Discard the first bite in the mouth in a characteristic way

regular:438.name: Guiso de Lentejas con Chorizo
regular:438.desc: Peasy lentils with chorizo, carrot, pepper and bay leaf, the easiest spoon dish.
hints: Pardine lentils do not need previous soaking unlike others
The chorizo in slices gives the red color and smoky flavor to the broth
The laurel, cumin and paprika are the spices that are not lacking
It's the most cooked weekend dish in the country's homes
They are served very hot with a splash of vinegar at the end

regular:439.name: Pipirrana Andaluza
regular:439.desc: Summer salad with tomato, cucumber, pepper, onion, hard egg and tuna in oil.
hints: All ingredients are minced very small before mixing
It is the most refreshing and popular summer salad in the South
Jaén and Granada have the oldest documented versions
Extra virgin olive oil is the main dressing
It is served very cold as a first dish on the hottest days

regular:440.name: Alboronía Cordobesa
regular:440.desc: Arab stew of aubergines, pumpkin, onion and honey, inherited from Al-Andalus in Cordoba.
hints: It is a stew of Andalusian Arab origin preserved since the 12th century
Eggplant and pumpkin are cooked together with honey and spices
Cumin, cinnamon and pepper are its Arab spices
Córdoba keeps this recipe almost intact since the Moorish era
Served as a side dish for roasted meats or as a single dish

regular:441.name: Atún Encebollado
regular:441.desc: Simmered bluefin tuna fillet with onion, tomato, white wine and bay leaf.
hints: Atlantic bluefin tuna is the most valued for this preparation
The onion is cooked very slowly until caramelize and become soft
Andalusian white wine gives acidity and aroma to the stew
Cádiz and the Portuguese Algarve are its areas of marine origin
It is served tempered, never very hot, so that the flavors settle

regular:442.name: Humita en Olla
regular:442.desc: Grated fresh corn simmered with onion, chilli and tomato, a creamy pot-cooked version of humita.
hints: Unlike the classic wrapped humita, this version is cooked in a pot.
The onion and tomato are sautéed before the grated corn is added.
This creamy version is especially popular in the Andean northwest.
Ground chilli gives it a reddish colour and gentle heat.
It is served hot as a starter during the colder months.

regular:443.name: Puchero Argentino
regular:443.desc: Cooked meats with vegetables, chickpeas and noodles in broth, Buenos Aires version of the cooked.
hints: Buenos Aires adopted this stew of Spanish and Italian immigrants
He's got beef pout, chorizo, chicken and sometimes mondongo together
Vegetables are added staggered according to their cooking time
It is served in two times: first the broth with noodles, then the meat
It is the dish of cold days of winter Buenos Aires

regular:444.name: Matambre a la Pizza
regular:444.desc: Fine slaughter of beef covered in tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese and oregano, grilled.
hints: Matambre is the fine skirt cut very appreciated in the Rio de la Plata
Covered with classic pizza ingredients and brought to grill
It is one of the most popular variants of Argentine matambre
Buenos Aires and the coast are where it is consumed the most
The Italian influence on Argentine gastronomy is evident in this dish

regular:445.name: Bife de Chorizo
regular:445.desc: Cut thick and juicy beef from the top of the loin, grilled with salt.
hints: It's the most ordered cut in the country's grilled restaurants
It has nothing to do with the sausage, it's just the name of the cut
Thick salt is the only seasoning that needs this premium cut
It is ordered by cooking points: stitched, juicy or round and round
Argentina’s pampas with their grass herd produce the best

regular:446.name: Entraña a la Parrilla
regular:446.desc: Cut of very thin and juicy rib diaphragm, roasted quickly to the embers.
hints: It cooks very quickly because it is a thin cut that hardens if passed
It's the favorite cut of parrillaros who know how to appreciate it
The exterior is with crispy crust and the inside pink and juicy
It is served cut diagonally to facilitate the bite
It is one of the cheapest but tastiest cuts of the cow

regular:447.name: Revuelto Gramajo
regular:447.desc: Scrambled eggs with crispy straw potatoes, ham and peas, classic porteño dish.
hints: Potatoes are cut into fine julian straws and fried separately
Its creation was attributed to Colonel Artemio Gramajo in the 19th century
The cooked ham and peas are mixed with the scrambled egg
It is a typical dish of Buenos Aires Buenos Aires Buenos Aires cuisine
It is served in bistros and restaurants of Argentine Creole cuisine

regular:448.name: Rogel Argentino
regular:448.desc: Fine pastry layer cake with sweet milk and burnt meringue on top.
hints: The layers of very fine puff pastry are separated with generous milk sweet
The Italian meringue is placed on top and burned with blowtorch
It is the most traditional birthday cake and celebrations in the country
Each province has its own slightly different variant
Can be done with many layers, up to 10 or 12 in festive versions

regular:449.name: Pastelitos de Membrillo
regular:449.desc: Square pastries of leafy dough stuffed with quince or sweet potato, fried.
hints: The dough folds squarely over the filling of sweet quince
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy
They are typical of the 25th of May and the festivities in Argentina
Markets are sold especially on national holidays
Sweet sweet potato or quince are the two most classic fillers

regular:450.name: Pionono Relleno
regular:450.desc: Slim cake rolled with milk sweet, cream or salty filling of ham and cheese.
hints: The cake is baked very finely in a tray and rolled hot
Sweet version carries sweet milk and whipped cream
Salty version carries ham, cheese and mayonnaise
It is the most popular roll cake of informal parties
Mar del Plata has a particularly famous seafood version

regular:451.name: Budín de Pan
regular:451.desc: Dessert of hard bread soaked in milk with eggs, sugar and lemon grated, baked.
hints: The bread of the day before is soaked in milk to soften
It is mixed with eggs, sugar and lemon or orange zest
Bake in a potty bath to make it creamy inside
It is the most popular dessert of Argentine grandmothers
It is served deflated with caramel or milk cream on top

regular:452.name: Churrasco a la Criolla
regular:452.desc: Fine fillet of grilled beef with tomato creole sauce, onion and pepper.
hints: Creole sauce is made cold with tomato, onion and pepper
The steak is cooked over very high heat to seal it quickly
It is the most ordered dish in Buenos Aires still lifes
Served with fries or white rice as an accompaniment
The cold creole sauce on hot meat is the key contrast

regular:453.name: Pollo al Verdeo
regular:453.desc: Chicken in green onion sauce — onion — with cream of milk and white wine.
hints: The green onion is the green onions with the long stem
Sauté before adding cream and white wine to chicken
It is a very simple dish of home cooking Buenos Aires
Dry white wine cuts fat from milk cream
Served with rice or mashed potatoes to absorb the sauce

regular:454.name: Zapallitos Rellenos
regular:454.desc: Zapallitos — zabacines — stuffed with ground meat or tuna with cheese gratin on top.
hints: The pumpkins are a variety of round and small zucchini
They are emptied, stuffed with picadillo and baked until grating
They are a typical dish of home cooking in the central provinces
Creamy cheese or mozzarella melts in the oven on top
They are also stuffed with rice, ham and vegetables in vegetarian version

regular:455.name: Ravioles Caseros Porteños
regular:455.desc: Pasta stuffed with ricota and spinach, with meat tuco or fillet sauce, Italian dominguera.
hints: Fresh pasta is made at home on Sunday morning
The filling of ricotta with spinach or minced meat is the most classic
Tuco (meat sauce) is the most traditional sauce to serve
Buenos Aires has the largest concentration of italo-argentinos in the world
Making ravioli in the family on Sunday is a deeply rooted tradition

regular:456.name: Matambre Relleno
regular:456.desc: Slaughter of beef stuffed with hard egg, vegetables and cheese, rolled over and baked.
hints: The kill spreads, fills and rolls tightly
The filling of hard egg, carrot and cheese is seen in slices when cut
It is tied with cooking thread before baking or cooking in broth
Serves cold cut into slices as inlet or coldness
It is the most elegant roast or birthday dish to present

regular:457.name: Sorrentinos de Jamón y Queso
regular:457.desc: Large circular pasta of ham and cheese, specializing in Mar del Plata.
hints: They're bigger and fatter than traditional ravioli
Mar del Plata popularized them in the 1960s in their restaurants
The filling of cooked ham and creamy cheese is the most traditional
Served with butter and sage or meat tuco
They are the most demanded stuffed pasta in Marplatense restaurants

regular:458.name: Carbonada Criolla
regular:458.desc: Meat stew with zapallo, choclo, peaches and rice, served inside a zapallo.
hints: The most spectacular presentation is serving the stew inside an empty pumpkin
Peaches give a sweet touch that contrasts with salted meat
The Argentine Northwest has the oldest versions of this stew
The choclo sliced and the zapallo in cubes are its base ingredients
Bake the whole zapallo with the stew inside for the festive presentation

regular:459.name: Bondiola al Horno
regular:459.desc: Pork chop marinated in garlic, wine and spices, slowly baked until tender.
hints: Bondiola is the pork paddle, a cut with lots of collagen
It marinates at least 12 hours before entering the oven
Red wine and garlic are the basis of classic marinade
Bake covered for hours and discovered at the end to brown
It is the most popular pig for bondiola sandwiches

regular:460.name: Alfajores Santafesinos
regular:460.desc: Three tender dough lids joined with dulce de leche and bathed in white icing sugar.
hints: They are different from the Cordobas by carrying three layers of dough
Santa Fe invented them with the white cover of icing sugar
The dough is more tender and less sweet than that of other provinces
They eat especially with mate in the afternoon as a snack
They're more delicate and they're undone before the alfajores chocolates

regular:461.name: Milanesa a la Napolitana
regular:461.desc: Milanese meat covered in tomato sauce, ham and mozzarella cheese, baked gratin.
hints: It is said that it was invented at the Neapolitan bar in Buenos Aires in the 1950s
The tomato sauce, ham and cheese are put on the Milanese already fried
Gratin in oven until the cheese bubbles and browns
It is the most festive and abundant variant of classical Milanese
Buenos Aires exported it to the rest of the Southern Cone as its own dish

regular:462.name: Empanadas Tucumanas
regular:462.desc: Baked with juicy meat, green onion, hard egg and cumin from Tucumán.
hints: Tucumán calls itself the national capital of the Argentine empanada
Cumin is the most characteristic spice of Tucuman filling
The meat is cut with a knife like in the saltews, never chopped
The filling broth makes them especially juicy when biting
The Festival of the Empanada in Famaillá summons the whole country

regular:463.name: Asado de Cordero Patagónico
regular:463.desc: Whole lamb roasted on horizontal cross over wood embers in Patagonia.
hints: Patagonia breeds the best lamb in the world for its green pastures
Roast on horizontal cross, different from the Uruguayan vertical cross
Cooking lasts between four and six hours over very slow heat
The animal usually weighs between 12 and 15 kilos for full roasting
Bariloche and Santa Cruz are the most famous destinations to eat lamb

regular:464.name: Empanadas Mendocinas
regular:464.desc: Packed with meat, onion, garlic, olives and egg, squirt closed and baked.
hints: Mendoza has its own variant with olive and less broth than the Tucumanas
Wheat-twilighting is its characteristic visual signature
The meat is cooked a little before filling, unlike the north
They are accompanied by the Malbec wine that Mendoza produces for the world
They are drier and less juicy than those in the north of the country

regular:465.name: Asado de Tira
regular:465.desc: Steak ribs cut into transverse strips and roasted to the embers slowly.
hints: The cross-section shows the bones in section, not long
It's slower to roast than other cuts into the inner bone
The thick salt is applied when the fat begins to drip
It is one of the cheapest but tastiest cuts in beef
It is served with chimichurri and Creole salad always

regular:466.name: Tarta de Acelga
regular:466.desc: Homemade dough cake stuffed with chard and egg, cheese and onion.
hints: The dough is made with flour, fat and water, very crispy when baking
The chard is soaked with onion until water is lost before filling
The egg and cheese cook the filling when baking
It is the most homemade and economical cake in Buenos Aires cuisine
It is eaten cold or warm, never reheated the same day

regular:467.name: Pebete de Jamón y Queso
regular:467.desc: Sandwich in round and soft bread with cooked ham, cheese and mayonnaise, the kiosk sandwich.
hints: The pebete bread is round, soft and slightly sweet inside
It is the best-selling sandwich in Argentine kiosks and warehouses
Bring cooked ham, feta cheese and mayonnaise without vegetables
It's the most classic snack kids take to school
Its small size and low price make it ideal for the snack

regular:468.name: Facturas Porteñas
regular:468.desc: Variety of sweet bread from pastries—watchers, croissants, cannons—from the Buenos Aires breakfast.
hints: It's the pastry breads that are bought at the bakery on Sundays
The vigilante is the most basic invoice, only sugar-plated dough
Cannoncytes carry sweet milk or pastry cream inside
Buenos Aires has the most famous bakeries on the continent
The Italian and Spanish influence in Buenos Aires pastry is total

regular:469.name: Berberechos a la Bonaerense
regular:469.desc: Berbers or clams sautéed with garlic, parsley and lemon, coastal entrance rioplatense.
hints: The coasts of the Río de la Plata produce abundant berberchos
Open steamed in skillet with hot olive oil
The chopped garlic and fresh parsley are added at the end out of heat
The lemon is squeezed over the open cockles when serving
They are a very popular snack in Puerto Madero restaurants

regular:470.name: Caldillo de Congrio
regular:470.desc: Conger broth with potatoes, onion, tomato and cilantro, the most poetic dish in the country.
hints: Congrio is a long eel and without scales highly valued in Chile
Pablo Neruda dedicated a complete ode to this dish in his poetry
Make a broth with head and fins before adding the pieces
The potatoes are cooked in the broth to absorb the marine flavor
Served with kneaded bread and a little lemon drip at the end

regular:471.name: Pantrucas Chilenas
regular:471.desc: Cuadraditos of flour dough cooked in vegetable or chicken broth, rural soup of the south.
hints: The dough stretches very thin and is cut into small squares
They are cooked directly into boiling broth
They are the Chilean equivalent of noodles but handmade dough
The Chilean countryside of the south consumes them as a winter dish
The broth can be made of vegetables, chicken or beef according to availability

regular:472.name: Longanizas Chilenas
regular:472.desc: Spicy pork sausage with garlic, cumin and chili, grilled or fried.
hints: Chillán, in the Biobío region, produces the most famous in the country
They differ from chorizo by being longer and less smoked
The cumin and the dried aji give them the spicy and smoked flavor
They're unstoppable in the Chilean barbecue next to the prites
They are accompanied with pebre and bread kneaded hot always

regular:473.name: Arrollado Huaso
regular:473.desc: Pernil pork rolled with chili, garlic and spices, cooked and served cold in slices.
hints: The pernil was marinated with chili, garlic and cumin before rolling
Be tied with pita and cooked in water with vegetables for hours
It is served cold, sliced, as meat for roasts and parties
The National Festivals of September 18th bring him to every table
The Huaso—Chilean Peasant—Gives the Name to This Preparation

regular:474.name: Torta de Mil Hojas
regular:474.desc: Strawberry cake with delicacy, cream Chantilly and walnuts, birthday dessert.
hints: The delicacy is the sweet Chilean milk, softer and darker than the Argentine
Sheet layers are already purchased ready in most homes
Garnished with crushed nuts or almonds on the edges
It is the most common birthday cake in Chilean homes
The chocolate version instead of delicacy is also very popular

regular:475.name: Chupe de Mariscos
regular:475.desc: Creamy seafood soup, varied with rice, milk, cheese and chili pepper.
hints: The colored pepper — ground paprika— gives the broth orange tone
Milk and cheese give you the creaminess that characterizes it
Valparaíso and the central coast are famous for this soup
Bring shrimp, choritos, machas and loco according to availability
Rice absorbs broth during cooking and thickens soup

regular:476.name: Valdiviano
regular:476.desc: Soup of charqui — dried meat — with potato, onion and egg, typical of the rainy south.
hints: charqui is rehydrated in water before shredding into soup
Valdivia, in the region of Los Ríos, is the city that gives it its name
Add a fried or poached egg on top when serving
It is the soup of the peasant and of the southern people in cold days
It differs from charquican in being a soup and not a dry stew

regular:477.name: Milcao de Chiloé
regular:477.desc: Crushed raw and cooked potato cake mixed, fried or baked, from Chiloé Island.
hints: Raw potato grated with potato cooked pressed in equal parts
Chiloé Island in the South is the cradle and guardian of this recipe
It can be fried in oil or grilled in embers according to the occasion
It is infallible on the curanto next to the chapalele
The filling of chicharrón or cheese is added in some versions

regular:478.name: Pebre Chileno
regular:478.desc: Fresh sauce of cilantro, onion, garlic, aji and tomato, the Chilean table salsa par excellence.
hints: The abundant fresh cilantro gives it the green color and aroma
It is prepared in mortar or simply by biting everything very thin
It is the sauce that accompanies any roast, bread or empanada
Each family has its own version with more or less aji
It is served in bowls on the table so that everyone takes to their liking

regular:479.name: Porotos Negros Guisados
regular:479.desc: Black beans stewed with zapallo, longaniza and oregano, Chilean winter soup.
hints: They're different from pomegranate porots because they're dry, not fresh
The zapallo — calabaza— gives the orange color and the sweetness to the broth
The sliced longaniza provides the smoky and spicy flavor
The dried oregano is the aromatic grass inseparable from this stew
Served with white rice or bread kneaded in the field

regular:480.name: Asado de Cerdo Chileno
regular:480.desc: Garlic marinated pork roasting, cumin and merkén, roasted slowly on grill.
hints: The merkén is the Mapuche smoky pepper that gives it a different touch
The rib is marinated all night before roasting
Cooks first on the side of the bone to cook from the inside
The National Festivals of September 18th are the moment for this dish
The thorn fire—Chilean bush—gives the best flavor to meat

regular:481.name: Cazuela de Cordero Chilena
regular:481.desc: Lamb broth with potato, pumpkin, choclo and rice, winter dish of the Chilean countryside.
hints: Patagonian lamb gives the deepest flavor to broth
A large prey of lamb with bone is placed on each plate
The pumpkin melts in the broth and gives it the orange color
Rice or noodles are added in the last minutes of cooking
It's Sunday casserole in the country's southern countryside

regular:482.name: Curanto en Olla
regular:482.desc: Cooking version of curanto with seafood, meat and potatoes cooked with steam in pot.
hints: It is the version to make at home without the land hole of the royal curant
The pot is hermetically covered for steam to do the work
Chiloé is the one who invented this most practical version of curant
Bring the same ingredients: choritos, potatoes, pork and milcao
The juice left in the pot is finally drunk as soup

regular:483.name: Estofado Chileno
regular:483.desc: Bovine beef stewed with carrot, potato, onion and red wine in pot.
hints: The meat will first sauté to seal before the slow stew
Chilean red wine gives dark color and acidity to broth
The potato and carrot are added in the last 30 minutes
Served with white rice or mashed potatoes to absorb the sauce
It is the most classic pot stew of the kitchens of the central field

regular:484.name: Kuchen de Manzana
regular:484.desc: German apple pie with cinnamon and broken dough, inherited from the southern German immigrants.
hints: German settlers from southern Chile brought this tradition of pastry
The apples of the Maule Valley are the most used for their flavor
The cinnamon powder on the apple is the touch that defines it
The broken butter dough becomes crispy when baking
The lakes of southern Chile have pastry shops famous for this kuchen

regular:485.name: Queque de Plátano
regular:485.desc: Moist cake of mature plantains crushed with brown sugar and nuts.
hints: Bananas must be very ripe, almost black, for more sweetness
The wet and dense texture differentiates it from a normal dry cake
The nuts inside give you the crunch and flavor that completes it
It's the easiest homemaker to make and favorite
It is eaten as a snack with coffee or tea in Chilean homes

regular:486.name: Pastel de Jaiba
regular:486.desc: Jaiba — Crab — demigrated in white sauce with cheese, baked in her shell.
hints: The crab — the Pacific Crab — is cooked and its meat depleted
The thick white sauce with cheese wraps it before baking
Served in the shell of the jaiba itself as a presentation
The area of Concepción and the coast of Biobío is where it is consumed the most
The cheese gratin forms a golden crust in the oven

regular:487.name: Ensalada Chilena
regular:487.desc: Sliced tomato with onion in juliana, salt, oregano and oil, classic accompaniment.
hints: The onion is put in cold water first to remove the spicy
The tomato is cut into thick slices and the onion very fine
Dry oregano is the only seasoning besides salt and oil
It is the salad that accompanies the most classic roast in the country
No vinegar or lemon, only olive oil or vegetable oil

regular:488.name: Caldo de Cabeza de Vacuno
regular:488.desc: Gelatinous beef-head broth with vegetables, garlic and cumin, reconstituted from the field.
hints: The head of beef is cooked whole for hours until the meat breaks off
The broth is very gelatinous and comforting by the collagen of the bone
It filters and is served alone or with pieces of soft meat
Garlic and cumin are the most characteristic aromas of broth
It is consumed especially in the countryside and in popular markets

regular:489.name: Torta Helada Chilena
regular:489.desc: Dessert layers of cake, delicacy, cream and preserved peaches, served very cold.
hints: The delicacy — Chilean milk sweet — is the cream between layers
Preserved peaches give you freshness and fruit juice
Refrigerate at least four hours before serving to settle
It is the favorite dessert of birthdays and summer celebrations
Chantilly cream with grated coconut decorates the top

regular:490.name: Pan de Pascua Chileno
regular:490.desc: Sweet Christmas bread with candied fruit, nuts, almonds, ginger and spices.
hints: It is prepared exclusively in December as a Christmas dessert
Colorful candied fruit is the most striking visual ingredient
Ginger, cinnamon and clove give you the festive aroma
It keeps several days and improves over time when ripening spices
It is the Chilean equivalent of Italian but denser panettone

regular:491.name: Porotos con Riendas
regular:491.desc: Pomegranate beans with long noodles, onion, tomato and paprika, summer stew.
hints: Long noodles are the reins that give the dish its name
Fresh seasonal beans are the basis of this summer stew
The red paprika sofrito gives you the color and smoky taste
It is the most expected stew when the season of pomegranates arrives
Served alone or with a piece of bread kneaded hot next to it

regular:492.name: Limonada Chilena
regular:492.desc: Lemon drink blended with water, sugar and ice until very sparkling and creamy.
hints: Unlike normal lemonade, everything is blended together with the pulp
The result is a very sparkling drink of yellow white colour
Served in high jar directly from the blender glass
It's the trendy drink in Chilean restaurants in summer
The version with Chilean pisco is the pisco sour to the Chilean

regular:493.name: Pastel de Choclo Sureño
regular:493.desc: Variant of the choclo cake with shrimp and seafood from the south instead of pine meat.
hints: Chile’s rainy south adapts classic cake with its seafood
The choclo grated and cooked with basil remains the sweet cover
The seafood and choritos base replaces the northern pine of meat
Puerto Montt and Chiloé are where this marine version was invented
Sprinkle sugar also above to brown in the oven

regular:494.name: Pulmo Frito
regular:494.desc: Poisoned and fried beef lung, very economical dish of popular southern cuisine.
hints: The lung boils first to soften it before frying
It is empanada just like the Milanese in egg and breadcrumbs
It is one of the most popular achuras dishes in the Southern countryside
Served with tomato salad and fried or cooked potatoes
It is a dish of total exploitation of the animal in the slaughter

regular:495.name: Potaje de Frijoles Negros
regular:495.desc: Thick soup of black beans with sofrito, cumin, oregano and a splash of vinegar.
hints: sofrito onion, garlic and pepper is the essential aromatic base
The vinegar at the end gives you the acidity that balances the bean
The beans are cooked until the broth is very thick
Served as a first course or as an accompanying dish for white rice
Cumin and oregano are the identitary spices of the dish

regular:496.name: Caldosa Cubana
regular:496.desc: Soup of everything: chicken, potato, green banana and vegetables in spicy broth, informal festive dish.
hints: It's called broth because it's a big broth where it fits everything
It is the dish that is made for neighborhood parties and popular birthdays
Every cook puts what he has available at the moment
The potato and the green banana are the most constant ingredients
Havana consumes it especially at the October neighborhood parties

regular:497.name: Maduros con Queso
regular:497.desc: Mature fried banana with melted white cheese on top, sweet and salty garnish.
hints: The very mature banana is fried until caramelized on the outside
Cuban white cheese gets on when it's still hot
The sweet-salted contrast is the key to this accompaniment
It is the garnish of practically any main course
The Cubans of the diaspora in Miami eat it as reminiscence of home

regular:498.name: Arroz Imperial
regular:498.desc: Rice pressed in layers with chicken in creole sauce, corn and mayonnaise, festive dish.
hints: It is layered in a mold: rice, chicken, corn, mayonnaise and rice again
Disassembles and decorates before serving in celebrations
Chicken shredded in sofrito Creole is the central filling
It is the star dish of birthdays and weddings of the Cuban community
The mayonnaise between the layers gives it the creaminess that distinguishes it

regular:499.name: Guiso de Chícharos
regular:499.desc: Potage of peas — yellow peppers — with chorizo, yam and sofrito creole.
hints: Yellow peas are dried peas that are widely used in Cuba
The yam gives consistency and body to the potage by thickening the broth
Sliced chorizo adds the characteristic smoky flavor
It is the most economical and nutritious potage in Cuban cuisine
Served on white rice as a midday spoon dish

regular:500.name: Boniato Frito
regular:500.desc: Batata or sweet potato cut into sticks and fried until crispy, antillean garnish.
hints: The sweeter inside of the sweeter sweet potato than the common potato
It's fried in plenty of oil, just like fries
The crispy texture on the outside and soft and sweet on the inside makes it special
It is the alternative garrison to toast in Cuban food
Can be salted or sprinkled with sugar according to preference

regular:501.name: Chilindrón de Pollo Cubano
regular:501.desc: Chicken stewed in red pepper sauce, tomato, capers and olives, Cuban version.
hints: Roast red pepper and tomato form the base sauce of the stew
The olives and capers give you the salty touch and briny
It is different from the Aragonese chilindron in its ingredients
Havana and the eastern region have the most popular versions
Served with white rice and fried ripe bananas always

regular:502.name: Panes con Lechón
regular:502.desc: Crispy Cuban bread with roasted pork, garlic mojo, onion and salt, the Christmas sandwich.
hints: Cuban bread has very crispy crust and fluffy crumb
The whole pig roasts on December 24th in every neighborhood
The sour and garlic orange mojo is the dressing of the suckle and bread
Sold in street stalls on 24 and 25 December
Havana and Santiago de Cuba have the best pork stalls

regular:503.name: Dulce de Coco Rallado
regular:503.desc: Coconut grated cooked with brown sugar and cinnamon until caramelizing, Cuban handmade dessert.
hints: Fresh grated coconut is cooked with sugar and water over low heat
Cinnamon and lemon zest give you the tropical aroma
Formed in balls or spreads in cool trays
It is the most popular sweet artisan in Cuban markets
It is preserved days without cooling for the sugar that preserves it

regular:504.name: Pudín de Pan Cubano
regular:504.desc: Hard bread pudding with milk, egg, sugar and vanilla, bathed in dark caramel.
hints: Last day’s hard Cuban bread is soaked in milk with sugar
The eggs give it the structure that is curdled when baking in a potty bath
The dark caramel is poured into the mold before adding the mixture
It melts cold so that the caramel falls on the pudding
It is the most widely used dessert in Cuban households

regular:505.name: Natilla Cubana
regular:505.desc: Soft pastry cream of egg yolk, milk, starch and cinnamon, Cuban homemade dessert.
hints: The egg yolk gives you the intense yellow color and richness
The corn starch thickens the cream softly without lumps
Cinnamon powder is generously sprinkled above when serving
It is the dessert of Cuban home cooking most common in homes
Serve cold after refrigerated at least two hours

regular:506.name: Caldo de Pollo Cubano
regular:506.desc: Chicken clear broth with malanga, yuca and cilantro, the island's most popular home remedy.
hints: Malanga—Caribbean root—is the most Cuban ingredient in broth
The cassava gives it the thickness and consistency that makes it so forceful
Fresh cilantro is added when serving to avoid overcooked
They say it cures any flu or discomfort you have
Serves hot with Cuban bread to wet in the broth

regular:507.name: Ensalada de Aguacate Cubana
regular:507.desc: Avocado rolls with onion, tomato, salt and lemon, fresh tropical accompaniment.
hints: Cuban avocado is twice the size of Mexican Hass
Cut into thick slices on which the other ingredients are put
Salt and lemon are the only dressing needed for this dish
It is the salad that accompanies any hot Cuban lunch
The variety of creole avocado is more aqueous and less creamy

regular:508.name: Plátano Maduro en Almíbar
regular:508.desc: Mature banana rolls cooked in sugar syrup, cinnamon and clove, simple dessert.
hints: The banana must be very ripe for it to caramelize well in the syrup
The clove and cinnamon aromatize the syrup while it boils
It is served hot or cold depending on the preference of the diner
It is the simplest and most economical dessert in Cuban cuisine
It can be accompanied with some cream cheese to balance the sweetness

regular:509.name: Tamal Cubano en Hoja
regular:509.desc: Tamal dough of tender corn with pork and sofrito, wrapped in steamed corn leaf.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the dough moister
The sofrito Cuban Creole season the dough with all its flavor
The pork in pieces is mixed into the dough before wrapping
It differs from tamal in casserole with corn leaf
Steamed for one hour and served hot

regular:510.name: Potaje de Lentejas Cubano
regular:510.desc: Peasy lentils with sofrito creole, ripe banana and a cured chorizo.
hints: The ripe banana in cubes is added to sweeten the pottage
The sofrito garlic, onion, tomato and pepper is the aromatic base
Cured chorizo gives a different smoky flavor to European
It is the lentil potage with the Caribbean seal most marked
Served on white rice for a full and nutritious lunch

regular:511.name: Ajiaco Criollo Cubano
regular:511.desc: Cuban dense soup of seven food and several meats, the most complex cooked on the island.
hints: Bring malanga, sweet potato, yucca, banana, corn and pumpkin together
The seven groceries — tubers — give you the dense and satiating texture
Pork, chicken and cassejo — dried meat — form the three meats
It's different from ajiaco Colombian in all its ingredients
Havana recognizes it as one of its most unique dishes

regular:512.name: Flan de Coco Cubano
regular:512.desc: Creamy flan of coconut milk, egg and milk condensed with dark caramel.
hints: Coconut milk gives it the tropical flavor that differentiates it from normal flan
Condensed milk makes it sweeter and creamier to the palate
Dark caramel is made first in the mold before adding mixture
Refrigerate for several hours to cook perfectly before demolishing
It is the most popular flan in the restaurants of the Havana Malecon

regular:513.name: Quimbombó con Cerdo
regular:513.desc: Okra — quimbombó — stewed with pork, sofrito and ripe banana in creole sauce.
hints: The quimbombó —okra — is a widely used African vegetable in Cuba
The natural viscosity of quimbombó thickens the sauce naturally
It is a dish of Afro-Cuban heritage with more than two centuries on the island
The pork in pieces is cooked next to the okra from the beginning
Served with white rice to absorb thick sauce

regular:514.name: Mariquitas
regular:514.desc: Green banana cut into very thin slices and fried until crispy as chips.
hints: The green banana is cut into very thin sheets with mandolin
Fry in hot oil until completely crispy
Salt right out of the oil for salt to stick
They are the most popular Cuban street appetizer next to the Tostones
In Miami they sell them as a snack in bags in all Cuban wineries

regular:515.name: Bacán Cubano
regular:515.desc: Mature banana dough with pork and spices, wrapped in steamed banana leaf.
hints: It differs from tamal for using mature bananas instead of tender corn
The inside of spicy pork contrasts with the sweet dough of banana
It is an inheritance of Afro-Cuban cuisine of congo origin
The eastern part of the island is where this recipe is most preserved
It is steamed wrapped in banana leaf for one hour

regular:516.name: Boliche Cubano
regular:516.desc: Beef stuffed with chorizo and olives, braised in wine and sofrito creole.
hints: The bowl is a cut of beef that is drilled to fill the center
The chorizo in strips and olives are the classic filling
It is slowly grilled in red or dry wine with the sofrito criollo
When cut into slices it shows the colorful filling in the center
It is the dish of special Sundays in the Cuban family

regular:517.name: Arroz con Mariscos
regular:517.desc: Green cilantro rice with varied seafood, ají amarillo and chicha jora.
hints: The blended cilantro dyes the intense green rice
chicha jora — fermented corn — is the secret ingredient of taste
Seafood is added in the last few minutes to avoid overcooked
Lima and the North Coast compete to make the best version
The ají amarillo gives you the itch and aroma that distinguishes it

regular:518.name: Chilcano de Pescado
regular:518.desc: Light broth of fish heads with kion — ginger, ají amarillo and lemon.
hints: Fishheads are used to give the most concentrated broth
The kion — ginger— gives the heat and special aroma to the broth
The ají amarillo whole is put to aromatize without biting too much
It is the most popular remedy against hangovers all along the coast
Served with lemon, salt and table aji to adjust to taste

regular:519.name: Olluquito con Charqui
regular:519.desc: Ollucos stew — yellow Andean tuber— with charqui and ají panca.
hints: The olluco is a small andean tuber of lemon yellow colour
charqui — flame or beef dried meat — is hydrated before use
The ají panca gives it the dark red color and the earthy taste
It is one of the oldest dishes in Peruvian Andean cuisine
Served with white rice for a full lunch in the mountains

regular:520.name: Bistec a lo Pobre
regular:520.desc: Beef steak with fries, rice, fried egg, fried banana and pickled onion.
hints: The name is ironic because it is a very abundant dish, not poor
Bring steak, rice, fries, ripe banana and fried egg all together
The pickled onion in lemon and salt is the refreshing accompaniment
It is the Peruvian version of the dishes Creole everything on a plate
Lima serves it in the popular menus of Creole restaurants

regular:521.name: Arroz Tapado
regular:521.desc: Rice pressed in mold on minced meat, tomato and raisins, unmodified and served.
hints: The rice in the form of a dome is pressed on the meat minced
The picadillo carries ground meat, tomato, onion, olives and raisins
The demoulding reveals the presentation in the form of a rice volcano
It is the most creative dish of Lima cuisine
Garnished with hard egg and black olives when demolishing

regular:522.name: Causa Norteña
regular:522.desc: Cause variant with crab, palm and mayonnaise, typical of the northern Peruvian coast.
hints: The country’s northern coast produces the best river crabs
The shredded crab replaces the tuna or chicken with the classic cause
The creamy avocado goes between the layers of yellow potato
Trujillo and Piura are the cities where it is prepared with more elegance
The Northern cause is often larger and more generous than Lima’s

regular:523.name: Shambar
regular:523.desc: Dense soup of wheat, beans, pork and herbs, typical dish of northern Peru.
hints: The peeled wheat is cooked for hours until disintegrated into the broth
Green beans give color and vegetable protein to the stew
The La Libertad region, especially Trujillo, consumes it on Mondays
It is a legacy of pre-Hispanic cuisine adapted with Spanish pork
The cilantro and the herb are aromatic herbs that are not lacking

regular:524.name: Pepián de Cuy
regular:524.desc: Cuy —cobayo— in thick sauce of pumpkin seeds toast and ají panca.
hints: The pumpkin seeds toasted and ground thickens the dense sauce
The ají panca gives it the dark red color and deep taste
The cuy is cooked whole and served in pieces on the sauce
It is the most complex holiday dish that combines these two Andean ingredients
Ayacucho and Cusco are the regions where it is best prepared

regular:525.name: Patita con Maní
regular:525.desc: Pork duck cooked in roasted peanut sauce, ají amarillo and yellow potatoes.
hints: The pork leg is cooked until very gelatinous and tender
The ground roasted peanut gives the creaminess and flavor to the sauce
The ají amarillo gives the plate the itching and golden color
It is a dish of the Lima Creole cuisine of African influence
Served with cooked yellow potatoes as an accompaniment

regular:526.name: Ceviche Mixto
regular:526.desc: Ceviche with fish, shrimp, shells and squid in the same acid tiger milk.
hints: Mix several seafood in the same marinade of lemon and chili
Squid and black shells give different textures to the dish
The tiger's milk of a mixed ceviche is more intense than that of the single
It is the most ordered dish in the cevicherías of Lima
The choclo Peruvian white and the canchita always accompany

regular:527.name: Sudado de Mero
regular:527.desc: Mero stewed in its own steam with onion, tomato, ají amarillo and chicha jora.
hints: The sweaty name comes from the fish being cooked in its own steam
The grouper is the most appreciated rock fish on the Peruvian coast
chicha jora gives acidity and body to light broth
Onion and tomato are put in layers on raw fish
Served in the bowl where it was cooked, with rice next to it

regular:528.name: Tacu Tacu de Frijoles
regular:528.desc: A golden pan-fried cake of cooked white beans, rice and spices, crisp outside and soft inside.
hints: The white-bean version differs slightly from the black-bean version.
The mixture is flattened in a frying pan until crisp outside and soft inside.
Culantro, a broad-leaved herb with a coriander-like flavour, is mixed into the rice and beans.
In Lima, it is a popular way to turn leftovers into breakfast or lunch.
It is served topped with a fried egg or stir-fried meat.

regular:529.name: Ponche Arequipeño
regular:529.desc: Hot milk drink with beaten egg, cinnamon and pisco, the reconstituter of Arequipa.
hints: The egg is beaten with sugar until foaming before adding hot milk
The pisco of Arequipa gives it the alcoholic touch that distinguishes it
The cinnamon powder is generously sprinkled on top of serving
Arequipa consumes it especially on the cold nights of the highlands
It is different from Mexican Rompope in the use of Peruvian pisco

regular:530.name: Arroz con Leche Peruano
regular:530.desc: Rice in milk with cinnamon, clove, lemon peel and sugar, served with purple dungeon.
hints: The combination with purple dungeon is called the Peruvian classic combo
Evaporated milk enriches the recipe by giving it more creaminess
The clove and cinnamon are cooked with rice from the beginning
It's the best-selling dessert in Lima's Criollos spicy restaurants
Served in small glasses next to each other in the classic

regular:531.name: Caldo de Gallina Serrana
regular:531.desc: Country chicken broth with thick noodles, potato and mint, Andean restorer dish.
hints: The field chicken gives a much more concentrated and tasty broth
Thick noodles — tallarines — are cooked directly in the hot broth
Fresh mint at the end gives it the scent that distinguishes it
It is the dish served by the restaurants of the mountains at 6 am
Add spicy table aji and lemon to taste on the table

regular:532.name: Picante de Mariscos
regular:532.desc: Seafood in spicy salsa of red chili pepper, peanut and turmeric, festive dish Arequipeño.
hints: Arequipa is the cradle of this very spicy seafood dish
Dry red pepper and ají amarillo form the double spicy sauce
The ground roasted peanut gives the consistency and flavor to nut
Served as a celebratory dish in the Arequipa peppers
The chicharrón of squid above is the final touch most appreciated

regular:533.name: Chupe de Camarones Arequipeño
regular:533.desc: Creamy soup of shrimps with potato, choclo, rice, egg and ají amarillo from Arequipa.
hints: The river shrimps of Arequipa are the most appreciated in the country
Arequipa is the city where it originated and where it is best prepared
Milk and fresh cheese give you the creaminess that distinguishes it
The ají amarillo gives you the color and itching that makes it unique
It is the Sunday dish in the restaurants of Arequipa

regular:534.name: Tortilla de Papa Peruana
regular:534.desc: Thick egg tortilla with potato cooked in slices, onion and ají amarillo.
hints: The potato cooked in slices is added between the beaten egg
The ají amarillo gives it the golden color and the soft flavor that distinguishes it
It is the Peruvian version of the Spanish tortilla adapted to Andean taste
Served as a breakfast or snack with molded bread
Lima markets sell it in individual portions to take away

regular:535.name: Lomo a lo Pobre
regular:535.desc: Fine loin fillet with fries, fried egg and fried banana, premium version of the steak.
hints: It's the most expensive version of the steak to the poor for using thin loin
The fine loin is sealed in very hot skillet to seal the juices
Everything is mounted on the plate visually and abundantly
It is the most popular dish in modern Creole restaurants
The ripe fried sweet banana contrasts with the salty loin

regular:536.name: Tallarín Saltado
regular:536.desc: Noodles skipped chifa style with beef, peppers, soy and tomato, Chinese-Peruvian fusion.
hints: He's the brother of the bouncing loin noodles but with chifa paste
The noodles are skipped in wok over very high heat just like the Chinese technique
Soybean—sillao—and kion — ginger—are the key condiments
Lima has thousands of chifa restaurants that have it on their menu
It is one of the most popular fusion dishes in everyday Lima cuisine

regular:537.name: Mute Santandereano
regular:537.desc: Corn soup peeled with beef, chickpeas, creole potato and field herbs.
hints: Mute is the corn peeled in bleach, typical of indigenous cuisine
Santander is the department where this dish is most emblematic
The beef is cooked for hours until it becomes very tender
The chickpea gives the thick consistency that makes it so substantial
It's the Thursday and Sunday dish at Santanderean restaurants

regular:538.name: Cuchuco de Trigo
regular:538.desc: Thick wheat soup broken with pork thorn, potato and Andean herbs from Boyacá.
hints: The broken wheat is cooked for hours until disposed in the broth
The pork thorn gives the fatty and rich taste to the bottom of soup
Boyacá and Cundinamarca are the departments that consume it the most
It is the dish of local markets and shops of the buoyacense highlands
The orange blossom herbs and the cilantro aromatize it at the end

regular:539.name: Cholado del Valle
regular:539.desc: Ice grated with tropical fruits, covered in condensed milk, syrup and chamoy.
hints: The ice grates very finely so that it absorbs the flavors
The Valle del Cauca, especially Cali, is famous for this dessert
Tropical fruits go over ice: mango, blackberry, pineapple, grape
Condensed milk and fruit syrup make it very sweet
It is Cali's most popular street dessert on hot days

regular:540.name: Obleas con Arequipe
regular:540.desc: Two large hosts of flour filled with arequipe — milk sweet — with cheese and strawberries.
hints: The wafers are very fine discs of flour like big hosts
The Colombian team is more liquid than the Argentine milk candy
You can add jam, grated cheese or strawberries on top
They're the best-selling street candy in any city in the country
Bogota and the coffee axis have the most famous wafer stands

regular:541.name: Bocadillo con Queso
regular:541.desc: Solid sweet guava paste with white peasant cheese, the most Colombian combination.
hints: The guava sandwich solidifies until cut into cubes
The sweet-salted contrast with white cheese is the secret of pleasure
Vélez, in Santander, produces the most famous and exported snack
It is sold wrapped in bijao leaf as did the grandmothers
It is the accompaniment of red coffee in the mornings

regular:542.name: Arepas de Choclo
regular:542.desc: Arepa sweet tender corn with melted cheese, typical of the coffee region and Antioquia.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw and the dough becomes sweeter and moister
The peasant cheese melts inside when cooking them in the griddle
They are smaller and thicker than the traditional arepas white
Eje Cafetero and Medellin sell them at the corner for breakfast
They are the sweetest arepas and favorite of Colombian children

regular:543.name: Puchero Bogotano
regular:543.desc: Cooked meat, vegetables, chickpeas and potatoes in broth, cooked from the capital.
hints: Bogota adopted this 19th century Spanish immigrants stew
Bring beef, chicken, chorizo and longaniza in one broth
Savannah vegetables — papa, cob, carrot — give sweet broth
It is served in two times just like the cooked Madrid Spanish
Market Day in Paloquemao in Bogotá is served early

regular:544.name: Sopa de Pasta Colombiana
regular:544.desc: Chicken broth with noodles, potato, peas and cilantro, the most homemade soup in the country.
hints: Noodles or pasta are cooked directly in the chicken broth
The small yellow creole potato gives the thickness to the broth
The fresh coriander is added right out of the fire
It's the most cooked midweek soup in every household in the country
It is eaten in all regions with small variations of ingredients

regular:545.name: Mondongo Colombiano
regular:545.desc: Soup of beef corns with potato, yucca, onion, tomato and hogao, Sunday dish.
hints: The calluses are cleaned very well before cooking for hours
Tomato and onion hogao is the aromatic base of broth
The cassava gives it the consistency and body that makes it so heavy
It is the most appreciated Sunday dish in Antioquia and coffee axis
Medellín has specialized restaurants only in mondongo from early

regular:546.name: Sancocho de Bagre
regular:546.desc: Bagre soup—river fish—with cassava, banana and cilantro, typical of Colombian rivers.
hints: Catfish is the most consumed freshwater fish in the country's rivers
The fish is cleaned well so as not to leave the muddy taste of the river
The cassava and the green banana are the food that gives the body
The fresh cilantro gives the aroma that balances the strong flavor of the catfish
The Magdalena and Cauca are the rivers that produce the best catfish

regular:547.name: Postre de Natas
regular:547.desc: Cream of cream concentrated milk with sugar and cinnamon, regional dessert Nariño.
hints: Creams are cream that forms on the surface of boiled milk
In Nariño several creams are collected patiently to make dessert
Sugar and cinnamon are the only flavorings of this simple dessert
It's one of the hardest desserts to make for the time it takes
Pasto, the capital of Nariño, serves it in typical restaurants

regular:548.name: Torta de Choclo Colombiana
regular:548.desc: Wet cake of tender corn, peasant cheese and grated coconut, from Valle del Cauca.
hints: The tender corn grated gives you the moisture and natural sweet taste
The salty peasant cheese inside contrasts with the sweetness of corn
The grated coconut adds aroma and tropical texture
Valle del Cauca has the sweetest and best known version of the country
Served in square portions as dessert or snack with coffee

regular:549.name: Tamales Tolimenses
regular:549.desc: Tamales large rice and pork with peas, carrots and egg, wrapped in banana leaf.
hints: They are the largest in Colombia and carry rice instead of corn
The Tolima is the department that claims them as its own
They carry ribs, bacon, chicken and pork all together in the filling
The banana leaf gives them the green aroma that wraps them all day long
Friday is the traditional day to prepare them and eat them sabatinos

regular:550.name: Arroz con Frijoles Costeño
regular:550.desc: Rice cooked along with red beans, grated coconut and spices from the Caribbean coast.
hints: Coconut milk or grated coconut gives you the coastal tropical flavor
The red beans are cooked first and their broth serves for rice
The Colombian Caribbean coast is where this festive rice is consumed the most
sofrito onion, garlic and tomato is the base before rice
It is the rice that accompanies fried fish in coastal seafood

regular:551.name: Caldo de Patas Colombiano
regular:551.desc: Gelatinous beef-footed broth with potato, corn and cilantro, an antioqueño restorative.
hints: The leg of beef is cooked for hours until the broth gels
Corn in grains and potatoes give the body to the thick broth
The fresh cilantro and the colored aji are added when serving hot
Antioquia consumes it as breakfast in the markets from very early
They say broth gelatin is good for joints and bones

regular:552.name: Insulso Colombiano
regular:552.desc: Dessert of corn cooked in milk with sugar and cinnamon, without dyes or added flavors.
hints: The name means insipid, although it is actually soft and delicate
Maize is ground thick to remain with semolina texture
Cinnamon sliced is cooked with corn and milk together
It is the purest and simplest dessert of traditional cuisine in the country
Hot served on cold nights in the Colombian Andes

regular:553.name: Pepitoria de Gallina Colombiana
regular:553.desc: Chicken stew with ground pumpkin cucumbers, potato and Andean spices.
hints: The cucumbers of the toasted and ground pumpkin thicken the sauce
The patio hen cooks for hours to release all the flavor
It is a dish of buoyan and native peasant cuisine
Andean spices like cumin and achiote give it color
It is different from Spanish pepitoria in its American ingredients

regular:554.name: Mamona de los Llanos
regular:554.desc: Young calf roasted in a rod to wood fire for hours on the eastern plains.
hints: Mamone is beef under one year of age raised in pasture
Tears into wooden sticks around a wood fire
The eastern plains—Meta and Casanare—are their natural territory
It is the festive dish of herd farmers of the Llanera tradition
Served with cooked cassava and hot pepper on the side

regular:555.name: Pisca Andina Venezolana
regular:555.desc: Andean milk soup with potato, cilantro, white cheese and poached egg from the Venezuelan moor.
hints: Milk is the main liquid base instead of water or broth
The Venezuelan Andean moor — Mérida and Táchira — is its historic cradle
The white cheese crumbles on top of the hot plate
The egg is poached directly into the hot soup when serving
It's the breakfast and dinner plus food in the Andes moor

regular:556.name: Arroz con Queso Venezolano
regular:556.desc: Rice cooked with melted white cheese and criollo dressing, typical Venezuelan accompaniment.
hints: Venezuelan white cheese is undone inside hot rice
The sweet and cilantro ají criollo dressing gives you the unmistakable taste
It is the simplest accompaniment of Venezuelan Creole dishes
The eastern plains consume it as a garrison in all meals
The cheese is added when the heat is put out so that it melts with residual heat

regular:557.name: Majarete Venezolano
regular:557.desc: Creamy dessert of tender corn grated with coconut milk, sugar and cinnamon.
hints: The tender corn is grated raw and mixed with coconut milk
Cinnamon powder is generously sprinkled above when serving
It is a dessert of Venezuelan Afro-Criolla cuisine of the 19th century
Refrigerate until firm before serving in paintings
Caracas and the Venezuelan coast consume it at parties and meetings

regular:558.name: Torta de Plátano Venezolana
regular:558.desc: Mature banana moist cake with brown sugar and grated white cheese on top.
hints: The very ripe crushed banana substitutes part of the flour
The salted white grated cheese contrasts with the sweetness of the banana
It is the dessert that most prepares in Venezuelan homes daily
Bake in square mold and cut into tables to serve
Cinnamon and vanilla are the aromas that complete the cake

regular:559.name: Caraotas con Papelón
regular:559.desc: Black beans cooked with paper —panel—, onion and onoto, the most Venezuelan accompaniment.
hints: The paper gives them the dark sweetness that differentiates them from other beans
The onoto — achiote — gives them the orange tone and the earthy taste
Creamy, without much broth, served on white rice
They are the base of the Venezuelan Creole pavilion, the national dish
Each arepera has its secret recipe of caraota that makes it special

regular:560.name: Pelao Guayanés
regular:560.desc: Rice with chicken and cachapa corn, typical dish of Venezuelan Guiana.
hints: Guiana to the southeast is the least known but most authentic region
The chicken is cooked with rice in a single large iron pot
The cachapa tender corn is served next door as an accompaniment
Sweet pepper and cilantro are the aromatics that never lack
Ciudad Bolívar and Puerto Ordaz have the best versions of the dish

regular:561.name: Hallaquitas de Maíz
regular:561.desc: Small tamales unfilled corn dough, boiled and served with cheese or butter.
hints: They are the small, unfilled version of the hallaca Christmas
The dough is made with precooked corn flour and salt
Wrapped in banana leaf and boiled for half an hour
Served as a companion bread of sancocho or boiled
They are the fastest breakfast of Venezuelan homes in the interior

regular:562.name: Guasacaca Venezolana
regular:562.desc: Green avocado sauce, cilantro, green pepper and vinegar, the Venezuelan chimichurri.
hints: It differs from the guacamole in which it carries vinegar and abundant coriander
It is blended to be completely liquid, not thick as guacamole
It is the salsa that accompanies roasting and arepas in Venezuela
Sweet green pepper gives you the taste that differs from other avocado sauces
Can be stored in the refrigerator for up to three days without rusting

regular:563.name: Bollito de Masa
regular:563.desc: Small ball of corn mass cooked in sancocho or boiled Venezuelan.
hints: The precooked corn dough is kneaded with salt and formed in small ball
It is added directly to the sancocho boiling during the last minutes
Absorb the flavor of broth and stay firm on the outside and soft inside
It is the ingredient that children expect most in the sancocho family
Venezuelan plains use it instead of the potato in some recipes

regular:564.name: Chicha Venezolana
regular:564.desc: Thick rice drink with condensed milk, sugar and cinnamon, Venezuelan cold drink.
hints: Unlike the Andean chicks, this one is not fermented and is very sweet
The rice is completely blended with milk to make it creamy
Cinnamon and vanilla are the main aromas of this chicha
It is served very cold with ice in large glasses in any season
It's different from the chicha Peruvian Jora or the chicha Bolivian corn

regular:565.name: Tequenos al Horno
regular:565.desc: Baked version of the traditional, lighter teak with the golden dough in the oven.
hints: Bake instead of frying for a lighter and healthier version
The puffy dough is also rolled on hard white cheese
They brown in the oven at high temperature the last few minutes
They are the favorite choice at adult parties that prefer less oil
The cheese must melt inside as in the fried version

regular:566.name: Sancocho de Pollo Venezolano
regular:566.desc: Chicken broth with cassava, green banana, potato and criollo dressing, the Sunday family dish.
hints: Creole dressing — sweet pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro — is the basis of the taste
Yucca, green banana and potato are added in cooking step
The chicken is added whole or in prey at the beginning of cooking
It is the most cooked dish on Sundays in Venezuelan families
Serves well hot with avocado and repeaters to the side always

regular:567.name: Puré de Plátano Venezolano
regular:567.desc: Green banana cooked and crushed with butter and white cheese, garnish.
hints: The well-cooked green banana is crushed with wooden fork or maja
Butter gives creaminess and white cheese the salty flavor
It's different from the mofongo Caribbean in which it doesn't fry before
The Venezuelan plains consume it as a garnish of roasted meat
Hot served directly from the wood stove in the field

regular:568.name: Quesillo Venezolano
regular:568.desc: Milk flan condensed with eggs, vanilla and caramel, the most beloved Venezuelan dessert.
hints: Condensed milk gives you sweetness and creaminess without adding sugar
Bake in a Maria bath to make it soft and without air bubbles
The caramel is made first in the mold before adding the mixture
The more porous texture that the European flan gives it the name of quesillo
It melts cold and is served with caramel falling on the flan

regular:569.name: Pasticho de Pollo Venezolano
regular:569.desc: Venezuelan lasagna with chicken torn in white sauce, cheese and tomato, lighter version.
hints: Made with chicken instead of ground meat for a smoother version
The abundant bechamel among the layers of pasta is the Venezuelan firm
The yellow cheese gratin on top is the essential finish
It is the most popular version in festive family reunions
It differs from the classic pasticho only by replacing meat with chicken

regular:570.name: Arroz con Pollo Criollo Venezolano
regular:570.desc: Rice cooked with pieces of chicken, olives, capers and criollo dressing in a single pot.
hints: Everything is cooked in the same pot so that rice absorbs the taste of chicken
Creole dressing carries sweet pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro and paprika
The olives and capers give the Venezuelan Mediterranean touch
It is the most cooked celebration dish in the homes of the country
It differs from Colombian in olives and capers included

regular:571.name: Asado Negro Venezolano
regular:571.desc: Round beef caramelized on paper and cooked in dark sauce with spices.
hints: The caramelized paper gives the sauce the intense black color
The meat is completely browned on the paper before adding liquids
It is the star dish of Caraqueña Creole cuisine since the 19th century
Served in slices on white rice with black broth next to it
It is the Christmas dish and important celebrations of Venezuela

regular:572.name: Bobó de Camarão
regular:572.desc: Fresh prawns in mashed cassava with coconut milk and dendê oil, bahian dish.
hints: The cassava is cooked and blended to form a creamy puree as base
The dendê — palm oil— gives it the orange color and African flavor
Shrimp are sautéed separately and added to the hot puree
Bahia is the northeast region where this stew originated
It is one of the most representative dishes of Afro-Babyan cuisine

regular:573.name: Escondidinho de Carne Seca
regular:573.desc: Manioc puree with defiant dried meat hidden under it and gratin cheese on top.
hints: Dried meat is desalted and defiled before being placed on the bottom
The cassava puree—yuca—completely covers the hidden flesh
The coalho or mozzarella cheese is gratina on top in the hot oven
The Brazilian Northeast invented it as a dish of use
It is one of the most popular restaurants in Northeastern cuisine

regular:574.name: Frango com Quiabo
regular:574.desc: Chicken in sauce with quiabo —okra— and turmeric, typical dish of Minas Gerais.
hints: The chiabo —okra — is sliced and fried separately to reduce the drool
The turmeric gives the yellow color and exotic touch to the sauce
Minas Gerais considers it one of its most representative dishes
The chicken is slowly cooked in the broth until it becomes very tender
Served with white rice and farofa manioc on the side always

regular:575.name: Tutu à Mineira
regular:575.desc: Cooked beans thickened with cassava flour and bacon, specialty of Minas.
hints: Manioc flour is added to beans to thicken them a lot
The bacon or fried turret is mixed inside to give smoked flavor
It is the classic accompaniment of mineira food par excellence
It is served along with rice, couve —col— fried and crispy towers
Belo Horizonte is the gastronomic capital where it is best prepared

regular:576.name: Tacacá Paraense
regular:576.desc: Hot tapioca rubber drink with jambu, dry shrimp and chicory pepper, from Pará.
hints: The liquid tapioca rubber gives you the characteristic viscous texture
The jambu is an Amazonian plant that produces a tingling in the mouth
The dry shrimp gives the sea flavor and color to the broth
It is sold at night street stalls in Belém del Pará
Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil formally recognized

regular:577.name: Bolo de Rolo Pernambucano
regular:577.desc: Very fine rolled biscuit with guava paste, specializing in Pernambuco.
hints: The dough is baked in very thin layers that are rolled with jam
The guava is the only filling allowed in the original and certified version
Pernambuco has Geographical Indication for this sweet since 2004
Cut into slices showing the spiral of dough and filling
Recife is the city where more specialized bakeries produce it

regular:578.name: Paçoca de Amendoim
regular:578.desc: Sweet ground peanut solid with sugar and salt, it is undone in the mouth, typical Junino.
hints: Peanut roasts and grinds until it looks like a thick, dry pasta
Sugar and little salt balance the intense taste of peanuts
Pressed in square forms or special moulds
He is the sweet star of June Junina Festas throughout Brazil
São Paulo and the Northeast produce the most famous versions of the country

regular:579.name: Mungunzá
regular:579.desc: Dessert of white corn grains with coconut milk and cinnamon, Northeastern version of the canjica.
hints: White corn — canjica milk — is cooked for hours in water
Coconut milk makes it creamy and gives it the tropical aroma
It differs from the canjica in that it is made with coconut milk
It is the dessert of the Junina Festas in the northeast states
Hot served on June nights during São João festivals

regular:580.name: Cocada Brasileira
regular:580.desc: Sweet handcrafted fresh grated coconut with sugar, in soft or hard version.
hints: The branca version —white— uses condensed milk and is soft and creamy
The hard version cooks longer until completely caramelized
Fresh grated coconut is always the best ingredient to make it
It is sold in beach stalls throughout the Brazilian coast
Bahia produces the most famous cocadas in the country at its popular fairs

regular:581.name: Pé de Moleque
regular:581.desc: Hard caramel of rapadura —cane sugar— with whole peanuts, sweet of popular fair.
hints: Rapadura — unrefined cane sugar — gives it the dark, caramelized taste
The whole roasted peanut is mixed in the hot caramel before solidifying
It is poured into mold and cut into squares when still tender
It is the sweetest fair ever purchased at the Juninas Festas in Brazil
The northeast has been producing it by hand since colonial times

regular:582.name: Sarapatel Nordestino
regular:582.desc: Pork viscera stew with blood, tomato, pepper and spices, African heritage.
hints: Pork viscera include clean liver, lung, and heart
The boiled blood of the thick pig colors the stew in dark red
It is African heritage brought by the slaves of Congo and Angola
Pernambuco and Bahia are the states where it is consumed the most daily
Served with white rice and farofa manioc to absorb the sauce

regular:583.name: Moqueca de Camarão
regular:583.desc: Fresh shrimp in a sauce of coconut milk, dendê oil, tomato and bell pepper, in the style of Bahia.
hints: It differs from the Baian moqueca in that the protagonist is shrimp
Shrimp are added within the last five minutes to avoid hardening
Coconut milk and dendê are the inseparable aromatic basis
Served with white rice and fish pirão in Salvador de Bahia
It is one of the most popular starters in the country’s restaurants serving food from Bahia.

regular:584.name: Pirão Brasileiro
regular:584.desc: Thick sauce of cassava flour cooked in fish or meat broth.
hints: Manioc flour is poured into the hot broth stirring non-stop
It looks like a thick polenta of color from the broth used
It is the inseparable accompaniment of moqueca and fried peixe
Northeastern and northern Brazil are the ones who consume it the most
Each cook adjusts consistency according to family preference

regular:585.name: Doce de Abóbora
regular:585.desc: Pumpkin compote with grated coconut and cinnamon, sweet artisan from northeastern Brazil.
hints: Pumpkin is cooked with sugar until caramelized and thickened
The grated coconut is added at the end so that it does not melt with heat
The cinnamon powder is sprinkled when served to aromatize the sweet
It is a sweet artisan sold in markets of Pernambuco and Bahia
It is kept several days in the refrigerator without losing texture

regular:586.name: Caldinho de Camarão Brasileiro
regular:586.desc: Thick broth of shrimp blended with coconut, spices and milk, served in a small glass.
hints: Shrimp are partially blended to thicken broth without losing texture
It is served in small glass as an entrance or appetizer before the main course
Coconut milk gives it the tropical creaminess that distinguishes it
It is the most popular seafood appetizer on the beach churrascos
Salvador de Bahia and Rio de Janeiro have it in almost all restaurants

regular:587.name: Encocado de Pescado
regular:587.desc: Fresh fish in coconut sauce with onion, tomato, aji and cilantro, tropical coastal dish.
hints: The fresh grated coconut and its milk are the basis of the thick sauce
The Ecuadorian Pacific coast is its historical region
The fish is added directly into the sauce to absorb the flavor
The cilantro and the ají give tropical freshness to the coastal dish
Served with white rice and patacones for a full meal

regular:588.name: Caldo de Bolas de Verde
regular:588.desc: Chicken broth with green banana balls stuffed with peanuts and pork, festive dish.
hints: The balls are made by pounding green plantain and filling with picadillo
Chicken broth is the base where the balls are cooked
The filling of roasted peanut ground with pork is the most traditional
The Ecuadorian coast consumes it at family parties and gatherings
It is the most laborious and spectacular dish in Ecuadorian coastal cuisine

regular:589.name: Arroz con Menestra
regular:589.desc: White rice with lentil or bean menu and roasted meat, the menu of the coastal day.
hints: Menestra is a lentil or bean stew with onion and tomato refrito
It's the best-selling lunch in Ecuador at noon
Roast meat —res or chicken — is put next to it as protein
Onion, tomato and chili refrito gives the base flavor to the menestra
Guayaquil and the entire Ecuadorian coast consider it their daily dish

regular:590.name: Colada Morada
regular:590.desc: A thick drink of purple corn with blackberry, mortiño and spices, typical of the Day of the Dead.
hints: Andean purple corn gives the intense violet color and flavor
Mortiño—Andean Android—gives you the most characteristic fruit acidity
Drink November 2nd as a tradition of the Day of the Dead
Cinnamon, clove and pepper from Jamaica are its spices
It is accompanied by bread guaguas — decorated bread figurines — always

regular:591.name: Hornado con Mote
regular:591.desc: Whole pork baked in a wood oven with cooked white mote and tomato pickle.
hints: The pork is baked whole for hours in wood or clay oven
The white mote — peeled corn cooked — is the inseparable accompaniment
The pig's skin is crisp after so many hours of baking
The markets of the Ecuadorian mountain range sell it in portions since Saturday
Riobamba and Ambato are the most famous cities for baking

regular:592.name: Pristiños Ecuatorianos
regular:592.desc: Fried fritters in the shape of thread bathed in honey panela, Easter dessert.
hints: The dough is made with flour and cheese and forms in argon before frying
Honey is made boiling panela with cinnamon, clove and orange
Specifically prepared during Easter Week throughout the mountain range
They are similar to Cuban fritters in shape but with different flavor
Served hot generously bathed in dark honey panela

regular:593.name: Dulce de Higo
regular:593.desc: Figs in panela syrup with cinnamon and clove, handmade dessert of the Ecuadorian mountain range.
hints: Green figs are cut and bleached before cooking in the syrup
The panela — unrefined cane sugar — gives the syrup the dark color
Cinnamon and clove aromatize the syrup throughout cooking
Served with fresh cheese for the classic sweet-salted contrast
It is the most traditional dessert of the fairs and festivals of mountain villages

regular:594.name: Helados de Paila
regular:594.desc: Handcrafted ice cream beaten in bronze paila on ice and salt, with natural fruit flavors.
hints: The bronze paila is placed on an ice bed and thick salt
Fruit juice is beaten with circular movements until frozen
Ibarra, in the north, is the most famous city for these artisanal ice creams
The most popular flavors are blackberry, taxo, naranjilla and tamarind
The process is 100% manual and without electricity, just like two centuries ago

regular:595.name: Pan de Yuca Ecuatoriano
regular:595.desc: Spongey bread of yucca starch and cheese, baked to brown, without natural gluten.
hints: Yucca starch gives you the elastic and gluten-free texture
Fresh grated cheese is mixed directly into the dry dough
Bake until the bark browns and the inside is hot
They are similar to the Brazilian cheese pão but with more cheese
They are served hot as breakfast or snack with coffee or purple laundry

regular:596.name: Chaulafán Ecuatoriano
regular:596.desc: Ecuadorian fried Chinese style rice with chicken, egg, chives and soy.
hints: It is the Ecuadorian version of Chinese fried rice adapted to local taste
Chicken, egg and chives are the essential ingredients
Soya gives the golden color and umami flavor to fried rice
Chinese communities arrived in Ecuador in the 19th century with this technique
Guayaquil has the chicas restaurants where it is consumed the most

regular:597.name: Mote Sucio
regular:597.desc: Maize mote white sautéed in the fat of chicharrón with onion and garlic, garnish sawdust.
hints: The fat of the chicharrón is what gives it the dark color and flavor
The mote is mixed in the frying pan with fat to absorb all the flavor
It is the most powerful garrison of the markets of the Sierra
Served next to baking and frying as a classic companion
The dirty name comes from the dark color that gives it pork fat

regular:598.name: Caldo de Gallina Ecuatoriano
regular:598.desc: Creole chicken broth with thick noodles, potato, cilantro and table aji.
hints: The Creole hen of the countryside gives the most concentrated and tasty broth
The thick noodles are cooked in the broth to absorb all the flavor
Spicy table aji is always served separately for everyone
It's the soup you eat on the markets since seven in the morning
Quito and the Andean cities serve it as a weekend breakfast

regular:599.name: Espumillas Ecuatorianas
regular:599.desc: Meringue guava smoothie or naranjilla rosette-shaped, Ecuadorian street candy.
hints: The guava cooked and laundry is beaten with egg white until foaming
Formed with spiral spoon over cones of crispy wafers
The guava foams are the most traditional and popular
Quito has been selling them at Ejido Park stalls for decades
It's the most nostalgic street candy for adult Quitos

regular:600.name: Seco de Carne Ecuatoriano
regular:600.desc: Steak stew in black beer sauce, tomato, onion, cumin and naranjilla.
hints: Black beer gives the bitter and caramelized flavor to the sauce
naranjilla — lulo — provides characteristic tropical citrus acidity
Served with white rice, beans and sliced avocado next door
It is the most requested dry in restaurants of the Ecuadorian mountains
It differs from seco de pollo by being darker and more res

regular:601.name: Arroz con Camarones Ecuatoriano
regular:601.desc: Creamy shrimp rice with onion refrito, pepper and coconut milk.
hints: Ecuadorian shrimps in the Gulf of Guayaquil are the largest in the world
Coconut milk gives you the creaminess and tropical coastal flavor
Refreshed onion pearl, pepper and tomato is the aromatic base
Served as a main dish in coastal seafood restaurants
Guayaquil and the entire coast produce the best shrimp on the continent

regular:602.name: Kak'ik
regular:602.desc: Chick-chomp —pavo — ritual broth with copper pepper, achiote and Maya herbs from Alta Verapaz.
