hints: The choppe—pavo—is the sacred bird of Maya q'eqchi culture
Cobanero pepper gives it the unique spicy and smoked flavor of this broth
Cobán, in Alta Verapaz, is the Mayan city where it originated centuries ago
The achiote gives the intense red color and earthy flavor to broth
Intangible Cultural Heritage of Guatemala officially recognized

regular:603.name: Fiambre Guatemalteco
regular:603.desc: Cold salad of meats, sausages, vegetables and pickled cheese, Day of the Dead dish.
hints: Only November 1st is prepared for All Saints Day
It has more than fifty different ingredients in a single salad
Guatemalan families have their secret recipe from generation to generation
There are white — no betabel — and red — versions of the same dish with betabel
It is the most laborious dish in Guatemalan cuisine that exists

regular:604.name: Hilachas Guatemaltecas
regular:604.desc: Chile and papa, Guatemalan ladino stew.
hints: The meat is boiled until it can melt completely with its hands
The tomato sauce with chili guajillo gives the red color to the stew
The cubed potatoes are added in the last twenty minutes of cooking
It is the most representative Ladin stew of Guatemalan daily cuisine
Guatemala City serves it in the popular dining rooms of the market

regular:605.name: Cocido Guatemalteco
regular:605.desc: Soup of beef with local vegetables—güisquil, yucca, ejotes—and weeds, dominguero dish.
hints: Güisquil — chayote — and cassava are the most characteristic vegetables
Fresh mint gives you the green scent that sets it apart
Served with freshly made corn tortillas in hot griddle
It is the dish of family Sundays throughout Guatemala
Each region has its own vegetables according to the local season

regular:606.name: Pollo en Crema Guatemalteco
regular:606.desc: Chicken dams in milk cream sauce with pepper chili and parrot, popular homemade dish.
hints: The parrot — edible flower— gives it the scent that sets it apart
The cream of milk thickens the sauce until it becomes very unctuous
Roast pepper chili brings the smoky and sweet flavor
It is the most cooked dish in Guatemalan homes in the urban area
Served with rice and corn tortillas for Sunday lunch

regular:607.name: Tamalitos de Chipilín
regular:607.desc: Tamales corn dough with chiplin — weed — and cheese, wrapped in cob leaf.
hints: The chipillin is an edible plant with a very nutritious small leaf
The dough is dyed green with the chipilin ground inside
Fresh cheese is placed in the center of the dough before wrapping
They are smaller than the tamales holidays and easier to prepare
They are eaten as breakfast or snack throughout the central region of the country

regular:608.name: Chuchitos Guatemaltecos
regular:608.desc: Tamales small corn stuffed with meat in red, wrapped in a tusa leaf.
hints: The tusa leaf is the dry leaf of the corn cob
The red errand is a tomato sauce and dried chilies that colors the dough
They are smaller and more frequent than the tamales festive colorings
They are sold in popular markets and canteens like street food
The errand has anato seed — achiote — and dried tomato

regular:609.name: Pulique Guatemalteco
regular:609.desc: Thick chicken or beef stew with corn, tomato and chili dough from the indigenous communities.
hints: The corn dough dissolves in the broth and thickens the sauce naturally
Tomato and chili are roasted first before being ground for the sauce
It is a stew of pre-Columbian origin that is still prepared in the communities
The western region — Quetzaltenango, Huehuetenango — preserves it better
Served at weddings and important celebrations of the Mayan peoples

regular:610.name: Espesado Guatemalteco
regular:610.desc: Thick stew of white beans with ejotes, chipsillines and beef, from the east of the country.
hints: White beans — beans — cook until they are undone in the stock
The chipilin provides green and vegetable protein to the thick stew
The green beans are added at the end so that they do not melt
The eastern part of Guatemala, especially Zacapa, is its region of origin
It is a dish that balances legume, vegetables and meat in one pot

regular:611.name: Atol de Maíz Guatemalteco
regular:611.desc: A thick hot drink of corn dough with milk, sugar and cinnamon, the Guatemalan atole.
hints: The dough of corn dissolved in water and milk is the thickening base
Cinnamon in slice and sugar give you sweetness and aroma
Hot sale in street stalls on cold mornings
It's the drink that accompanies the tamales at parties and fairs
It is different from the guava or strawberry atole in its pure corn flavor

regular:612.name: Garnachas Orientales
regular:612.desc: Fried tortillas with beans, stewed meat and pickled salad, oriental popular snack.
hints: The eastern garnachas are different from those of the capital in mass
The stewed and shredded beef is put on top of the beans
The pickle of cabbage and carrot gives you refreshing acidity
Zacapa and Chiquimula are the cities where they best prepare
Eating in the afternoon as a snack before main dinner

regular:613.name: Sopa de Pan Cobanera
regular:613.desc: Cobán holiday soup with French bread, chicken broth, vegetables, capers and raisins.
hints: Cobán, in the northern verapaces, is the only place where it is made
Prepares only for the All Saints celebrations in November
French bread soaked in chicken broth gives you the special texture
Capers and raisins give you the salty and sweet contrast together
It is one of the most unknown and unique dishes in all Guatemala

regular:614.name: Subanik Guatemalteco
regular:614.desc: Mayan stew of meats in dried chili sauce and tomato, wrapped in maxan leaf.
hints: Wrapped in maxan leaf or plantain for steaming
Bring a mixture of meats: pork, beef and chicken together in the stew
Roasted dried chilies form a dark and complex sauce
It is a ceremonial dish of the Tz'utujil villages of Lake Atitlán
The name means 'asar' in the Mayan tz'utujil language of the lake

regular:615.name: Gandinga Puertorriqueña
regular:615.desc: Liver, heart and pig kidney stew in boricua creole sauce with olives.
hints: The ganginga are the viscera of the pig — liver, heart and kidney —
The sofrito boricua with caroo and sweet pepper is the base of the stew
Olives and capers give the Caribbean salty touch
It is a very valued dish in the rural municipalities of the island
Served with white rice and toast as a classic accompaniment

regular:616.name: Alcapurrias de Yuca
regular:616.desc: Oval croquettes of yucca and green guineo stuffed with ground meat, fried in oil.
hints: The dough mixes yucca and green guineo — banana — grated together
Ground meat with sofrito boricua is the most classic filling
They fry until they are golden and crispy on the outside
They are the most popular fritre of Luquillo kiosks and beaches
The achiote in the oil gives it the characteristic orange color

regular:617.name: Bacalaítos Fritos
regular:617.desc: Fried cod cakes, sauced with flour, garlic and parsley, beach appetizer.
hints: The desalado cod is crushed in the flour dough with garlic
The dough is fine to cool until it becomes very crispy
They are the best-selling aperitif in the kiosks of the beaches of the island
They eat freshly fried hot with lemon squeezed on top
Garlic and parsley are the aromatics that give them the distinctive taste

regular:618.name: Surullitos de Maíz
regular:618.desc: Crispy fried popcorn flour with cheese, popular boricua appetizer.
hints: Precooked corn flour is mixed with cheese to make the dough
Form in thin cylindrical sticks before frying
They are the most typical aperitif of the Puerto Rican fritures in the kiosks
Hot served with garlic sauce or mayoketchup next door
Its crunchy texture on the outside and soft inside makes them irresistible

regular:619.name: Rellenos de Papa Boricua
regular:619.desc: Potato puree balls stuffed with ground meat with sofrito, fried and golden.
hints: The mashed potato is mixed with egg and cornstarch to keep it firm
The ground meat with sofrito boricua and olives is the classic filling
Fry in hot oil until golden on the outside
They are one of the most popular dishes in Puerto Rican families
Hot served with mayoketchup — mayonnaise and ketchup mix —

regular:620.name: Empanadillas de Guayaba
regular:620.desc: Fried pastries of crispy dough stuffed with sweet guava paste.
hints: The pasta guava is the most popular sweet filling in Puerto Rico
The dough closes with a fork forming the characteristic pattern
They fry until golden brown and sprinkle with icing sugar
They are the sweetest-selling bakery and coffee shop on the island
They are also stuffed with cream cheese or guava and cheese together

regular:621.name: Majarete Puertorriqueño
regular:621.desc: Dessert of tender corn with coconut milk, sugar and cinnamon, boricua version of the majarete.
hints: The tender corn is ground with coconut milk for the creamy base
Cinnamon is the spice that most aromatizes it with vanilla
It is a dessert of the Afro-Caribbean cuisine very ancient
Refrigerated in squares and sprinkled with cinnamon when serving
It is different from the Venezuelan majarete in the proportion of ingredients

regular:622.name: Dulce de Lechoza
regular:622.desc: Papaya — owl — green cooked in sugar syrup with cloves and cinnamon, Christmas sweet.
hints: The green piggy is cooked in syrup until translucent
The clove and cinnamon aromatize the syrup throughout cooking
It is one of the most traditional Christmas sweets on the island
Cold served with hand white cheese for salty contrast
The pigock is the boricua name for papaya throughout the Caribbean

regular:623.name: Bienmesabe Boricua
regular:623.desc: Sweet coconut cream, condensed milk, yolks and cinnamon, boricua celebration dessert.
hints: Coconut in milk or grated is the main ingredient and most aromatic
Condensed milk gives you intense sweetness without adding extra sugar
The egg yolks give it creaminess and yellow color
It is different from the Venezuelan bienmesabe in coconut ratio
Cold served on biscuits or cheese as a party dessert

regular:624.name: Sopón de Pollo Puertorriqueño
regular:624.desc: Hard chicken soup with thick noodles, chickpeas, potato and sofrito boricua.
hints: The sofrito with careo and sweet chili gives the unmistakable boricua flavor
The chickpeas give you the protein and texture that make it very forceful
The thick noodles absorb the broth and are very tasty when eating
It is the soup of Sundays and rainy days throughout the island
Grandma is the most authorized person to prepare the best sopon

regular:625.name: Caldo Santo Boricua
regular:625.desc: Cod soup desalted with potato, green plantain and sofrito Easter Boricua.
hints: Prepared exclusively on Good Friday as a religious tradition
Cod desalted 48 hours earlier is the only valid fish
Green banana and potato give the body and consistency to broth
It is the dish most remembered by Puerto Ricans of their religious childhood
Every grandmother has her secret recipe that she doesn't share with anyone

regular:626.name: Chuletas Can Can
regular:626.desc: Pork chops with crispy fried bark until it is carammeladas, dish from Barranquiño.
hints: Barranquitas, in the mountainous center, is the town that invented them
The bark of the pig is crispy like chicharrón on the edges
marinate in adobo boricua with garlic, oregano and vinegar before frying
They eat in the Creole restaurants of the interior of the island
The name can can comes from ballerina skirts by sponged bark

regular:627.name: Tembleque Boricua
regular:627.desc: Coconut milk flan with cornstarch, sugar and cinnamon, served cold with cinnamon powder.
hints: It is made only with coconut milk, cornstarch, sugar and cinnamon
The name comes from the tremor made by gelatin when moving it
It is the most traditional holiday and Christmas dessert on the island
Refrigerate several hours before demolishing on the plate
It is gluten-free naturally and suitable for many special diets

regular:628.name: Pionono Puertorriqueño
regular:628.desc: Fried ripe banana roll stuffed with ground meat with sofrito, fried and baked.
hints: The ripe banana is flattened in strips before rolling with the filling
Ground meat with sofrito boricua is the most traditional filling
Fry first and then bake briefly to caramelize the banana
It is the most popular appetizer in Puerto Rican parties everywhere
It is always accompanied with ketchup — tomato sauce— in Puerto Rico

regular:629.name: Fricasé Paceño
regular:629.desc: Thick pork soup with mote, chuño and ají amarillo, Sunday breakfast in La Paz.
hints: The fresh ají amarillo gives the taste and golden color to the broth
The pig is cooked in pieces with bone to give more flavor to the broth
The corn mote and the frozen chuño are inseparable companions
La Paz serves it exclusively on Sunday mornings
Considered the best remedy to recover from Saturday night

regular:630.name: Lagua de Maíz
regular:630.desc: Thick corn soup ground with potato, cheese and Andean spices from the Bolivian highlands.
hints: The corn is ground thick and cooked in broth to thicken the liquid
Cooked potato and fresh cheese are added almost at the end
Cumin and oregano are the spices that most aromatize it
It is the most comforting soup of cold nights in the highlands
Oruro and Potosí are the most consumed cities on a daily basis

regular:631.name: Ají de Papalisa
regular:631.desc: Papalisas stew — Andean tuber— with chicken, ají amarillo and toasted peanuts.
hints: Papalisa —ulluco — is a very nutritious yellow Andean tuber
The ají amarillo gives the color and flavor that defines the stew
The roasted peanut ground thicken the sauce and gives the flavor to nut
It is a dish of pre-Columbian cuisine that keeps alive in Bolivia
Sucre and Cochabamba have the most documented and old versions

regular:632.name: Humintas Bolivianas
regular:632.desc: Mass of choclo tender with cheese and cinnamon, wrapped in steamed corn leaf, sweet version.
hints: The choclo tender is grated raw to make the dough moist and sweet
Cinnamon and cheese are incorporated into the ground dough
Wrapped in corn leaves and steamed for one hour
They are the Bolivian version of the humitas or tamales Andean sweets
They differ from salty ones in bringing sugar and cinnamon inside

regular:633.name: Cuñapé Boliviano
regular:633.desc: Juice and cheese starch muffin, gluten-free, typical of Santa Cruz de la Sierra.
hints: The cassava starch gives the natural elastic texture to the muffin
Fresh cheese is mixed directly in the dry dough
They bake until brown and the inside is very fluffy
They are similar to the Brazilian queijo pão for their ingredients
Santa Cruz de la Sierra sells them in bakeries and markets early on

regular:634.name: Api con Buñuelos
regular:634.desc: Hot drink of purple corn with fried cheese fritters, traditional Bolivian breakfast.
hints: The purple api is served next to the freshly fried fritters
The fritters bring fresh cheese in the dough before frying
The sweet combination of the api and the salty fritter is the pleasure of the dish
The markets and fairs of Bolivia sell them together from 6 in the morning
La Paz and Cochabamba have the most famous stalls in this combination

regular:635.name: Chaque de Maíz
regular:635.desc: Crocante corn soup fried with meat, potato and chuño, dish of the north high plateau.
hints: Maize is roasted or fried first until crispy before soup
The beef with bone gives you the bottom of the broth concentrate
The chuño – dehydrated andine papa – is a typically Bolivian ingredient
The north of the Bolivian highlands, near Lake Titicaca, consumes it more
It is a very nutritious and strong soup for the cold of the highlands

regular:636.name: Enrollado de Cerdo Boliviano
regular:636.desc: Pernil pork rolled with spices and vegetables, cooked and served cold in slices.
hints: The pernil is seasoned with chili, cumin and garlic before rolling
It is bound with thread and cooked in water with vegetables for hours
Serves cold in thin slices as party meat and roasts
Cochabamba has the most famous rollers in the whole country
It is the most prepared festive lunch for Bolivian celebrations

regular:637.name: Buñuelos Bolivianos
regular:637.desc: Fries of dough and cheese, bathed in cane honey, festive Christmas dessert.
hints: The flour dough with fresh cheese is formed in argolla before frying
Hot cane honey pours over the fritters by taking them out of oil
It's New Year's dessert and the Christmas religious holidays
Bolivia consumes them next to the hot purple api as is tradition
Different from Colombians in consistency and size

regular:638.name: Mocochinchi
regular:638.desc: Cold drink of dehydrated peach soaked in water with cinnamon and sugar.
hints: Dry peach is hydrated in cold water for several hours or one night
Cinnamon sliced is added to the water to aromatize the whole drink
It is Bolivia's most popular refreshing street drink in summer
The markets of Cochabamba and La Paz sell it in large jars
The pink color of the water comes from naturally rehydrated peach

regular:639.name: Chicharrón de Cerdo Boliviano
regular:639.desc: Fried pork in its own fat until golden and crispy, with mote.
hints: The pig fryes slowly in its own fat without extra oil
Cochabamba is the most famous city for its pork chipper
Always served with white mote and tomato salad with onion
The pig's skin is very crispy by prolonged cooking
Sundays at noon is the classic time to eat it as a family

regular:640.name: Sopa de Quinua Boliviana
regular:640.desc: Chicken broth with white quinoa, potato, chuño and puna Andean vegetables.
hints: Quinoa is the Andean superfood grown since Inca times
The chuño — dehydrated dad — gives the earthy taste so Andean
The puna—altiplano over 3800 meters—is where quinoa is grown
It is the most nutritious and energetic soup of the entire Bolivian Andean diet
Bolivia produces 40% of all quinoa consumed in the world

regular:641.name: Asopao Dominicano
regular:641.desc: Broth rice with chicken or seafood, sofrito Dominican and spices, party dish.
hints: It's hotter than normal rice, almost like a thick soup
The sofrito Dominican aji cubanela and cilantro is the aromatic base
It is served very hot as a party dish in celebrations
It can be chicken, shrimp or a mixture of varied seafood
Santo Domingo and Santiago have the best restaurants that serve it

regular:642.name: Chivo Guisado Dominicano
regular:642.desc: Chived meat in tomato creole sauce, pepper and spices, country holiday dish.
hints: The goat is the most festive and cherished meat in the country
The sofrito Dominican gives the color and Caribbean aroma to the salsa
Let the meat macerate with garlic, oregano and vinegar before cooking
The northwest of the country, especially Azua, is famous for this dish
Served at parties and celebrations as a main dish

regular:643.name: Bistec Encebollado Dominicano
regular:643.desc: Beef steak with abundant caramelized onion and creole sauce, midday dish.
hints: The onion is simmering slowly until completely caramelized
Criolla tomato and chili sauce cubenela complements the sweet onion
It is the most consumed lunch dish in Dominican households
Served on white rice with beans and fresh salad
The meat should be juicy and tender, not well cooked and dried

regular:644.name: Pasteles en Hoja Dominicanos
regular:644.desc: Mass of green banana and yucca with pork, wrapped in steamed banana leaf.
hints: The dough mixes grated green plantain with grated yucca
Pig in pieces with sofrito creole is the most traditional filling
They are wrapped in banana leaf and steamed for one hour
They are the Dominican equivalent of tamales other countries
Prepare for Christmas and New Year as an annual family tradition

regular:645.name: Jalao Dominicano
regular:645.desc: Sweet handcrafted coconut grated with honey bee or ball paper, Christmas dessert.
hints: The grated coconut is cooked with honey or paper until very dense
It forms into small balls while still hot and manageable
Preserved days without cooling for sugar that hardens it
It is the most artisanal and ancient Christmas sweet in Dominican cuisine
It is sold in squares and markets wrapped in transparent paper

regular:646.name: Majarete Dominicano
regular:646.desc: Thick dessert of corn and coconut with cinnamon and sugar, served cold in pictures.
hints: Ground corn and coconut milk are the two bases of dessert
The powdered cinnamon on top is the infallible finish
Refrigerate in a mold until firm before cutting into squares
It is the easiest and most economical Dominican dessert to make
Each Dominican home has its slightly different recipe for generations

regular:647.name: Arroz con Dulce Dominicano
regular:647.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with sugar, cinnamon, raisins and ginger, festive dessert.
hints: Coconut milk replaces cow's milk in rice cooking
The fresh grated ginger gives you the special touch that sets it apart
The raisins are added to give extra texture and natural sweetness
It is the most consumed Dominican Easter dessert in the country
Cold served with powdered cinnamon generously sprinkled on top

regular:648.name: Morir Soñando Dominicano
regular:648.desc: Drink of orange juice mixed with evaporated milk and sugar, served very cold.
hints: The mixture of acidic juice with milk is the secret that gives it cream color
It should be mixed very quickly so that the milk is not cut
It is the most refreshing and characteristic drink of Dominican cuisine
It is served very cold with ice for Caribbean hot days
The name says that with so much flavor they want to die dreaming when drinking it

regular:649.name: Quipes Dominicanos
regular:649.desc: Croquettes of ground meat with bulgur wheat and mint, the island's Arab quibe.
hints: They came with 19th-century Lebanese and Syrian Arab immigration
Fine bulgur wheat is mixed with raw ground beef
The minty fresh chopped gives it the Arab aroma that differentiates them
They are the most popular fry in Dominican celebrations and festivals
They eat cold or hot with chili pepper sauce next door

regular:650.name: Habichuelas con Dulce Dominicanas
regular:650.desc: Sweet cream of red beans with coconut milk, raisins and sweet potatoes, Easter dessert.
hints: It is the only vegetable dessert in the world — beans are cooked sweets —
It is eaten exclusively during Holy Week by religious tradition
Sweet potatoes — sweet potatoes — give you the sweetness and soft texture at the end
Coconut milk makes the cream very aromatic and tropical to the palate
Dominicans share it with neighbors door to door on Easter

regular:651.name: Pernil Dominicano
regular:651.desc: Pernil pork marinated in Creole season, sour orange and garlic, roasted in oven.
hints: Sour orange gives you the acidity that penetrates the meat when marinating
Dominican Creole Season Is Different From Other Caribbean Countries
It marinates at least 24 hours before for the flavor to penetrate well
It is the most cooked Christmas Eve and New Year dish in the country
The crispy skin —curito— is the most contested part in serving

regular:652.name: Morcilla Dulce Uruguaya
regular:652.desc: Pork blood sausage with raisins, nuts and sugar, sweet variant rioplatense.
hints: The Uruguayan sweet pudding is a rarity in the world of sausages
It carries raisins and nuts inside the spicy blood
Roast on the grill just like classic salty sausage
Uruguay is the only country where this sweet version is so popular
It is eaten in the roast on Sunday next to the other barbecue achuras

regular:653.name: Ojo de Bife Uruguayo
regular:653.desc: Cut of fine loin of roasted beef to the embers, one of the most valued in the country.
hints: The beef eye is the high back, the leanest and premium cut
Uruguay produces it with high quality natural pasture cattle
Thick salt is the only seasoning that needs this luxury cut
Served mid-point —juice— to appreciate texture and flavor
Montevideo has specialized parrillaros who dominate this court

regular:654.name: Chivito al Plato
regular:654.desc: A dish version of the goat with loin, ham, egg, cheese, salad and fries.
hints: It's the little guy served on a plate instead of a sandwich
Bring the same ingredients but without bread, with fries
It's more abundant and you eat with cutlery, not hands
Montevideo’s restaurants serve it as a main dish
It is the version for those who prefer less carbohydrates of bread

regular:655.name: Chajá Uruguayo
regular:655.desc: Dessert of cake, cream of milk, meringue and peaches in syrup, from Paysandú.
hints: Paysandú, northwest of the country, is the city that invented this dessert
Soft biscuit and whipped cream are the main layers
Peaches in syrup provide moisture and fruity sweetness
The crispy dry meringue contrasts with the moist cream inside
It is the most exported dessert from Uruguay to the rest of South America

regular:656.name: Alfajores Montevideanos
regular:656.desc: Alfajores of tender dough stuffed with sweet milk and bathed in bitter chocolate.
hints: Uruguay and Argentina dispute the invention of this classic sweet
The corn starch dough is tenderer and more delicate than Argentina’s
The rioplatense milk candy is the filling that binds the two lids
The black chocolate cover gives you the bitter touch that balances
They are the best selling souvenir in Montevideo for tourists who visit

regular:657.name: Garrapiñada Uruguaya
regular:657.desc: Caramelized toasted peanuts with sugar and cinnamon, very popular street candy.
hints: Peanut is roasted in a skillet with sugar and water until caramelized
The sprinkled cinnamon at the end gives it the scent that distinguishes it
It is sold in paper cones in the plazas and ramblas of Montevideo
The crunching of peanuts with hard candy is its main feature
It is the most economical and popular street candy in urban Uruguay

regular:658.name: Pasta Frola Uruguaya
regular:658.desc: Broken dough cake with quince or guava and lattice on top.
hints: The broken butter dough is partially baked before filling
The quince sweet is the most traditional and classic filling
The grating of strips of dough on top is the visual signature of dessert
Uruguay and Argentina share this cake of Italian origin
It's the most classic mate hour dessert in Rioplatan homes

regular:659.name: Sándwich Olímpico Uruguayo
regular:659.desc: crumb bread sandwich with ham, cheese, tomato and lettuce, classic Montevideano.
hints: The very soft white crumb bread is the bread of Uruguayan sandwiches
It is made with several layers interspersed of ingredients and cut into triangles
Cooked ham and feta cheese are always the main fillings
Montevideo sells them in rotiserías that open at 6 am
They eat at breakfast or snack as an alternative to daily roasting

regular:660.name: Milanesa al Limón Uruguaya
regular:660.desc: Fillet of baked and fried beef, served with plenty of lemon and mixed salad.
hints: The lemon squeezed generously on top is the Uruguayan touch
It differs from Argentina in that it is always served with lemon
Montevideo has rotiserías in every neighborhood specialized in Milanese
The Champignon version carries mushroom sauce on top
It is the most ordered dish in Montevideo homes on Sundays

regular:661.name: Asado a la Cruz Uruguayo
regular:661.desc: Lamb or beef roasted on cross of vertical iron over embers of firewood for hours.
hints: The iron cross holds the flesh vertically in front of fire
The lamb on the stick is the most traditional and festive version of the country
Cooks for 4 to 6 hours without rush, with total patience
Montevideo and the cattle ranching interior have the most deeply rooted culture
The meat only carries thick salt, nothing else is needed in the recipe

regular:662.name: Tapado Olanchano
regular:662.desc: Soup of fish and seafood with coconut, yucca and green banana, from the Honduran Caribbean.
hints: Coconut milk is the basis that gives it the tropical Caribbean flavor
Olancho and the Caribbean coast are the regions where you consume the most
Fresh fish and seafood are added in the last few minutes
The cassava and the green banana give you body and consistency
It is the Honduran version of the English-speaking influence Caribbean rundown

regular:663.name: Enchiladas Hondureñas
regular:663.desc: Corn toast with minced meat, salad, dry cheese and tomato sauce on top.
hints: They are different from Mexican enchiladas in being cold and over toasted
Cooked ground meat is the basis that is put on toast
The grated dry cheese and chopped cabbage are the classic toppings
They are eaten as a snack or fast dinner in the dining rooms and fondas
Homemade tomato sauce is served above when serving

regular:664.name: Tamales de Elote Hondureños
regular:664.desc: Tamales sweets of tender corn with sugar and cheese, wrapped in steamed corn leaf.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the dough sweet and moist
The dried salted cheese inside contrasts with the sweetness of the corn
They are steamed on the leaves of the corn itself for an hour
They're sweeter than the tamales salty dry corn dough
They are sold in markets especially during the season of tender corn

regular:665.name: Sopa de Pescado Hondureña
regular:665.desc: Sea or river fish broth with yucca, banana, sweet chili and cilantro.
hints: The fish is cleaned and added whole or in pieces to the stock
Yucca and green plantain are the most characteristic food
The sweet pepper — a bell pepper— gives the broth sweetness
The fresh cilantro at the end gives it the scent that distinguishes it
Tegucigalpa and coastal ports have the best versions

regular:666.name: Rosquillas Hondureñas
regular:666.desc: Hard corn doughnuts with dry cheese and anise, the most typical sweet bread in the country.
hints: Maize flour with dry cheese is the basis of these doughnuts
The anise gives the most characteristic aroma of this dry sweet
They bake until they are very hard and last many days without getting bad
They are the sweet bread most gifted and sold throughout the country
Each municipality in western Honduras has its own version

regular:667.name: Caldo de Res Hondureño
regular:667.desc: Rib broth with güisquil, yucca, green banana, corn and fresh cilantro.
hints: Güisquil — chayote — and cassava are the most characteristic vegetables
The rib with bone gives the gelatinous base of the comforting broth
The whole sliced corn is added to give the sweet taste
The fresh cilantro at the end gives it the aromatic green touch
It is the most traditional Sunday lunch of Honduran families

regular:668.name: Chanfaina Hondureña
regular:668.desc: Peat stew with potato, tomato and spices, popular dish of the markets.
hints: The beef viscera — liver, slap — are cooked in tomato sauce
It is the economic dish par excellence of popular markets in the country
The cooked potato gives consistency and body to the stew
Cumin and oregano are the spices that most aromatize it
Served as a breakfast or lunch with fresh tortillas

regular:669.name: Atol de Elote Hondureño
regular:669.desc: Hot, thick drink of tender corn with milk, sugar and cinnamon, Honduran snack.
hints: The tender corn is ground and cooked in milk to make the base
Cinnamon and sugar give you the sweetness and warm aroma
It is sold in street stalls on the cold afternoons of the highlands
It is very similar to Guatemalan atol in its ingredients
Honduran markets have it from early to noon

regular:670.name: Catrachitas Hondureñas
regular:670.desc: Toast corn with refried beans, grated dry cheese and on top cabbage and cream.
hints: The cabbage in thin strips and the acidic cream are the classic toppings
The dried cheese hard and very salty is grated on top of the beans
Honduran toast is smaller and rounder than Mexican toast
They are the most popular snack in the markets and stadiums of the country
The name comes from a loving kindness for Hondurans

regular:671.name: Tajadas con Queso Hondureñas
regular:671.desc: Mature banana fried in long slices with melted white cheese and cabbage on top.
hints: Cuts are fried in hot oil until caramelized from the outside
The white cheese is put on the hot slices to melt
The cabbage in thin strips with lemon is put on top at the cool end
It is the most popular garrison of Honduran lunches in the country
It is accompanied with any kind of grilled meat or fried next to it

regular:672.name: Sopa de Caracol Hondureña
regular:672.desc: Creamy sea snail soup with coconut milk, yucca, banana and fresh cilantro.
hints: The Caribbean coast of the country is where this creamy soup originated
Coconut milk gives it the creaminess and tropical flavor that defines it
The spade snail is the mollusc used in the recipe
La Ceiba and Roatan are the best places to prepare
Served with freshly baked coconut bread to accompany

regular:673.name: Plato Típico Hondureño
regular:673.desc: Rice, beans, roasted meat, fried banana, cheese and cream all in one dish.
hints: It is the dish that most represents Honduran daily cuisine
White rice and fried beans are the basic components
Roast beef or chicken provides the main protein
Sweet fried ripe banana and fresh cheese complete the dish
Tegucigalpa and San Pedro Sula serve in all popular dining rooms

regular:674.name: Guacho de Mariscos
regular:674.desc: Cushion rice with varied seafood, cilantro and Panamanian spices, festive sea dish.
hints: Guacho is a very brothy rice, almost between rice and thick soup
The cilantro—a wide coriander—gives it the unmistakable Panamanian aroma
The various seafoods are added in the last minutes of cooking
Panama City and Columbus have the most famous versions of the dish
It is different from rice with seafood because of its more liquid consistency

regular:675.name: Carimañola Panameña
regular:675.desc: Oval croquette of cooked yucca stuffed with ground meat or cheese, fried in oil.
hints: The cooked cassava is kneaded until it becomes moldable dough
The ground meat with sofrito Panamanian is the most classic filling
It forms in oval and frys until golden and crispy
It is the most popular street snack in all of Panama
It is sold in street breakfasts next to pastry and tortillas

regular:676.name: Chicheme Panameño
regular:676.desc: Refreshing drink of tender corn cooked in milk with cinnamon, sugar and vanilla.
hints: Sweet corn — choclo — boils in milk until softened
Cinnamon and vanilla give you the characteristic tropical aroma
It is served cold or hot depending on the season of the year
It is the best-selling craft drink in trade fairs and employers
The Panamanian interior consumes it as a drink of the holidays

regular:677.name: Hojaldras Panameñas
regular:677.desc: Soft, airy fried bread served for breakfast with fresh white cheese or butter.
hints: The flour dough is stretched and fried to inflate like a balloon
It is the most popular Panamanian breakfast bread next to the carimañola
Hot served with melted white cheese or butter on top
Street stalls sell them from 5 a.m. across the country
They are eaten next to black coffee or natural orange juice

regular:678.name: Arroz con Pollo Panameño
regular:678.desc: Rice cooked with chicken, cilantro, peppers and Panamanian spices in a single pot.
hints: The Panamanian cilantro—a wide leaf—gives it the most characteristic aroma
Everything is cooked in the same pot so that rice absorbs the taste
The colored peppers give you the sweet taste and the colorful color
It is the dish of birthdays and popular parties of the country
Panama City serves it in typical food restaurants always

regular:679.name: Pesada de Guandú
regular:679.desc: Guandú beans cooked in coconut milk with sugar and cinnamon, Christmas Panamanian dessert.
hints: Guandú —palo beans—is a popular legume in Panama
Cooked in coconut milk until very tender and creamy
Sugar and cinnamon give you the sweetness and special aroma
It is the most traditional dessert of Panamanian Christmas in the countryside
Penonomé and the interior of the country have the most authentic versions

regular:680.name: Arroz con Coco Panameño
regular:680.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with raisins, sugar and cinnamon, coastal accompaniment.
hints: Coconut milk completely replaces the water in cooking
Sweet raisins give texture and natural sweetness to coastal rice
Cinnamon powder is added at the end to flavour when serving
Jamaican Afro-Antillean influence is evident in Panamanian recipe
Columbus and the Caribbean area are where this rice is consumed the most

regular:681.name: Almojábano Panameño
regular:681.desc: Fried or baked cheese and cassava starch, breakfast typical of the interior.
hints: The cassava starch gives the elastic and gluten-free texture to the bun
Panamanian white cheese blends into the dry dough
You can bake or fry depending on regional preference
Veraguas and Los Santos are the provinces of the interior that consume them most
They are similar to the Bolivian wedge and Brazilian cheese pão

regular:682.name: Sancocho de Mariscos Panameño
regular:682.desc: A variety of seafood soup with yam, yucca, cilantro and spices, marine version of the sancocho.
hints: It's the marine version of the sancocho national seafood chicken
The yam and the yucca give him the body that makes it so strong
The cilantro (broad leafed coriander) is the most Panamanian aroma
Panama City and Columbus are where this sancocho is best prepared
Served in celebrations and holidays of coastal communities

regular:683.name: Sopa de Mondongo Panameña
regular:683.desc: Soup of beef callos with chickpeas, potato, cilantro, aji chombo and Panamanian spices.
hints: The chili chombo gives it the intense and fruity itching that distinguishes it
The cilantro is the most Panamanian aroma that differs from other versions
The chickpeas and the potato make the soup very strong and nutritious
It is especially eaten on weekends as a restorative dish
Panama City and Columbus have the best versions of the country

regular:684.name: Tostones con Salmón Panameño
regular:684.desc: Crispy green banana toast with smoked salmon, cream and capers.
hints: This fusion version was born in modern restaurants in Panama City
Smoked salmon and capers give you international elegance
Toas are the crispy base that holds all the ingredients on top
Panama City has the most diverse fusion cuisine in Central America
The canal and geographical position explain the global gastronomic influence

regular:685.name: Bollo de Yuca Panameño
regular:685.desc: Mass of yucca grated with salt and white cheese cooked in steamed bijao leaf.
hints: The bijao leaf is a tropical plant that wraps and gives flavor
Raw grated cassava forms the dough without having to cook before
White cheese or chicharrón are the most popular fillings
Veraguas and Azuero are the provinces where it is consumed the most
Served as a breakfast or snack in local rural markets

regular:686.name: Nacatamal de Pollo Nicaragüense
regular:686.desc: Tamal large corn dough with chicken, rice, olives and chiltoma, wrapped in banana leaf.
hints: The chicken version is an alternative to the classic nacatamal pork
The dough carries corn dough with butter and broth to make it soft
Chiltoma—sweet pepper—gives it the typical Nicaraguan aroma
Wrapped in banana leaf and boiled for three hours
Saturdays are the traditional day to prepare and eat them on Sunday

regular:687.name: Gallo Pinto Nicaragüense
regular:687.desc: Rice and black beans sautéed together with onion and cilantro, Nicaraguan national breakfast.
hints: Nicaragua and Costa Rica dispute who has the best gallo pinto
Nicaraguan version uses black beans and does not have Lizano sauce
Fry the rice already cooked next to the beans with onion
Served with scrambled egg, dried and ripe cheese fried at breakfast
The name comes from the black and white speckled appearance of the dish

regular:688.name: Vigorón Nicaragüense
regular:688.desc: Yucca cooked with crispy chicharrón and cabbage tanned served on banana leaf.
hints: Served on banana leaf instead of dish — the classic presentation—
Sour cabbage tanning contrasts with chicharrón fat
Granada, colonial city of the lake, is where the vigorón originated
Sold in street stalls and markets throughout Nicaragua
The name vigorón comes from the advertising of a 19th century medicine

regular:689.name: Indio Viejo Nicaragüense
regular:689.desc: Thick stew of corn dough with shredded beef, tomato, achiote and mint.
hints: The corn dough dissolves in the broth and thickens the stew completely
The fresh mint inside is the scent that makes it completely unique
It is one of the oldest and most pre-Columbian dishes in Nicaragua
Served with white rice and corn tortillas as an accompaniment
Managua’s restaurants serve it as a typical dish of national cuisine

regular:690.name: Plátano Frito con Cuajada
regular:690.desc: Mature banana fried in slices with curd — fresh cheese— and acidic cream on top.
hints: Curd is Nicaragua’s most typical fresh cheese, soft and moist
The very mature banana is fried until caramelized on the outside
The acidic cream is served on top along with the shredded curd
It is the most popular snack of Nicaraguan afternoons in the countryside
The sweet-salted combination of banana and curd is the local pleasure

regular:691.name: Güirilas Nicaragüenses
regular:691.desc: Thick and sweet corn tortillas cooked in comal, with cream and cheese.
hints: Sweet tender corn makes the tortilla taste natural
They are thicker and sweeter than Salvadoran or Guatemalan tortillas
Acid cream and grated dry cheese are your classic accompaniments
They are breakfast and seasonal snack when tender corn is available
Nicaragua sells them on the markets all year round

regular:692.name: Sopa de Res Nicaragüense
regular:692.desc: Broth of beef ribs with potatoes, chayotes, yucca and herbs from the Nicaraguan countryside.
hints: The rib with bone gives the most tasty and gelatinous broth
The chayote — güisquil— and cassava are the most characteristic vegetables
The grasses of the field—culantro and oregano—give it the local aroma
It is the most traditional Sunday lunch of Nicaraguan families
Served with freshly made corn tortillas

regular:693.name: Perrerreque Nicaragüense
regular:693.desc: Sauce bread or corn with dry, sweet and fluffy cheese, traditional dessert.
hints: The ground corn is the basis of this bread denser than wheat
The salted dried grated cheese contrasts with the sweetness of corn
Bake in wood-burning oven in the countryside for patron saintly parties
It is the sweetest prepared in the celebrations of Pacific peoples
Leon and Managua have the best-known and best-selling versions of the country

regular:694.name: Buñuelos Nicaragüenses
regular:694.desc: Yucca balls and fried cheese bathed in honey of sweet cover, Christmas dessert.
hints: Cooked and crushed cassava is mixed with cheese before frying
The sweet cap —panel— is boiled to make the honey thick
It is Nicaragua’s most anticipated and traditional Christmas dessert
They are sold in the squares during December and the patron saintly holidays
They are different from Mexican fritters in the use of cassava instead of flour

regular:695.name: Rosquillas de Maíz Nicaragüenses
regular:695.desc: Hard cheese corn donuts, the most popular and exported dry bread in the country.
hints: The dough of corn with dry cheese is baked until very hard
They are the dry sweet most exported by Nicaraguans in the diaspora
Carazo, south of Managua, produces the most famous donuts
They eat soaked in black coffee or hot chocolate
Its hardness allows to keep them for weeks without cooling

regular:696.name: Caballo Bayo Nicaragüense
regular:696.desc: Thick soup of beans with legs of pork, corn and spices, festive dish of the north.
hints: The name does not refer to the horse but to the brown colour of the beans
The legs of pork — pig — are cooked to the ground in the broth
Maize in grains is added to give more consistency to the thick stew
The northern part of Nicaragua, especially Estelí and Matagalpa, consumes more
It is the dish of holidays and important celebrations of the north

regular:697.name: Carne Asada Nicaragüense
regular:697.desc: Beef marinated in sour orange, garlic and chili, roasted to the embers, Nicaraguan dish.
hints: Sour orange gives you the acidity that penetrates the meat when marinating
Congo pepper and garlic are the most commonly used condiments
Served with gallo pinto, ripe fried and fresh salad
It is the dish of Nicaraguan holidays and family reunions
The embers of oak wood give you the most authentic smoked aroma

regular:698.name: Tamales Costeños Nicaragüenses
regular:698.desc: Tamales rice with pork, olives and chiltoma from the Nicaraguan Caribbean.
hints: Nicaragua’s Caribbean Coast Uses Rice Instead of Maize
Chiltoma—sweet pepper—gives the tropical flavor different to the interior
Olives and pork are the most typical fillers of the coastal version
Totally different from nacatamal Pacific corn mass
Bluefields and the Caribbean Coast are cities of historical origin of the dish

regular:699.name: Sopa de Pata Salvadoreña
regular:699.desc: Rope soup with corn, yucca, loroco and spices, the most Salvadoran soup that exists.
hints: The beef leg is cooked until the bone gelatin enriches the broth
The parrot — edible flower— gives it the unique and inimitable aroma
Corn in grains and cassava give the body to thick broth
San Salvador has specialized restaurants in this soup from early on
Eating Sundays as a celebration and recovery dish

regular:700.name: Carne Guisada Salvadoreña
regular:700.desc: Meat of beef in tomato sauce, sweet chili and spices, national daily stew.
hints: The sweet chili — pepper — is the vegetable that identifies it most
The tomato sauce with onion and garlic is the simplest base
It is the most cooked meat stew in Salvadoran homes
Served on white rice with fried beans and corn tortillas
It can be made with beef, chicken or pork with the same base sauce

regular:701.name: Atol Shuco Salvadoreño
regular:701.desc: Hot drink of black corn fermented with beans and chili, Salvadoran ancestral drink.
hints: Fermented black corn gives it the acidic flavor and grayish color
The ground beans give the thickness and protein to the drink
The chili gives it the mild itching that makes it a hot breakfast
It is the oldest pre-Columbian drink that keeps alive in the country
San Salvador sells it in street stalls since 4 a.m

regular:702.name: Horchata Salvadoreña
regular:702.desc: Drink of ground morro seed with cocoa, fat pepper and other spices.
hints: Morro seed is the base ingredient that does not exist in other horchatas
Cocoa and cinnamon give you the most characteristic aromatic depth
The fat pepper gives it the spicy and unique spiced touch
It's completely different from the rice horchata of Mexico
San Salvador and Santa Ana have the best handmade horchata stalls

regular:703.name: Semita Salvadoreña
regular:703.desc: Sweet bread layered with sweet panela or fruit, the most traditional dessert in the country.
hints: The flour dough is made in thin layers with butter between them
The sweet grated panela is the most classic and ancient filling
Suchitoto and Sensuntepeque are famous for their handmade semites
Eating at breakfast or snack with black coffee
It is the sweet bread most representative of the traditional Salvadoran bakery

regular:704.name: Quesadilla de Arroz Salvadoreña
regular:704.desc: Sweet cake of rice flour with hard cheese and sesame seeds, colonial dessert.
hints: Rice flour gives you a denser texture than wheat flour
Dried cheese grated hard is mixed in the dough before baking
The sesame seeds above are the visual touch that identifies it
It is different from the Mexican tortilla quesadilla in all its concept
San Salvador has colonial bakeries that have made it for centuries

regular:705.name: Mariscada Salvadoreña
regular:705.desc: A variety of seafood soup with coconut milk, cream and sweet chili, coastal festive dish.
hints: The seafood of the Salvadoran Pacific are the protagonists of the dish
Coconut milk gives tropical creaminess to the festive broth
Sweet pepper — pepper — is the most characteristic vegetable of the dish
La Libertad and the Port of La Unión are the best places to eat it
Served in special celebrations such as weddings and fifteen years

regular:706.name: Riguas Salvadoreñas
regular:706.desc: Thick corn cakes roasted in griddle, accompanied by cream and cheese.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw for the dough without any flour
They are cooked directly in the griddle without oil until golden on the outside
Cream and hard cheese are the only classic accompaniments
They are the whim of season when the corn is at its tender point
Salvadoran markets sell them especially from July to September

regular:707.name: Sopa de Frijoles Salvadoreña
regular:707.desc: Thick cream of red beans with parrot, hard cheese grated and acidic cream.
hints: The parrot is a Salvadoran edible flower with a very special aroma
Salvadoran red bean blends to make the cream thick
The hard cheese grated and dried is generously sprinkled on top
It is the most daily and consumed soup in all Salvadoran homes
Served with freshly made corn tortillas to soak in the cream

regular:708.name: Tamale de Chipilín Salvadoreño
regular:708.desc: Tamal corn dough with chiplin and cheese, wrapped in steamed corn leaf.
hints: The chipilin is a very nutritious plant with high iron content
The dough is dyed green with the chipilin ground directly
Fresh cheese in the center contrasts with vegetable flavor
They are the tamales lightest and most vegetarian in Salvadoran cuisine
They are eaten as breakfast or snack in popular markets

regular:709.name: Tortitas de Yuca Salvadoreñas
regular:709.desc: Fried yucca cakes grated with cheese and parrot, popular Salvadoran appetizer.
hints: Raw grated cassava is mixed with cheese and parrot before frying
The parrot gives the unmistakable Salvadoran aroma to pancakes
They fry until they get crispy on the outside and soft on the inside
They are very popular as appetizers in typical cuisine restaurants
The fresh parrot is found only in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras

regular:710.name: Pollo Encebollado Salvadoreño
regular:710.desc: Chicken stewed with abundant caramelized onion, tomato and Salvadoran spices.
hints: The onion is simmering very slowly until completely caramelized
The chopped tomato is added to make the base sauce of the stew
It is a dish of Salvadoran home cooking very simple and nutritious
Served on white rice with beans and corn tortillas always
It is the most cooked chicken in the popular eaters of San Salvador

regular:711.name: Asado Paraguayo
regular:711.desc: Meats of beef and pork roasted to the embers with rib and chorizo, tradition of the countryside.
hints: Paraguay has one of the oldest livestock traditions in the region
Roast is made on a stick or iron grill depending on the region
The beef rib and red chorizo are the most popular cuts
Sundays are the sacred day of family roasting in the country
Paraguayan meat of natural pastures is highly appreciated regionally

regular:712.name: Vorí Vorí
regular:712.desc: Soup of corn balls and cheese cooked in chicken broth, classic Guaraní dish.
hints: Balls are made with mixed corn flour and Paraguayan cheese
Cook directly in the hot chicken broth until floating
It is different from the bori bori in corn type and cheese ratio
The Guaraní language gave the name to this ancestral dish of the country
It is one of the most beloved soups and representative of national cuisine

regular:713.name: Chipa Guazú
regular:713.desc: Spongy pastel of choclo tender with Paraguayan cheese and eggs, party dish.
hints: The choclo tender grated is the wet and sweet base of the cake
Fresh Paraguayan cheese gives it the salty flavor that balances corn
The beaten eggs give you the sponginess when baking in the oven
It is different from the sopa paraguaya in being choclo tender, not dry corn
Served as a side dish for roasting in the country's celebrations

regular:714.name: Chipa de Almidón
regular:714.desc: Circular bread of cassava starch and cheese, baked and consumed in Easter.
hints: Manioc starch gives you the elastic texture and slightly chewable
Fresh Paraguayan cheese is the most important ingredient of flavor
It is consumed massively in Easter, each family makes its own
The circular shape with hole in the center is the most classic and traditional
The aroma of the freshly baked chipa is recognized throughout the country

regular:715.name: Kivevé Paraguayo
regular:715.desc: Sweet pumpkin puree with corn flour, cheese and milk, dessert and national garnish.
hints: Andaí (Paraguaya calabaza) is the most commonly used variety
The corn flour thickens the pumpkin puree to become very dense
The salty Paraguayan cheese contrasts with the natural sweetness of pumpkin
It is a dish that functions as dessert or as a side of roasting
Asunción recognizes it as part of the national gastronomic identity

regular:716.name: Estofado Paraguayo
regular:716.desc: Steak beef with vegetables, olives and red wine, the country's creole stew.
hints: Olives give the local stew a salty and Mediterranean touch
Red wine gives acidity and dark color to the stew broth
Vegetables in the vegetable garden — carrot, onion — are the most widely used
It is the most classic pot stew in Paraguayan Dominican cuisine
Assumption and interior have the most authentic and abundant versions

regular:717.name: Sopa de Maní Paraguaya
regular:717.desc: Chicken broth with ground peanuts, noodles, potato and vegetables, dish of national comfort.
hints: The ground peanut thickens the broth naturally and gives it the flavor
It is one of the most beloved spoon dishes in Paraguayan cuisine
Noodles and potatoes go straight into the broth until cooked
Asunción and Villarrica have the most famous restaurants for this dish
Eating in all regions with small local variations

regular:718.name: Arroz con Leche Paraguayo
regular:718.desc: Rice cooked in milk with cinnamon, lemon zest and sugar, simple family dessert.
hints: The lemon zest gives you the citrus freshness that distinguishes it
Cinnamon is added in powder at the end above cold rice
It is the simplest and most home-made dessert in Paraguayan village cuisine
Served cold in individual bowls with sprinkled cinnamon
Each Paraguayan grandmother has a slightly different variant

regular:719.name: Locro Paraguayo
regular:719.desc: White corn stew with meat, pumpkin and cheese, Paraguayan version of the locro Andean.
hints: White maize — locro — cooks for hours until soft
The zapallo — calabaza— gives the color and sweetness to the thick stew
The beef or pork is cooked next to the corn from the beginning
It is different from the locro Argentine in the use of added Paraguayan cheese
It is eaten especially in the cold months of Paraguayan winter

regular:720.name: Pastel Mandi'o Paraguayo
regular:720.desc: Large empanada of cassava dough —yuca— filled with ground meat, baked.
hints: The cassava, cooked and crushed forms the dough of this cake
Ground meat seasoned with onion and spices is the filling
Bake in the oven until golden on the outside and cooked inside
It is a dish of utilization that uses the leftover cooked cassava
Asunción and the Paraguayan countryside prepare it especially on Saturdays

regular:721.name: Dulce de Mburucuyá
regular:721.desc: Wild maracuyá jam — Burrucuyá— with sugar, Paraguayan traditional dessert.
hints: Burucuyá is the Guaraní name of passion fruit or passion fruit
The fruit is cooked with sugar to thicken and form the jam
It grows wild in the mountains and fields of Paraguay naturally
It is spread on bread or used as a filling of cakes and desserts
The Guaraní name reminds us of the indigenous origin of this tradition

regular:722.name: Olla de Carne Costarricense
regular:722.desc: Thick beef soup with chayote, yuca, banana and corn, the most Costa Rican dish.
hints: The chayote – güisquil – is the most Costa Rican vegetable in the country
The cassava and the green banana are added next to the meat to thicken the broth
It is the most consumed dish on Sundays throughout the tica family
Served with corn tortillas and white rice next door
San José and the central provinces have the best versions of the country

regular:723.name: Arroz con Leche Tico
regular:723.desc: Rice cooked in milk with cinnamon, vanilla and condensed milk, national creamy dessert.
hints: Condensed milk gives you the extra sweetness that makes it very creamy
The natural vanilla of Costa Rica gives you the most special aroma
It is the most cooked dessert in Costa Rican homes every day
It is served cold with sprinkled cinnamon like any good rice with milk
It's different from the tico in using vanilla instead of lemon zest

regular:724.name: Picadillo de Papas Tico
regular:724.desc: Potato cooked in sofrito of onion, tomato, sweet chili and cilantro, garnish tica.
hints: The cilantro (broad leafed coriander) is the most Costa Rican aroma
The potato is cut into small cubes and fried with all vegetables
It is the most basic and economical garrison of everyday cooking
Served as a side dish for any roasted or fried meat
There are variants with chayote, vainicas or raracache depending on the region

regular:725.name: Chorreadas Costarricenses
regular:725.desc: Thick tender corn tortillas cooked in comal, the tico breakfast par excellence.
hints: The tender corn ground is the only dough, without dried corn flour
They are thicker and fluffy than normal Central American tortillas
They are accompanied with acidic cream and tender cheese at breakfast
It is the most traditional country breakfast in rural tica
The Central Valley sells them in fairs and sodas from very early

regular:726.name: Sopa de Frijoles Negros Tica
regular:726.desc: Thick cream of black beans with cilantro, onion and sour cream, Costa Rican national soup.
hints: The beans are completely blended to make the cream dense
The cilantro —a broad-leaf coriander— gives it the Costa Rican seal
The acidic cream is added to each dish at the time of serving
It is the most consumed soup in the country’s sodas — local restaurants
Served with white rice and corn tortillas as an accompaniment

regular:727.name: Tamal Tico
regular:727.desc: Tamal dough of corn with pork, olives, raisins and rice, wrapped in banana leaf.
hints: Olives and raisins differentiate it from tamales other countries
The banana leaf gives you the green aroma that characterizes it
It prepares massively on Christmas and New Year in all families
The dough carries butter and pork broth to be very soft
They are boiled by two — pines — for easier conservation

regular:728.name: Picadillo de Arracache
regular:728.desc: Arracache —white Andean root— in sofrito pork, onion and spices, garnish tica.
hints: Arracache is a unique white and aromatic tuber of Costa Rica
It is chopped in small cubes and fried with ground pork and onion
It is the most Costa Rican garrison that exists to use the arracache
San José and the Central Valley consume it as a weekend dish
The aroma of the root is impossible to confuse with any other vegetable

regular:729.name: Cajetas de Coco Ticas
regular:729.desc: Hard coconut caramel grated with sugar and condensed milk, sweet artisan tico.
hints: Fresh grated coconut is cooked with sugar until caramelized
Condensed milk gives creaminess to soft cards
There are hard and soft versions depending on the cooking time of the sugar
It is the best selling sweet craft in markets and fairs
Liberia and Guanacaste have the most authentic coconut versions of the country

regular:730.name: Carne Asada Tica
regular:730.desc: Flesh marinated in chimichurri tico, roasted and served with gallo pinto and mature.
hints: Chimichurri tico has mixed cilantro, lemon, garlic and parsley
Always served with gallo pinto, fried ripe banana and salad
Sunday is the traditional day to make roast meat in Costa Rica
The Lizano sauce can not be missed on the table next to roast meat
Guanacaste has a tradition of deep-rooted and festive roast meat

regular:731.name: Mondongo Tico
regular:731.desc: Soup of corned beef with chickpeas, potato, sweet chili and cilantro, Sunday soup.
hints: The calluses are cleaned well and cooked for hours until garnished
The chickpeas give it the thick consistency that makes it so nutritious
Fresh cilantro and sweet chili are the most aromatic
It is consumed as a recovery dish on Sundays throughout the family
San Jose and the Central Valley have the best sodas that serve it

regular:732.name: Tamale de Elote Tico
regular:732.desc: Tamal sweet tender corn with butter and cheese, wrapped in leaf of choclo.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw and mixed with butter and sugar
The tender cheese is placed in the center for salty contrast
Wrapped in the corn leaves themselves before steaming
They are the sweetest and most fluffy of Costa Ricans tamales
They are sold at farmers' fairs all over the country

regular:733.name: Pudín de Pan Tico
regular:733.desc: French bread Budin soaked in milk with eggs, sugar and vanilla, baked.
hints: The French bread of the previous day is soaked in hot sugary milk
The Costa Rican aromatic vanilla gives you the most special touch
Bake in the water bath until spongy and firm
It is the most home-made dessert of grandmothers
Served with acidic cream on top or with a little liquid caramel

regular:734.name: Tacos de Canasta
regular:734.desc: Tacos of simple stews — beans, chicharrón, papa — stored in a basket to sweat.
hints: The basket keeps them warm and sweaty by the steam they accumulate
The most classic stews are beans, potato with chorizo and chicharrón
They are sold by bicycle in the streets of Mexico City from early
They're cheaper than any other taco in the country
The heat of the basket softens the tortilla and mixes all flavors

regular:735.name: Tostadas de Cueritos
regular:735.desc: Crispy toasted with pork scabies in vinegar, onion and green sauce.
hints: The skins are pork skin tanned in vinegar and spices
Serve cold on top of toast with green sauce
They are popular in taquerías and cantinas of the center of the country
The vinegar of the scabies gives the characteristic acidic touch
Mexico City serves them as a snack in popular bars

regular:736.name: Mole Amarillo
regular:736.desc: Oaxaqueña sauce of yellow chili with tomato, holy grass and dough to thicken.
hints: The yellow pepper —chilhuacle— gives the golden color to mole
The holy grass gives it the unique anise aroma of Oaxaca
It is one of the seven moles in Oaxaca, the softest of all
Served on chicken or beef rib with chayotes
The dough dissolves the sauce naturally without flour

regular:737.name: Caldo Xóchitl
regular:737.desc: Chicken broth with rice, chickpeas, avocado, jalapeño and herb, from the capital markets.
hints: The markets of Mexico City serve him as a morning replacement
Fresh avocado is added cold over the very hot broth
The jalapeño in small slices gives the characteristic fresh itching
Fresh mint gives it the scent that identifies it
Considered the best remedy to recover from a difficult night

regular:738.name: Tamales de Rajas con Queso
regular:738.desc: Tamales dough of corn stuffed with rajas de chile poblano with Oaxaca cheese and cream.
hints: Roasted pepper slices are the most popular filling in vegetarian
The yarn cheese melts inside with the heat of steam
They are the tamales best sellers in Christmas tamales next to pork
Mexico City sells them from 6 a.m. in street stalls
The dough brings butter to make it softer and fluffy

regular:739.name: Pozole Negro
regular:739.desc: Dark variant of pozole with black chili and spices, typical of Guerrero and Oaxaca.
hints: The toasted black chili pepper gives the broth the dark color
Guerrero and Oaxaca have the most authentic versions of pozole black
Spices include cloves, cinnamon and black pepper
It is decorated as red: lettuce, radish, oregano and lemon
It is the least known of the three wells but the most complex

regular:740.name: Caldo de Camarón
regular:740.desc: Soup of dried shrimps with guajillo chili, tomato and vegetables, Lent dish.
hints: Dried shrimps have a much more concentrated flavor than fresh shrimps
The guajillo chili gives the red color and deep flavor to the broth
It is the star dish of Lent in the Pacific coastal states
It is accompanied with toast and lemon at the time of serving
Oaxaca and Guerrero have the oldest versions of this broth

regular:741.name: Tamales Oaxaqueños de Mole
regular:741.desc: Tamal wrapped in mole black and chicken banana leaf, typical of Oaxaca.
hints: It is wrapped in banana leaf, not corn, unlike another tamales
The mole black Oaxacan is the filling that makes it unique
Oaxaca is the southern state where this variant originated
Steamed for more than an hour
Typical of Day of the Dead celebrations in the region

regular:742.name: Morisqueta Michoacana
regular:742.desc: White rice cooked with brooded beans and pork rib, humble dish of Michoacán.
hints: Morisqueta is the simplest and most nutritious dish in Michoacana cuisine
The rice is cooked separately and the ribed beans are served on top
Michoacán consumes it daily as an economic lunch
The brothy beans bathe the rice giving it an incomparable flavor
It eats in a deep bowl so that the broth is not lost

regular:743.name: Chileatole de Pollo
regular:743.desc: Atole thick corn mass with poblano pepper, corn and chicken, dish of Puebla.
hints: Chileatole mixes atole drink with chili and chicken stew
The corn dough thickens the broth naturally and bluntly
Puebla claims it as its oldest and most emblematic dish
The corn in grains gives you the sweetness that balances the itchy pepper
Served in very hot clay jar as a first course

regular:744.name: Sopa Azteca
regular:744.desc: Restaurant version of tortilla soup with tomato broth, pasilla pepper and cream.
hints: It is the most elaborate version of tortilla soup for restaurants
Fried pasilla pepper is cut into strips and added as garnish
Cream, cheese and avocado are served separately so that everyone mixes
Mexico City offers it in virtually all Mexican cuisine restaurants
The roasted tomato broth gives the different depth to the raw tomato

regular:745.name: Cecina Enchilada Yecapixtla
regular:745.desc: Pork leaves enchilated with ancho pepper and marinade, from Yecapixtla, Morelos.
hints: Yecapixtla in Morelos is the national capital of enchilada cecina
The wide pepper and the achiote give the flesh dark red color
Roast into a griddle until crisp on the outer edges
Served in toast, tacos or with beans and nopales always
The drying and enchilating process lasts several days before being sold

regular:746.name: Mole Colorado Oaxaqueño
regular:746.desc: Oaxacan sauce of dried red chilies with spices and tomato, one of the seven moles.
hints: Mulato pepper and width are the basis of this mole Oaxacan red
It's less dark than black but more complex than the little coloring
Oaxaca uses it for tamales and as a beef stew or pork sauce
The roasted sesame and almonds give the sauce its body
It is the second mole most consumed in Oaxaca after black

regular:747.name: Tlayuda de Tasajo
regular:747.desc: Giant Oaxacan Tortilla with seat, beans and roast beef gravy on top.
hints: The beef taxage is the most traditional cut over the tlayuda
The seat — chicharrón grease — goes first on the tortilla
Oaxaca serves it in restaurants and markets at any time
The yarn cheese and the chapulin are additional toppings
It's different from the standard tlayuda for carrying beef assessment

regular:748.name: Pinole con Leche
regular:748.desc: Roasted corn drink ground with milk, cinnamon and sugar, pre-Hispanic drink from the north.
hints: Pinewood is roasted corn flour, sometimes mixed with cocoa
North Mexico — Chihuahua, Sonora— consumes it since raramuri times
It is mixed with cold or hot milk according to preference
It is a natural energy drink used by Tarahumara corridors
It is also eaten in balls or mixed with simple water

regular:749.name: Gorditas de Azúcar
regular:749.desc: Sweet corn dough fried with sugar and cinnamon, very popular street candy.
hints: The dough is prepared with corn, piloncillo and cinnamon before frying
Fry until crispy and sprinkle with more sugar
They are different from salty gorditas in all their concept and flavor
Guanajuato and Bassio sell them as market treats
They eat hot freshly fried as afternoon snack

regular:750.name: Carne Enchilada Norteña
regular:750.desc: Grilled beef steak in red chili and garlic, grilled or embers.
hints: The red pepper from the north — dried-red chili — gives it color and flavor
Chihuahua and Sonora are the states with the greatest tradition of this dish
Meat is macerated in chili marinade for several hours
Served with red rice, beans and flour tortillas from the north
Garlic and cumin complement the taste of chili in marinade

regular:751.name: Quesillo Oaxaqueño Frito
regular:751.desc: Oaxaqueño cheese fried to brown, served with sauce and toast.
hints: The cheese is melted into strips and fried in hot oil
It's golden on the outside and melted inside in a few seconds
Oaxaca serves as a snack or entrance before the main course
The green or red sauce is served next to the fried cheese
It can also be prepared in oilless griddle for lighter version

regular:752.name: Pambazos de Papas
regular:752.desc: Pambazo bread bathed in chili sauce guajillo, stuffed with potatoes with chorizo and fried.
hints: Pambazo is a fluffy crumb bread that is bathed in guajillo red sauce
It is pressed in comal with oil until the sauce is integrated into the bread
The potato filler with chorizo is the most classic and popular
Mexico City sells them in virtually all markets
The intense red color of the exterior makes them very striking and recognizable

regular:753.name: Helado de Mamey
regular:753.desc: Creamy snow of mamey pulp with milk and sugar, very Mexican tropical flavor.
hints: Mamey is a tropical fruit with pink orange pulp
The creamy texture and sweetness of the mamey make it ideal for snow
Cuernavaca and Morelos are famous for their handcrafted mamey snows
The taste is unique in the world, between pumpkin and almond
Can be made with or without milk, the water version is lighter

regular:754.name: Tamal de Chipilín
regular:754.desc: Tamal corn dough mixed with chipilin, stuffed cheese, from the Mexican southeast.
hints: The chipilín is a very popular edible plant in the southeast of the country
The dough is dyed green with the chiplin chopped and mixed inside
Chiapas and Tabasco are the states that consume it the most
The fresh cheese inside contrasts with the vegetable flavor of the dough
Wrapped in corn leaf and steamed one hour

regular:755.name: Arroz con Leche de Arroz
regular:755.desc: Rice cooked in homemade rice milk with cinnamon and piloncillo, ancient vegan dessert.
hints: Rice milk is made by grinding rice soaked with water
The piloncillo gives the dark sweetness different from white sugar
It is the vegan version of rice with milk, without lactose
Indigenous communities prepare it for special festivities
Oaxaca and the mountain areas consume it more frequently

regular:756.name: Caldo de Habas
regular:756.desc: Soup of dried beans with nopal, onion, epazote and serrano pepper, Mexican Lent.
hints: Dried beans soak and peel before cooking in the broth
The nopal gives you mucilage texture and mild acidic flavor
It is the star dish of Lent in downtown states
The epazote is the grass that can not be missed in any broth of beans
Served with toast and dried chili to crush inside

regular:757.name: Salbutes Yucatecos
regular:757.desc: Fried and sponged corn tortilla with shredded chicken, lettuce, tomato and purple onion.
hints: The tortilla is fried until sponged and inflated with hot air
The shredded chicken is seasoned with achiote and sour orange
