Iquitos consumes it massively at the San Juan festival—June 24—
It is the most elaborate and festive tamal Amazonian in the entire Peruvian jungle

regular:822.name: Cuchuco de Cebada
regular:822.desc: Pearl barley soup with pork spine and criolla potato, similar to wheat cuckoo.
hints: Pearl barley has a creamier texture than broken wheat
The pork thorn gives the fat and nutritious flavor to the thick broth
Boyacá also prepares this version with barley instead of wheat
It is slightly softer and sweeter than the classic wheat cuckoo
It is consumed in the markets of the buoyacense highlands on Saturdays

regular:823.name: Fritada de Cerdo Colombiana
regular:823.desc: Fried pork in its own fat with mote and onion and tomato hogao.
hints: The pig fryes slowly in its own fat until it is golden
White peeled corn mote is the most typical accompaniment
The tomato and onion hogao is served above to give acidity and freshness
It is different from the Ecuadorian fried in the use of Colombian hogao
The inter-Andean valleys of Cauca and Valle consume it more frequently

regular:824.name: Hogao con Arroz
regular:824.desc: Sofrito Colombian tomato and long onion on white rice, the base of every dish.
hints: Hogao is the sofrito most basic and indispensable Colombian in cooking
Long onion —onion—and tomato are the only two ingredients
Cook over low heat until the onion caramelizes with tomato
Accompany virtually any dish of Colombian everyday cuisine
Cumin and garlic are optional but very common in many versions

regular:825.name: Patacón con Guacamole
regular:825.desc: Crusty green banana patacón covered in guacamole with tomato and onion.
hints: The patacón is fried, crushed and fryed again to make it crisper
Colombian guacamole carries tomato, onion and lemon without jalapeno
It is the most popular appetizer of Colombian coastal restaurants
Also served with hogao, seafood or simply sea salt
The Caribbean and Pacific coasts are where this combination is consumed the most

regular:826.name: Empanadas de Pipián
regular:826.desc: Empanadas del Valle del Cauca stuffed with potatoes and pipián nuggets, without meat.
hints: The pipián nuggets is pumpkin sauce that gives the unique flavor
The empanadas vallecaucanas are smaller and crispier than other regions
The potato in cubes and the pipián are the most traditional meatless filling
Cali and Valle del Cauca produce the most famous pipián empanadas
They are eaten with spicy chili that is poured into with a spoon

regular:827.name: Sancocho de Cola
regular:827.desc: Red-tailed soup with cassava, banana and papa criolla, Sunday dish in the Valley.
hints: The cooked beef tail slowly releases all its collagen into the broth
The Valle del Cauca, especially Cali, claims this sancocho as its own
The cassava, the green banana and the papa criolla are inseparable food
The hogao is served separately to add to taste above sancocho
It is the sancocho most expensive for the price of beef glue on the market

regular:828.name: Arroz de Lisa
regular:828.desc: Rice cooked with smooth — riverfish— and sofrito Caribbean rice in a pot.
hints: Lisa is a very common fish in the rivers and swamps of the Caribbean coast
Rice is cooked with fish from the beginning in the same pot
The sofrito tomato, pepper and onion gives you the unmistakable Caribbean flavor
Mompox and the banks of the Magdalena River consume it daily
It is the dish of artisanal fishermen from the Colombian Caribbean coast

regular:829.name: Changua Bogotana
regular:829.desc: Milk soup with water, cilantro and poached egg, breakfast of the Bogotans.
hints: Milk and water are boiled together as the basis of this light soup
The egg is poached directly into the hot liquid at the end
Bogotá and the cundiboyacense savanna have eaten it as breakfast for ever
The fresh chopped cilantro is added just before serving in the bowl
It is accompanied by bread-wrought bread—soaked bread to soak in the soup

regular:830.name: Refajo Colombiano
regular:830.desc: A mixture of beer and Colombiana — colored gassy— served as a festive appetizer.
hints: The flaw is the typical mixture of Colombian celebrations and festivals
Colombiana —Orange Refreshment — Mixes With Blonde Beer in Equal Parts
It is the most popular festive drink of roasts and informal meetings
The Valle del Cauca and Bogotá are the places where you consume the most
There are no fixed proportions: each mix according to his personal preference

regular:831.name: Caldo de Costilla Bogotano
regular:831.desc: Clear beef rib broth with potatoes and coriander, traditionally eaten for breakfast in Bogotá after a night out.
hints: The bone-in ribs are put on to simmer in the early hours.
The broth stays clear while taking on flavour and collagen from the bones.
Fresh coriander and small yellow criolla potatoes complete the broth.
Restaurants in Bogotá serve it for breakfast from four in the morning.
It is a popular restorative breakfast in the Colombian capital at weekends.

regular:832.name: Envuelto de Mazorca
regular:832.desc: Sweet corn dough with sugar and cheese, wrapped in steamed cob leaf.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw and mixed with cheese and sugar
It is the equivalent of humita or tamal sweet in the Colombian version
Wrapped in the corn leaf itself and steamed
It is sweeter than tamal salty and it is eaten as a snack or dessert
The Eastern Plains and the Coffee Shaft have the most consumed versions

regular:833.name: Sancocho de Mariscos Costero
regular:833.desc: A variety of seafood soup with cassava, banana and coconut milk, from the peaceful coast.
hints: Coconut milk gives you the tropical creaminess of the peaceful coast
Colombian Pacific seafood is of the highest quality and freshness
The cassava and the green plantain are the meats that thicken the broth
Buenaventura is the most famous city for this sancocho seafood
The cilantro — broad-leaved coriander — flavour the broth at the end

regular:834.name: Sudado de Pollo
regular:834.desc: Chicken stewed in sofrito with potato, tomato and cumin, the most homemade version of the stew.
hints: The chicken is slowly cooked in the sofrito tomato and onion
The Criolla potato is cooked next to the chicken in the last 20 minutes
Cumin and coriander are the most aromatic Colombian stew
It is the daily dish in Colombian homes of any region
Served with white rice and fried ripe banana as an accompaniment

regular:835.name: Masato de Maíz
regular:835.desc: Fermented corn drink with panela and cinnamon, handmade drink of the Llanos.
hints: The corn is fermented several days with panela to develop the acidic flavor
Cinnamon cracked is added during fermentation to flavour
The Eastern Plains—Meta and Casanare—are the best known for doing so
It's different from the chicha in which it's made of white and non-purple corn
Served at room temperature in totuma or glass of artisanal clay

regular:836.name: Arepa de Huevo Costeña
regular:836.desc: Arepa fried whole egg, star dish of the Colombian Caribbean coast.
hints: The arepa is first fried before filling with raw egg
It closes with fresh dough and fry again until the egg is boiled inside
Barranquilla and Cartagena are the most famous cities for this dish
The egg is poached inside the oil without breaking the yolk
It is accompanied with tomato hogao and chili pepper to the side always

regular:837.name: Queso de Mano Venezolano
regular:837.desc: Fresh Venezuelan cheese made of cow's milk, soft and moist, served with paper and coffee.
hints: The hand cheese is called that because it forms by pressing the curd with hands
It is the most consumed cheese in Venezuela, wetter than white cheese
It is accompanied by grated paper for the classic sweet-salted contrast
The central states — Aragua and Carabobo — produce the best hand cheese
It melts easily over arepas hot and hot dishes from all the Venezuelan cuisine

regular:838.name: Catara de Bachaco
regular:838.desc: Indian salsa of bachaca ants with ají, salt and spices, from the Venezuelan Amazon.
hints: The bachaca is a large ant used as ancestral food
The indigenous peoples of the Venezuelan Amazon have consumed it for centuries
Ants roast before they grind with chili and salt
It is one of the most exotic and ancient salsas in Venezuela
The southern part of the country — Amazonas and Bolívar — are the regions where it is prepared

regular:839.name: Hervido de Gallina Venezolano
regular:839.desc: Chicken soup with vegetables, banana and criollo dressing, the Venezuelan reconstituent.
hints: Hen boil is more concentrated than the normal sancocho
The patio hen gives a broth much more intense than the farm chicken
It boils for hours until the chicken is very tender
The criollo dressing with sweet aji and coriander gives the Venezuelan label
It is the dish that is consumed most after giving birth, as a restorative

regular:840.name: Fosforera Venezolana
regular:840.desc: Aphrodisiac soup of varied seafood with spicy pepper, egg and lemon, from the coast.
hints: The phosphorous name comes from its so-called popular aphrodisiac properties
Seafood on the Venezuelan coast of the Caribbean are the protagonists
Heavy black pepper and lemon give it the itching and acidity
It is sold in the premises of Venezuelan ports at dawn
The beaten egg is added at the end to enrich the hot broth

regular:841.name: Mandoca Venezolana
regular:841.desc: Sweet corn doughnut and ripe cambur fried with paper, zulian breakfast.
hints: Zulia state, in western Venezuela, is the cradle of the boss
Mature cambur — small banana — gives you sweetness and wet texture
The paper—panel—gives the dark, caramelized sweetness to the dough
They fry until golden brown and eat hot with grated cheese
It is the most typical breakfast of Maracaibo and the Venezuelan Zulia

regular:842.name: Pabellón Criollo Venezolano
regular:842.desc: White rice, black caraotas, wicked meat and slices of banana, the national dish.
hints: It is the most representative national dish of Venezuela unanimously
The four colours — white, black, brown and yellow — represent the flag
The wicked meat is melted in thin strips with fork or hand
The slices of fried ripe banana are the sweetest element of the dish
Everything is served together on the same plate without mixing components

regular:843.name: Cachapa con Queso de Mano
regular:843.desc: Thick and sweet tortilla of choclo tender with melted hand cheese in the center.
hints: The choclo tender is ground raw to make the dough naturally sweet
Venezuelan hand cheese melts inside when the cachapa hot closes
It is cooked in griddle or budare until golden on both sides
It is the most popular breakfast and snack on Venezuelan weekends
The texture is between tortilla and pancake, much thicker and moister

regular:844.name: Bienmesabe de Coco Venezolano
regular:844.desc: Coconut cream with sugar, egg yolks and cinnamon, Venezuelan colonial dessert.
hints: Fresh grated coconut is the main ingredient and most aromatic
The egg yolks give the creaminess and golden yellow color
Sugar and cinnamon balance coconut flavor with the necessary sweetness
It is different from the Spanish bienmesabe in the abundant use of coconut
Cold served as party dessert with cookies or biscuits next door

regular:845.name: Golfeado Venezolano
regular:845.desc: Sweet dough roll with paper, cheese and anise, the Venezuelan sweet-salted muffin.
hints: The paper —panel — inside the dough gives it the dark sweetness
Venezuelan salty white cheese contrasts with sweet paper
The anise gives it the floral aroma that makes it unmistakable
Spiral baking and caramelizing paper on the edges
It is the most popular sweet bread in bakeries throughout Venezuela

regular:846.name: Sopa de Arvejas Venezolana
regular:846.desc: Soup of peas split yellow with criollo dressing, potato and cilantro.
hints: The yellow split peas are cooked until disposed in the broth
Creole dressing with sweet chili and onion is the aromatic base
The potato in cubes gives consistency and body to the broth
It is the most economical and nutritious soup on Mondays in many homes
Served with arepa hot and sliced avocados always

regular:847.name: Parrilla Venezolana
regular:847.desc: Venezuelan beef roast with guacaca and Creole salad, weekend tradition.
hints: The avocado and cilantro guacaca is the irreplaceable sauce of roasting
Lomito, rib and churrasco are the most popular cuts
The wood fire gives you the smoky aroma that distinguishes you from gas
Creole salad with tomato, onion and cilantro is always served
The eastern plains have the country’s most deeply rooted roasting tradition

regular:848.name: Pastel de Morrocoy
regular:848.desc: Morrocoy tortoise pie on banana leaf, ancient llanero dish.
hints: The morrocoy is a terrestrial turtle whose meat is consumed in the plains
It is an ancestral dish of the Llanero peoples of Venezuela
The meat is cooked with sweet chili, onion and creole spices
Wrapped in banana leaf and roast over the coals of the stove
It is a dish in danger of gastronomic extinction for the protection of the animal

regular:849.name: Yoyos de Plátano Maduro
regular:849.desc: Mature fried banana discs stuffed with white cheese, glued and fried again.
hints: The banana is cut into thick slices and fried first until softened
The white cheese is put between two slices and squeezed like a sandwich
They fry again until the cheese melts and the banana caramelizes
They are one of the most creative and popular appetizers in Venezuelan cuisine
His name comes from the round shape that remembers the toy yoyo

regular:850.name: Ensalada de Gallina Venezolana
regular:850.desc: Chicken torn with potato, carrot, mayonnaise and mustard, Venezuelan Christmas salad.
hints: The chicken cooks whole and then completely debones
Potato and carrot are cooked separately and cooled before mixing
Mayonnaise and mustard give the creamy and acidic touch to the whole
It is the most prepared Christmas and New Year salad in Venezuela
It always goes along with the pernil, the hallaca and the Christmas ham bread

regular:851.name: Hervido de Res Venezolano
regular:851.desc: Soup beef with potatoes, cassava, banana and criollo dressing, bovine version of the boiled.
hints: The boiled beef uses rib or skirt meat with bone
The cassava, the potato and the banana are the food that can not miss
The Venezuelan criollo dressing with sweet chili gives the Caribbean label
It is the Sunday dish in the homes of Venezuelan plains
It's different from the sancocho when it boils longer and with more water

regular:852.name: Palomita de Maíz Venezolana
regular:852.desc: Popcorn caramelized with paper and butter, the snack of Venezuelan cinema.
hints: The melted paper —panel — covers popcorn with hand-made caramel
The butter is mixed with the paper to make the caramel creamier
It is the Venezuelan version of sweet popcorn in American cinema
Caracas cinemas sell them in huge buckets of paper
The salty version with butter is also very popular in the country

regular:853.name: Canjica Branca
regular:853.desc: White corn cooked in milk with grated coconut, cinnamon and sugar, Festa Junina dessert.
hints: White canjica corn cooks for hours until softened completely
Cow's milk and grated coconut give you tropical creaminess
The cinnamon in branch is cooked inside and removed before serving
It is the most popular dessert of June Junina Festas in the country
It differs from nordestine mungunzá in using cow's milk and not coconut milk

regular:854.name: Macarrão ao Sugo
regular:854.desc: Italian pasta with simple homemade tomato sauce, the Sunday dish of São Paulo italo-Brazilian.
hints: Italian immigration in São Paulo made macarrão the most consumed pasta
The sauce is simply tomato, garlic, onion, basil and oil
Italobrasileiros cook it on Sundays for the whole family gathered
São Paulo has more Italian descendants than any city in the world
Queijo parmesão grated above is the only classic accompaniment

regular:855.name: Arroz de Carreteiro
regular:855.desc: Dried rice cooked with dried meat and vegetables, gaucho dish of the troiros.
hints: The troiros —arrieros— cooked it on the stands with what they had available
Dry dehydrated meat is rehydrated and mixed with dry rice
Rio Grande do Sul claims it as its most unique field dish
Onions and tomatoes are the only vegetables that always go
Dry meat should be soaked at least 8 hours before use in the recipe

regular:856.name: Galinha à Cabidela
regular:856.desc: Chicken stewed in its own blood with vinegar and spices, Portuguese heritage.
hints: The chicken blood is collected with vinegar so that it does not clot too fast
The vinegar gives the acidity that balances the intense taste of the blood
It is a direct heritage of the Portuguese colonial cabidela galinha
The north and northeast of Brazil are the ones who consume it most today
The dark color of the dish impresses but the flavor is deep and complex

regular:857.name: Tapioca de Queijo
regular:857.desc: Crispy tapioca starch cream stuffed with melted coalho cheese from the Northeast.
hints: The tapioca starch spreads into the hot griddle and is pressed to form the crepe
The North American coalho cheese melts inside when the tapioca is closed
It is the most popular breakfast in Recife, Fortaleza and the whole Northeast
It does not carry wheat flour, it is gluten-free 100% natural
It is also filled with sweet grated coconut for dessert version

regular:858.name: Feijoada Vegetariana
regular:858.desc: Version of the feijoada without meats with beans, banana da terra and couve refogada.
hints: Black beans are cooked with onion, garlic, bay leaf and orange
Banana da terra frita replaces pork sausages
The couve —coal curly— is fried in garlic and served as an accompaniment
São Paulo has restaurants specializing in modern vegetarian feijoada
It is as tasty as traditional because of the aromatic background of well seasoned beans

regular:859.name: Caldeirão de Peixe
regular:859.desc: Northeastern fish stew with coconut milk, inhame and cheiro pepper.
hints: The inhame — yams — gives consistency and starch to the caldeirão
The pepper of aromatic but not very spicy cheiro gives the nordestino seal
Maranhão and Piauí are the states best known for this preparation
Coconut broth gives it the creaminess that differentiates it from other stews
Served on white rice with farofa dendê next to it

regular:860.name: Cururu de Camarão
regular:860.desc: Shrimp cooked with amendoim — peanuts — and dendê in thick sauce, from the Bay.
hints: The amendoim — peanuts— toasted and ground thickened the sauce naturally
The dendê gives it the orange color and the African aroma so characteristic
It is one of the oldest stews in Bahia's Afrobahian cuisine
It is served with white rice and moqueca vegetables as an accompaniment
It's different from the bobó in which it uses peanut instead of cassava as a thickening base

regular:861.name: Pão Francês com Manteiga
regular:861.desc: The French crocante bread spread with butter, the most consumed breakfast in the country.
hints: Brazil is the largest consumer of French pão in the world
The crispy shell and fluffy crumb are its main features
It is always spread with butter of can or margarine, never cold
The Brazilian breakfast without pão francês com manteiga is inconceivable
Bakeries open at 5am for workers

regular:862.name: Strogonofe Brasileiro
regular:862.desc: Estroganoff de carne o frango con champignons y creme de leite, version Brazilian with ketchup.
hints: The Brazilian version has ketchup and mustard, different from the original Russian
Creme de leite thicke the sauce until very creamy and soft
São Paulo adopted it as a daily dish in the 20th century by European influence
Served with white rice and sweet potato palma — straw potatoes — on top crispy
The Frenchman — chicken— replaces beef in the lightest popular version

regular:863.name: Acarajé da Bahia
regular:863.desc: Fried ball of feijão fradinho pasta with dry shrimp and vatapa on top, Afro-Baaian ritual dish.
hints: The feijão fradinho — black-eyed chicharo — is ground raw for the dough
It is fried in dendê oil that gives it the intense orange color and aroma
The vatapa and the dry camera are the most classic filling inside
It is a ritual food dedicated to Iansã in the Afrobahian candomblé
Baianas de acarajé sell in Salvador street stalls dressed in white

regular:864.name: Coxinha Cremosa
regular:864.desc: Thigh-shaped chicken croquette, stuffed with garnet torn with catupiry.
hints: The shape of chicken thigh gives it the name coxinha in Portuguese
Catupiry is a Brazilian cream cheese that mixes with chicken
It empties twice so that the outside is very crispy when frying
São Paulo has it as the state's best-selling bakery snack
The mandioquinha dough — yellow papa— gives you the special texture

regular:865.name: Torresmo Crocante
regular:865.desc: Fried pork chicharrón until very crispy, accompanied by feijão.
hints: The turret is fried twice — first down and then at high temperature —
The result is a chicharrón very inflated and crispy like rice shells
It is the irreplaceable accompaniment of feijoada and tutu mineiro
Minas Gerais has the country’s most deeply rooted turret tradition
Sprinkle thick salt when coming out of the oil so that it adheres better

regular:866.name: Empadão de Frango
regular:866.desc: Chicken cake with catupiry and palmite in wheat dough, covered and baked.
hints: Catupyry and palm within give you the creaminess and tropical flavor
The dough of wheat with butter completely covers the filling up and down
Bake until browned with varnished egg gem on top
It is the most popular party cake of anniversaries in São Paulo
The palm gives it the fibrous texture that contrasts with the creaminess of catupyry

regular:867.name: Arroz com Pequi
regular:867.desc: Rice cooked with pequi (closed fruit) and chicken, typical dish of Goiás and Minas.
hints: The pequi is a fruit of Brazilian closed with very intense and unique flavor
Goiás and northern Minas Gerais are the ones who consume it the most daily
The small thorny core of the pequi should not be bitten when eating
Only a small pequi fruit perfumes an entire pot of rice
It is the most beloved identity dish of the interior of central-western Brazil

regular:868.name: Farofa de Ovo
regular:868.desc: Toast cassava flour with scrambled egg, bacon and onion, the most basic farofa.
hints: farofa is cassava flour toasted in oil or butter
The scrambled egg and bacon are mixed with cassava flour
It is the indispensable accompaniment of the churrasco and the Brazilian feijoada
It can be made with any additional ingredients: banana, carrot, olives
The granular texture of the farofa absorbs the juices of roast meat

regular:869.name: Fugazza Argentina
regular:869.desc: High pizza with fluffy dough covered only with onion and oregano, without cheese or sauce.
hints: Fuguezza does not carry tomato or cheese, only onion in abundance
Buenos Aires claims it as its own pizza and identity
Onion can be put raw or caramelized according to preference
The dough is taller and fluffy than the original Italian Neapolitan
The fuozetta version carries cheese inside but not on the surface

regular:870.name: Locro Porteño
regular:870.desc: Thick stew of white corn, porots, pumpkin and pork meat, dish of 25 May.
hints: 25 May and 9 July are the national days of the locro porteño
White maize — locro — cooked for hours until disposed
The porotos — beans—and the pumpkin give the thick body to the stew
Red chorizo and patí are the most used meats in locro
The Argentine Northwest—Tucumán, Salta—has the most authentic versions

regular:871.name: Milanesa de Pollo
regular:871.desc: Fillet of chicken breast empanado and fried, the most popular alternative to beef.
hints: The crushed chicken breast is packed into egg and breadcrumbs
It is the lightest and cheapest variant of Milanese classic res
Buenos Aires serves it in rotiserías with chips or salad
Children and adults prefer it because it is more tender than beef
It can be made to Neapolitan also: with tomato, ham and cheese

regular:872.name: Pollo con Papas al Verdeo
regular:872.desc: Baked chicken with potatoes and greenish onion sauce, Sunday home dish.
hints: The chicken is baked on a potato bed in pieces with olive oil
The green onion — onion— is chopped and added in the last few minutes
Chicken juice and potatoes form a natural baking sauce
It is the simplest and most loved baking dish in the Buenos Aires kitchen
You can add morrons and garlic to taste for more flavor

regular:873.name: Asado de Cerdo con Chimichurri
regular:873.desc: Grilled pork cuts with parsley chimichurri, garlic and oregano.
hints: The pig in Argentina roasts with the same mastery as the vaccine beef
Parsley chimichurri, garlic, oregano and vinegar accompany the pig
Bondiola and pork vacuum are the most popular grilled cuts
The free-bred Patagonian pig has the best quality in the country
It is consumed especially in the winter due to increased fat availability

regular:874.name: Milanesa con Huevo
regular:874.desc: Milanese served with two fried eggs on top as breakfast or quick dish porteño.
hints: The mirror fried egg is placed directly on the hot Milanese
It is the late breakfast dish of the weekends in Buenos Aires
Eating without fries to make the egg the protagonist
The still lifes of Buenos Aires serve it as a midday economic dish
The egg yolk that breaks over the Milanese is the best time

regular:875.name: Chipá Argentino
regular:875.desc: Manioc starch bread with cheese, Guaraní heritage of the Argentine Northeast.
hints: It is very similar to Paraguayan chipa in ingredients and preparation
The Argentine Northeast—Corrientes, Misiones—adopted it from the Guaraní
The cheese is mixed directly into the dried manioc starch
Bake until golden on the outside and very elastic and soft inside
It is the snack of collective trips in the Argentine Northeast

regular:876.name: Dulce de Batata Argentino
regular:876.desc: Solid sweet potato pasta — sweet potato — with sugar and lemon, a pair of milk dulce.
hints: The cooked sweet potato is ground and cooked with sugar until solidified
Lemon gives the acidity that balances sweetness of sweet potato
Eating with fresh cheese or cream cheese in the most rioplatense dessert
Argentina exports it as the finest sweet potato on the continent
Used as filling of sweet empanadas and Christmas cakes

regular:877.name: Empanadas Santiagueñas
regular:877.desc: Empanadas de Santiago del Estero with meat, hard egg and raisins, baked or fried.
hints: Santiago del Estero has one of the oldest empanadas traditions
The raisins inside are the sweet touch that distinguishes them from other provinces
The repulgue—closing the dough—is different and very elaborate in this province
They can be baked or fried according to the regional preference of the North
Cumin and paprika are the spices that most aromatize the filling

regular:878.name: Asado de Cabrito
regular:878.desc: Whole goat roasted to the stick or grill, dish of arid valleys from the northwest.
hints: La Rioja and San Juan are the most famous states of the roasted kid
The kid roasts himself whole to the horizontal stick on wood embers
Thick salt is the only seasoning needed for this austere dish
The taste is more intense and gamey than the lamb for being younger
Served with lettuce salad and olive oil as the only accompaniment

regular:879.name: Tortilla Española Porteña
regular:879.desc: Spanish style potato and egg tortilla adapted to the Buenos Aires cuisine.
hints: Spanish immigration brought the tortilla to Buenos Aires in the 19th century
It's the same as Spanish: potatoes in oil and beaten eggs
The Bonanese always add onion, unlike the Spanish purists
It is eaten cold or tempered in a snack or as an entrance dish
The warehouses and rotisseries of the Gran Buenos Aires sell it all day

regular:880.name: Guiso de Fideos con Estofado
regular:880.desc: Short noodles stewed in tomato sauce with stewed meat and vegetables.
hints: It is the most comforting stew of the cold nights of winter Buenos Aires
The noodles are cooked directly in the sauce to absorb the flavor
The meat of stew — morcillo or buttocks — is cooked first and shredded
It is the dish of Wednesdays in Buenos Aires family cuisine by tradition
You can add grated cheese on top when serving according to family

regular:881.name: Cazuela de Mondongo Porteño
regular:881.desc: Mondongo —streets— stewed with vegetables, potatoes and chickpeas in broth, winter dish.
hints: The calluses are cleaned very well before cooking for hours
The chickpeas and potatoes give the body and consistency to the stew
The paprika and cumin are the most characteristic spices of mondongo porteño
Buenos Aires eats it especially in winter in traditional still lifes
It is a very popular dish among the workers of the capital's markets

regular:882.name: Pastafrola de Membrillo
regular:882.desc: Broken dough cake with quince sweet and lattice, dominguero dessert.
hints: The broken butter dough is partially baked before filling
The solid and dark quince sweet is the most classic filling in the country
The grating of strips of dough on top is the visual signature of pastafrola
It is the dessert of mate and weed on Sundays throughout Argentina
Also made with sweet potato or guava depending on the region

regular:883.name: Churrasco Porteño
regular:883.desc: Fine fillet of grilled beef served in snack with chimichurri and lettuce.
hints: The Argentine churrasco is a meat sandwich in French bread
Parsley chimichurri, garlic and vinegar is the sauce that cannot be missed
It is sold in the kiosks and cafes of Buenos Aires 24 hours
It is the most popular street sandwich in Buenos Aires
Meat is grilled over maximum heat for a few minutes

regular:884.name: Noquis del 29
regular:884.desc: Potato Ñoquis with tomato sauce and cheese, eaten on the 29th of each month with silver underneath.
hints: Tradition says you eat noquis on the 29th of every month for prosperity
You put money or bills under the plate before you eat for good luck
The Italian recipe came with the massive nineteenth century peninsular immigration
Buenos Aires has the best fresh pasta gnoceries on the continent
The tomato and basil fillet sauce is the most traditional to accompany

regular:885.name: Matambre de Cerdo
regular:885.desc: Grilled pork skirt, more tender and faster to cook than beef skirt.
hints: Pork slaughter is the thinnest cut of the animal's flank
It is cheaper and faster to cook than beef slaughter
Grilled over high heat for a few minutes on each side
Buenos Aires and the coast prefer it to that of beef for its affordable price
Served with salad and chimichurri like any other roasted cut

regular:886.name: Tomaticán Norteño
regular:886.desc: Tomato stew with choclo, meat and Andean spices, from northwestern Argentina.

The choclo in sweet grains gives you contrast and natural sweetness
Tucumán and Salta consume it more frequently in hot summer

regular:887.name: Humita en Chala
regular:887.desc: Pasta of choclo fresh with onion and basil, wrapped in leaf of choclo steamed.

regular:888.name: Arvejas Guisadas con Jamón
regular:888.desc: Fresh peas stewed with cooked ham, onion and tomato, Chilean summer garnish.

Onion and tomato are first fried to create the base of the stew
It is the most popular garrison when peas are in your station
Served with white rice as an accompaniment to any roast

regular:889.name: Pescado a la Mantequilla
regular:889.desc: Fish fillet — hazelnut or queen — sautéed in butter with lemon and parsley.

Served with rice or cooked potatoes and simple tomato salad

regular:890.name: Cazuela de Pescado
regular:890.desc: Rock fish broth with potatoes, pumpkin and cilantro, marine version of the casserole.
hints: Rockfish — Cabrilla, old — gives you the most concentrated broth

regular:891.name: Sopa de Mariscos del Litoral
regular:891.desc: Thick broth of seafood varied with cream, potatoes and chili pepper color, comforting Chilean.

regular:891.displayName: Seafood Soup of the Coastal Sea

regular:892.name: Anticucho Chileno
regular:892.desc: Heart brochetas of cattle marinated in ají panca and vinegar, Peruvian heritage in Chile.

regular:893.name: Caldo de Cordero Chileno

regular:894.name: Ensalada de Porotos con Choclo

regular:895.name: Cazuela de Cerdo
regular:895.desc: Pork rib broth with potato, choclo and Zapallo, swine variant of the casserole.

The choclo sliced and the zapallo in squares are the most characteristic vegetables

regular:896.name: Budín de Pan Casero
regular:896.desc: Mould bread Budin soaked in milk, egg and sugar, baked with caramel.

The beaten eggs give you the structure that curds when baking in bath maria

It is the most home-made dessert of Chilean grandmothers

regular:897.name: Empanada de Mariscos
regular:897.desc: Chilean empanada baked stuffed with various seafood with onion and ají.
hints: The port of Valparaiso is the most famous place to eat seafood empanadas

The poached onion slowly gives the sweet base to the marine filling
Bake the same as pine pie until golden and crispy
It is the most valued seafood alternative in Chilean coastal empanadas

regular:898.name: Guatitas con Papas
regular:898.desc: Beef calluses in tomato sauce with potato, onion and paprika, popular stew.

The potatoes in cubes are added the last 20 minutes so they don't get undone

Santiago has specialized posts in potatoes and guitas in the markets

regular:899.name: Pan Amasado Chileno
regular:899.desc: Homemade flour bread kneaded with lard and salt, baked in clay oven.
hints: The lard gives you the fluffy crumb and the flavor that makes it unique
The clay or wood oven gives you the ideal crispy bark

You eat hot fresh out of the oven with butter or potato
Rural communities in southern Chile do so every weekend

regular:900.name: Encebollado de Atún
regular:900.desc: Fresh tuna soup with yucca, tomato, onion and cilantro, the Ecuadorian coastal breakfast.

regular:901.name: Seco de Pollo Ecuatoriano
regular:901.desc: Chicken stewed in black beer, tomato, naranjilla and spices, the serrano party dish.

The Ecuadorian Sierra — Quito, Cuenca— Considers It Its Celebration Discourse

regular:902.name: Yahuarlocro
regular:902.desc: Soup of potatoes with blood of sheep, guita and dressing, very special Andean dish of Quito.

regular:903.name: Llapingacho Serrano
regular:903.desc: Potato tortilla pressed with fresh cheese, golden in butter on the griddle.

regular:904.name: Caldo de Bagre Ecuatoriano
regular:904.desc: Cattle broth of the river with potato, green banana, cilantro and aji, from the Amazon.

regular:905.name: Sancocho de Gallina Ecuatoriano
regular:905.desc: Creole hen soup with yucca, banana, potato and cilantro, dish of celebration costaño.

regular:906.name: Tostado de Maíz
regular:906.desc: Dry corn toasted in butter or oil with salt, crispy Ecuadorian Andean snack.

regular:907.name: Ceviche de Concha Negra

The red pepper pepper gives the itching and color to the ceviche very fresh
Esmeraldas and the North Pacific are the best places to eat it fresh
Served in the shell of the shell for presentation

regular:908.name: Chupe de Pescado Ecuatoriano
regular:908.desc: Creamy soup of fish with potato, milk, cheese, chili and cilantro, from the south coast.

The fresh fish of the Ecuadorian Pacific is the main protagonist
The provinces of Loja and Gold have the most creamy and famous versions
Serve very hot with yucca bread or corn tortillas next to it

regular:909.name: Ají de Cuy
regular:909.desc: Cuy roasted in chili sauce and toasted peanut, festive dish of the Ecuadorian mountains.

The ají amarillo sauce and peanuts bathe it completely when serving
Latacunga and Riobamba are the most famous cities for roasting

regular:910.name: Rosero Quiteño
regular:910.desc: Cold drink of cooked fruits —bacco, naranjilla, pineapple— with starch and cinnamon, from parties.

Cold served with ice after completely cooling in the refrigerator

regular:911.name: Bollo de Pescado Manabita
regular:911.desc: Maize stuffed with shredded fish cooked in steamed banana leaf.

The ground corn dough wraps the fish before wrapping in the leaf

regular:912.name: Caldo de Pollo Quiteño

regular:913.name: Tigrillo de Verde
regular:913.desc: Grated green banana mixed with scrambled egg and cheese, breakfast from southern Ecuador.

Loja and the south of the country are the ones who consume the most green ring

It is eaten accompanied by black coffee or hot corn laundry at breakfast

regular:914.name: Pollo en Pepitoria Cubana
regular:914.desc: Chicken stewed in an egg-yolk, almond and saffron sauce, a Spanish culinary legacy in Cuba.

regular:915.name: Fricasé de Pollo Cubano

regular:916.name: Ropa Vieja con Garbanzos

regular:917.name: Congri Oriental

regular:918.name: Tostones al Ajo

regular:919.name: Malanga Frita Cubana

regular:920.name: Chicharrón de Pollo Cubano

regular:921.name: Arroz con Pollo Habanero

regular:922.name: Huevos Habaneros

regular:923.name: Ensalada Cubana de Aguacate

regular:924.name: Dulce de Naranja Cubano

regular:925.name: Tamal Cubano en Cazuela

regular:926.name: Lechón Asado Cubano

regular:927.name: Papas con Mojo Cubano

regular:928.name: Sofrito Boricua

regular:929.name: Pasteles de Masa Boricua

regular:930.name: Pollo Guisado Boricua

regular:931.name: Mofongo con Camarones

regular:932.name: Pernil Boricua

regular:933.name: Gandinga con Arroz

regular:934.name: Tortitas de Plátano Maduro

regular:935.name: Arroz con Pollo Boricua

regular:937.name: Majarete de Coco Boricua

regular:938.name: Alcapurria de Jueyes

regular:939.name: Sopa de Plátano Verde

regular:940.name: Sancocho Boricua

regular:941.name: Pana Frita Boricua

regular:942.name: Coquito Navideño

regular:943.name: Pepián de Res
