Cocoa powder gives you the bitterness and depth typical of Mayan cuisine
The guajillo chili gives the intense red color and smoked flavor to broth
The Petén and northern Guatemala have the oldest documented versions
It is one of the oldest pre-Hispanic dishes in Central American gastronomy

regular:949.name: Recado Rojo Guatemalteco
regular:949.desc: Thick pasta of dried chilies, tomato and spices to season tamales and stews.
hints: Red errand is the most important flavor base of Guatemalan cuisine
Dried chilies — guajillo and mulatto — are roasted before being ground
Roast tomato is mixed with chilies and achiote for pasta
It can be stored in the refrigerator for weeks to season stews and tamales
It is as important in Guatemala as the sofrito in Cuban or Venezuelan cuisine

regular:950.name: Champurradas Guatemaltecas
regular:950.desc: Hard cookies of corn and wheat with sesame, the Guatemalan breakfast cookies.
hints: The sesame is the visual signature of these Guatemalan cookies
Bake until very hard to last days without getting soft
They are bigger and harder than any other cookie in the region
Wet in black coffee or hot chocolate to soften them
They are the breakfast of market days and festivities all over the country

regular:951.name: Guacamol de Chipilín
regular:951.desc: Crushed avocado mixed with chipillin — grass — lemon, onion and serrano pepper.
hints: The chipilin gives the intense green color and Andean aroma to this variant
It is a Guatemalan version of the classic guacamole with local grass
The serrano pepper gives you the fresh itching that complements the chipilin
Served as tortilla sauce, toast and meat accompaniment
It is completely different in aroma to the Mexican guacamole by chipilín

regular:952.name: Pepita en Dulce
regular:952.desc: pumpkin seeds in panela syrup with cinnamon, sweet Guatemalan dessert handmade.
hints: The pumpkin seeds are cooked in panela syrup until caramelized
Cinnamon cracked gives the sweet aroma throughout the cooking
It is the sweetest artisan of Guatemalan indigenous markets
It is sold in the markets of Chichicastenango and Antigua Guatemala
Each region has its own version with different proportion of panela and cinnamon

regular:953.name: Pollo en Amarillo
regular:953.desc: Chicken in yellow tomato sauce, miltomate, chili and corn dough, Guatemalan national dish.
hints: Yellow chicken is one of the eight recognized national dishes in Guatemala
The corn dough dissolves in the broth thickening the sauce naturally
Tomato and miltomate — tomatillo — form the yellow acid base
It's different from mole in not bringing chocolate or so many complex spices
The dried chili gives it the deep flavor without excessive itching of other stews

regular:954.name: Rellenitos Guatemaltecos
regular:954.desc: Mature crushed banana pellets stuffed with sweet black bean, fried in oil.
hints: The ripe cooked banana is crushed to make the outer sweet cover
Black beans are cooked with sugar to make sweet filling
They are formed in oval with the filling of sweet beans inside the banana
They fry until browned on the outside and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon on top
They are Guatemala City's most popular street dessert in the markets

regular:955.name: Tortitas de Yuca Guatemaltecas
regular:955.desc: Juice cakes grated with cheese and parrot, fried until crispy.
hints: The raw grated cassava forms the base of these crispy and simple pancakes
The parrot — edible flower— gives it the most Central American aroma of the dish
Fresh cheese is mixed inside the cassava dough before frying
Hot freshly fried with homemade tomato sauce next door
They are similar to Salvadoran pancakes in ingredients but thicker

regular:956.name: Tamal de Elote Dulce Guatemalteco
regular:956.desc: Tamal sweet tender corn with sugar and cinnamon, wrapped in corn leaf, festive dessert.
hints: The tender corn is ground raw to make the dough sweet and fluffy
Cinnamon and sugar are the only flavorings, without additional filling
They are smaller than the tamales salted and prepare for dessert
They are sold especially at the patron saint festivals and November
The steam leaves them very humid and soft, completely different from the salty ones

regular:957.name: Caldo de Costilla Guatemalteco
regular:957.desc: Breed rib broth with güisquil, potato, carrot and mint, market breakfast.
hints: Guatemala City markets have been serving it since 4 a.m
The beef rib gives you the most gelatinous and nutritious broth to start the day
Güisquil — chayote — is Guatemala’s most representative vegetable in the stock
Fresh mint at the end is the scent that distinguishes it from any other broth
It is served with corn tortillas and spicy chile chamborote next door always

regular:958.name: Pampaku Boliviano
regular:958.desc: Cooking meats and potatoes underground with hot stones, Bolivian version of curanto.
hints: It is the Bolivian version of underground cooking with hot stones
The stones are heated to bright red before being placed in the earth hole
Meats, potatoes and vegetables are wrapped and put on hot stones
It is a pre-Hispanic technique of the Bolivian Andean peoples
The rural communities of the highlands prepare it for agricultural festivals and rituals

regular:959.name: Thimpu de Cordero
regular:959.desc: Lamb slowly cooked with potatoes, chuño and veggies in broth, from the Bolivian highlands.
hints: The lamb of the altiplano is the most tasty for the hard pastures it eats
The chuño — dehydrated dad — gives you the most Andean texture and flavor
It cooks for hours until the meat leaves the bone alone
La Paz and the Bolivian highlands are the ones who consume it most daily
It is the most powerful and nutritious lamb soup in the Bolivian Andes

regular:960.name: Saice de Tarija
regular:960.desc: Ground beef stew with onion, tomato and cumin, typical Tarija dish in southern Bolivia.
hints: Tarija, the southernmost and most viniferous city of Bolivia, is the cradle of the saice
The ground meat is cooked in sofrito onion and tomato with enough cumin
Served with white rice, cooked potato and tomato salad always
It is the most consumed daily dish in Tarija city at noon
The Tarragona cumin has a special intensity because of the valluno climate

regular:961.name: Revuelto de Charqui
regular:961.desc: Dried llama meat — charqui — melted with potato, onion and tomato, scrambled Andean.
hints: The charqui flame has a more intense flavor than that of beef or pork
The dried meat is melted after hydrating it for hours in water
Onion and tomato are fried with meat to make the stir
The Bolivian highlands use charqui as they have been preserved since pre-Hispanic times
It is the most popular protein breakfast in rural highland communities

regular:962.name: Lawa de Chuño
regular:962.desc: chuño thick soup — dehydrated potato — with fresh cheese and good grass, from the highlands.
hints: chuño dehydrated is first hydrated in cold water before use
The soup is very thick and grayy for the chuño cooked in the broth
Fresh Andean cheese is broken into the hot soup
The mint gives you the fresh aroma that balances the intense flavor of chuño
Potosí and Oruro are the cities that consume this Andean soup the most

regular:963.name: Sopa de Maní Cochabambina
regular:963.desc: Roasted peanut soup ground with potatoes, rice and beef, Cochabamba dish.
hints: Cochabamba is the gastronomic capital of Bolivia and the cradle of this soup
The roasted and ground peanut is the base that thickens the broth naturally
Rice and potatoes are cooked directly in the peanut stock
The beef in pieces is added at first to give flavor to the broth
It is the most popular soup on the Cochabambino menu in local restaurants

regular:964.name: Fritanga Cruceña
regular:964.desc: Fried pork with locoto, onion, tomato and potato, festive dish of Santa Cruz de la Sierra.
hints: Santa Cruz de la Sierra in the Bolivian tropical east is its cradle
The madoto—spicy Andean pepper—gives it the heat that distinguishes the fritanga cruzena
The pork is fried in large pieces with the skin included
It is served at the patron saint festivals and celebrations of Santa Cruz
It is different from the Ecuadorian fritted by locoto and oriental spices

regular:965.name: Picante Mixto Boliviano
regular:965.desc: Combination of chicken, cuy and rabbit in spicy sauce of red aji and peanut, festive.
hints: The mixed spicy blends three different proteins into the same hot sauce
The red aji — Bolivian dry pepper— gives it the itching and intense red color
The roasted peanut gives the creaminess and body to the thick sauce
Sucre and Cochabamba are the cities where most is consumed in celebrations
It is the dish of weddings and most important parties in the Bolivian interior

regular:966.name: Yuca Frita Boliviana
regular:966.desc: Yuca cooked and then fried until golden, a popular garrison of eastern Bolivia.
hints: The cassava boils first until tender before frying
Santa Cruz de la Sierra consumes it as the most popular and economic garrison
Served with hot locoto lajua sauce to wet each piece
The crispy texture on the outside and creamy inside makes it very satisfying
It is the most common alternative to potato chips in tropical eastern Bolivia

regular:967.name: Jallpawayca
regular:967.desc: Bolivian locoto sauce roasted with tomato and onion, the most popular lajua of the highlands.
hints: Llajua is the irreplaceable hot sauce of any Bolivian dish
The locoto —a fleshy and spicy bolivian ji— is roasted before grinding it
Fresh tomato and onion grind together with roasted locoto
It grinds in batan — grinding stone— to achieve the right rough texture
There is no Bolivian table without the locoto lajua to the center for all dishes

regular:968.name: Tawa Tawa Boliviana
regular:968.desc: Fried flour dough in the form of a bow, covered with sugar and anise, Bolivian candy.
hints: The dough of flour with anise is formed in loops or rings before frying
Fry in hot oil until golden brown and cover with sugar
They are the sweet of carnival parties in Oruro and La Paz especially
Sold in bags on the streets during Bolivian Carnival in February
Anise gives you the most characteristic aroma of this traditional treat

regular:969.name: Papas Licchi
regular:969.desc: Small potatoes cooked in charqui broth with locoto, onion and Andean herbs.
hints: Small Andean potatoes —imillas or huaycha — are cooked whole in the broth
The charqui gives the salty and protein background to simple potato broth
The fresh spicy locoto is added in pieces to give the Andean heat
It is a dish of the most humble and ancient cuisine of the Bolivian high plateau
It is eaten especially in the peasant markets and rural communities of the highlands

regular:970.name: Chicharrón de Mondongo
regular:970.desc: Mondongo of fried beef until it is crispy, appetizers from the markets of Cochabamba.
hints: The mondongo —streets— is cooked first until it is ground and then fried
The result is a slice of mondongo crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside
Cochabamba sells it in the markets as a morning snack
It is accompanied with locoto lajua and white mote on the plate
It is the most economical and popular appetizer in Bolivian popular markets

regular:971.name: Plátano Pasado
regular:971.desc: Mature banana roasted or fried in butter with sugar, simple dessert from eastern Bolivia.
hints: The very mature banana is roasted whole in shell in the embers or baked
Upon opening it has the creamy and sweet flesh completely caramelized
Santa Cruz eats it as dessert or snack in the heat of the tropics
You can sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon when you eat it hot
It is the simplest and most natural dessert in tropical eastern Bolivia

regular:972.name: Sancocho Prieto Dominicano
regular:972.desc: Sancocho dark with three meats, vegetables, Dominican spices and tomato paste.
hints: The sancocho prieto —dark— is made with tomato paste that dyes it
Bring chicken, beef and pork cooked together in the same dark broth
El ají cubanela and el colantro Dominicana are irreplaceable aromatics
It is the sancocho most elaborate holiday in all Dominican cuisine
It is prepared for special celebrations such as weddings and quinceañera birthdays

regular:973.name: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
regular:973.desc: Green banana puree with pickled red onion, fried eggs, fried cheese and salami.
hints: The three strokes are fried egg, fried cheese and fried salami
The mangú is made by grinding the green plantain cooked with oil and hot water
The red onion pickled in vinegar is put on top of mangú only
It is the Dominican national breakfast par excellence, unmatched
The Dominican salami is a very particular flavor sausage and spicy

regular:974.name: Habichuelas Guisadas
regular:974.desc: Red beans stewed in sofrito Dominicana with auyama and Caribbean spices.
hints: The red beans are cooked with sofrito cilantro, chili pepper and tomato
The auyama —calabaza— gives the sweetness and thicken the broth of beans
They are always served with white rice as inseparable accompaniment
It is the dish of Dominican noon: rice, beans, meat and salad
Each Dominican home has its own secret seasoning for beans

regular:975.name: Pollo Asado con Sazón
regular:975.desc: Chicken marinated in Dominican season with sour orange, garlic and oregano, roasted in the oven.
hints: Sour orange — sour orange — penetrates the meat during marinating
The dried Dominican oregano has a more intense flavor than the imported dry
Sail at least 24 hours before roasting in the oven at medium temperature
It is the Sunday chicken that is accompanied with rice and green salad
The Dominican seasoning based on aji, onion and cilantro is the base of marinade

regular:976.name: Sancocho de Siete Carnes
regular:976.desc: The most elaborate version of the sancocho Dominican with seven types of meat together.
hints: The seven meats may vary but always include beef, chicken and pork
It is the dish of the biggest parties: weddings, fifteen years and baptisms
It takes several hours to cook for the quantity and variety of meats
It is the sancocho most expensive and elaborate of all Dominican cuisine
Served in large dishes with a representation of each meat included

regular:977.name: Bizcocho Dominicano
regular:977.desc: Wet birthday cake covered in Italian merengue, the Dominican party cake.
hints: Italian sugar meringue and egg white is classic coverage
The cake is moist and fluffy, very different from the American dry cake
Every Dominican birthday has its cake as a mandatory central element
The bakery that makes the best cake in a community is highly valued
Decorates with meringue flowers and brightly colored fruits always

regular:978.name: Chivo Liniero
regular:978.desc: Chivo del Cibao cooked in vinegar, oregano and chijí gentleman, festive dish of the north.
hints: The Cibao, northern region of the island, is famous for its best breeding goat
White vinegar is used to soften and remove the strong smell of goat
The Dominican oregano and the knight ají (very spicy) are irreplaceable
It is the most expected dish of the patron saintly celebrations of the Dominican north
Santiago de los Caballeros has the best restaurants of chivo liniero

regular:979.name: Tostones Dominicanos
regular:979.desc: Green banana fried and crushed twice, the most Dominican side of lunch.
hints: They fry first, crush with the toston-presser and fry again
The second frying gives them the crispy crust that makes them perfect
Served with garlic mojo or crushed avocado as a companion
They're the Dominican lunch garnish just like American fries
The Dominican green banana is larger and has the perfect texture for toast

regular:980.name: Arroz con Coco Dominicano
regular:980.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with raisins, sugar and cinnamon, Easter dessert.
hints: Coconut milk replaces water completely in rice cooking
Sweet raisins give extra texture and natural sweetness
Fresh grated ginger gives it the spicy touch that sets it apart
It is the most consumed Easter dessert on the island
Cold served with powdered cinnamon generously sprinkled on top

regular:981.name: Locrio de Longaniza
regular:981.desc: Rice cooked with Dominican longaniza, sofrito and spices, the sausage locrio.
hints: The Dominican longaniza is a very spicy and spicy sausage
It cooks just like the chicken locrium but with the sliced longaniza
The sofrito of cilantro, tomato and aji cobanela is the aromatic base
It is the cheapest and fastest locrium to prepare of all kinds
Dominicans prepare it when the budget does not give for chicken or fish

regular:982.name: Casabe con Queso
regular:982.desc: Yucca cake with Dominican white cheese on top, fast and tasty snack of the island.
hints: The casabe crispy serves as the basis for white cheese melting on top
Dominican white cheese is soft and moist, different from dry cheese
Heats in frying pan or microwave so the cheese melts well
It is the fastest and cheapest snack in Dominican homes
You can also spread butter or avocado crushed on top

regular:983.name: Pollo Guisado con Papas
regular:983.desc: Chicken in Creole sauce with cooked potatoes inside, the most homemade Dominican chicken stew.
hints: Potatoes are cooked directly in the Creole sauce next to chicken
The sofrito Dominicans with cilantro and aji cubanela is the basis of the taste
It is served with white rice and fried banana as an accompaniment always
It is the most cooked lunch dish in Dominican homes day to day
The achiote seasoning gives you the golden color and Caribbean flavor

regular:984.name: Ensalada de Coditos
regular:984.desc: Macaroni cooked with mayonnaise, ham, carrot and beetroot, Dominican party salad.
hints: The elbows — macaroni — are mixed with abundant mayonnaise after cooling
The beet dyes the whole salad of a bright pink or magenta color
The cubed ham and grated carrot complete the filling
It is the salad of Dominican parties, weddings and family reunions
Prepares with one day in advance for all flavors to mix well

regular:985.name: Fritura de Yuca Dominicana
regular:985.desc: Yuca cooked in sticks and fried until crispy, popular Dominican aperitif.
hints: The cassava is boiled first until tender before being cut into sticks
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy on the outside
Served with garlic mojo or spicy mayonnaise as dip for wetting
It is the most popular fry in Dominican bars and crowded neighborhoods
Yuca fryings are sold in street stalls across the country

regular:986.name: Rabas Fritas
regular:986.desc: Squid rings overflowed and fried to crispy, top of the Montevidean bars.
hints: The squid is cut into rings and packed in flour before frying in hot oil
The lemon squeezed above is the irreplaceable condiment of Uruguayan rabas
It is the most requested bar top in the restaurants of Puerto de Montevideo
They are accompanied with garlic mayonnaise or golf sauce to wet each hoop
The key is very hot oil to make them crispy and non-greasy

regular:987.name: Sopa de Cebolla Uruguaya
regular:987.desc: Caramelized onion soup with beef broth and gratin cheese on top of the Montevidean bistro.
hints: The onion cooks slowly for 45 minutes until it is completely caramelized
The concentrated beef broth gives the depth to the taste of dark soup
Mozzarella cheese gratina on top in the oven until golden and melted
The bistros of the Montevideo Center have it in letter all year long
It is of French heritage, brought by 19th century European immigrants

regular:988.name: Estofado de Cordero Uruguayo
regular:988.desc: Lamb stewed with vegetables, red wine and herbs, the stew of stays.
hints: Uruguay has one of the best lambs in the world for its pastures
Uruguayan Tannat red wine gives depth and dark color to the stew
Root vegetables — zanahoria, turnips — are cooked next to the lamb
It is the dish of cattle ranches in the interior of the country during winter
Served with creamy polenta or white rice to absorb dark sauce

regular:989.name: Empanadas Fritas Uruguayas
regular:989.desc: Fries in oil until golden browned, stuffed with meat or ham and cheese.
hints: Fry in plenty of hot oil until completely golden
The filling of ground meat with hard egg and olive is the most traditional
The version of ham and cheese is the fastest and cheapest to prepare
Montevideo sells them in rotiserías and small bars as street snack
They are more crispy and juicy than the baked empanadas by oil

regular:990.name: Postre Chajá
regular:990.desc: Biscuits with cream Chantilly, merengue and peaches in syrup, dessert of Paysandú.
hints: Paysandú, the city of Uruguay, is the official cradle of Chajá dessert
The sponge cake and whipped cream are the main layers
Peaches in syrup give you the moisture and bittersweet fruity flavor
The crispy dry meringue contrasts with the moist cream inside
It is called Chaja by the Uruguayan wild bird of fluffy plumage

regular:991.name: Asado de Tira Uruguayo
regular:991.desc: Cross-cut ribs, slowly roasted with thick salt.
hints: Uruguay cuts ribs as well as Argentina, transversally
Sea salt is the only seasoning that needs this cut
Cook patiently for at least 90 minutes over moderate heat
Uruguayan cattle from natural pastures produce high quality meat
Served as a main course of roasting with chimichurri and creolla salad

regular:992.name: Fideos a la Manteca
regular:992.desc: Spaghetti cooked with butter, garlic and grated Parmesan cheese, simple and popular dish.
hints: Quality butter is the key to this simple but tasty dish
Laminated garlic is fried in butter before mixing with pasta
Parmesan grated cheese is added out of the heat so that it does not count
It is the dish of Italian immigration cuisine that was most cooked in Montevideo
Eat Tuesdays by tradition in many Uruguayan homes of Italian origin

regular:993.name: Sopa de Mondongo Uruguaya
regular:993.desc: Soup of calluses with chickpeas, vegetables and paprika, dish of the markets of Montevideo.
hints: The calluses are perfectly cleaned and cooked for hours until garnished
The chickpeas give consistency and extra protein to the broth
Sweet paprika and oregano are the spices that most aromatize it
Montevideo’s popular markets serve it on Fridays and Saturdays
It is a very popular dish among Spanish immigrants and their descendants

regular:994.name: Alfajor de Maicena
regular:994.desc: Alfajor soft cornstarch dough stuffed with sweet milk and covered in grated coconut.
hints: Cornstarch —corn starch — gives you the texture that is undone in your mouth
The rioplatense milk sweet is the classic and irreplaceable filling
The white grated coconut covers the entire exterior of the alfajor cornstarch
It's the alfajor th evening with mate in Uruguayan homes
It differs from Cordobes in that it does not bring chocolate but grated coconut

regular:995.name: Caldo de Gallina Casero
regular:995.desc: Chicken broth with fine noodles, carrot, leek and parsley, the grandmother's broth.
hints: The field hen gives you the most concentrated and gelatinous broth
The fine capellini noodles are added in the last minutes of broth
Pork and fresh parsley give you the scent that differentiates home broth
It is the dish that Uruguayan grandmothers prepare for the sick and visitors
It is served very hot in bowl with toasted bread to wet the noodles

regular:996.name: Revuelto de Zapallitos
regular:996.desc: Zapallitos — calabacines— soaked with egg, onion and grated cheese, simple vegetarian dish.
hints: The zapallitos are cut into cubes and cooked with onion until garnished
The scrambled eggs are added when the pumpkins are already cooked well
The grated cheese is incorporated at the end out of the fire so that it does not change
It is the simplest and most nutritious vegetarian dish in Uruguayan cuisine
Served with white rice or bread as light dinner accompaniment

regular:997.name: Milanesa a la Francesa
regular:997.desc: Milanese covered with caramelized onion and melted cheese, Uruguayan gourmet variant.
hints: The onion is slowly caramelized before putting on the hot Milanese
Mozzarella cheese melts on the onion in the oven or under the grill
It is the most elaborate and festive variant of Milanese in Uruguay
Pocitos restaurants in Montevideo have it as a star dish
Served with fresh salad to balance the richness of onion and cheese

regular:998.name: Mate Cocido con Galletas
regular:998.desc: Hot infusion of yerba mate cooked in pot, served with milk and water cookies.
hints: Unlike the bitter mate, the cooked mate is prepared like a potted tea
The milk is added to the weed broth to soften the bitterness
It is the most popular breakfast of Uruguayans who do not want bitter mate
The crispy water cookies are the accompaniment that never misses
It is softer and more accessible for those who are not used to bitter mate

regular:999.name: Budín de Zapallo Uruguayo
regular:999.desc: Pastel baked with cheese and eggs, served cold as an entrance or garnish.
hints: The pumpkin is steamed and crushed before mixing with the eggs
The grated cheese gives the structure and salty flavor to the vegetable pudding
Bake in mold and serve cold or at room temperature
It is a very popular entrance to Montevidean homes in spring
Garnished with cherry tomatoes and olives on top before serving

regular:1000.name: Baleada Sencilla
regular:1000.desc: Wheat flour tortilla with refried beans, cream and dry cheese, national breakfast.
hints: The flour tortilla is different from that of corn in soft and thick texture
Refried beans spread abundantly over the hot tortilla
The acidic cream and the dried cheese crumble complete the simple baleada
It is the most consumed breakfast in Honduras since 6 am
Special versions carry egg, avocado, chorizo or meat on top

regular:1001.name: Mondongo Hondureño
regular:1001.desc: Soup of corns with cassava, güisquil, potato and mint, from central Honduras.
hints: Calluses — mondongo — clean well before cooking hours
Yucca and güisquil are the most representative vegetables in Honduras
The herb gives it the fresh aroma that distinguishes the Honduran mondongo
Tegucigalpa serves it in popular fondas on Sundays early
It is the most popular recovery dish on Honduran weekends

regular:1002.name: Tapado Caribeño Hondureño
regular:1002.desc: Seafood soup with coconut milk, banana, yucca and vegetables from the Honduran Caribbean.
hints: The Ceiba and the Caribbean coast are the most famous cities for this cover
Coconut milk gives it the tropical creaminess that distinguishes it from other broths
Honduran Caribbean seafood is fresh and varied in the cover
Yucca and green plantain give the body and consistency to the stew
It is the most evident English Caribbean Garifuna influence in Honduran cuisine

regular:1003.name: Carne Asada con Chimol
regular:1003.desc: Grilled beef with tomato chimol and onion, weekend dish.
hints: Honduran chimol is a pico de gallo of tomato, onion, cilantro and lemon
The meat is grilled to the embers without marinated, only with marine thick salt
Served with rice, beans, banana slices and cabbage salad
It's Friday and Saturday dinner in popular dining rooms in Honduras
Lemon squeezed on hot meat is the most Honduran final touch

regular:1004.name: Sopa de Albóndiguitas Hondureña
regular:1004.desc: Light broth with small balls of beef and vegetables, the family broth of Tegucigalpa.
hints: Small meatballs are made with beef, rice, garlic and mint
Cook directly in the vegetable broth for 20 minutes
Potatoes, carrots and chayotes are the most common vegetables in broth
It's Sunday broth in the most humble Tegucigalpa homes
It is accompanied by freshly made corn tortillas in Honduras

regular:1005.name: Pupusas Hondureñas
regular:1005.desc: Thick corn tortilla stuffed with beans and dry cheese, Honduran version of the pupusa.
hints: They are very similar to Salvadorans but with dry cheese instead of fresh cheese
The corn dough is worked just like in El Salvador to fill and seal
They are cooked in dry griddle without oil until golden spots appear
They are accompanied with kale tanned similar to the Salvadoran but softer
Honduras adopted them as part of its daily cuisine from the neighbor

regular:1006.name: Arroz Blanco con Frijoles Negros
regular:1006.desc: White rice served with black bean broth and cream, the simplest lunch.
hints: Black beans cooked with garlic and cumin give you the darkest broth
Acid cream is served on top of beans to soften the flavor
It is the most economical and nutritious food of humble Honduran households
It is accompanied by corn tortillas and fried bananaites as garnish
The bean broth is so tasty that it serves as soup of the first dish

regular:1007.name: Sopa de Pollo Madre
regular:1007.desc: Strong chicken broth with chayotes, cobs, carrots and noodles.
hints: Whole chicken gives the most gelatinous and nutritious broth of all
The sliced cob gives the sweet flavor that cheers the broth
Fine noodles are added in the last ten minutes to not get rid of
It's Monday's broth—when there's plenty of Sunday chicken—in Honduras
Served as a unique dish with hot corn tortillas always

regular:1008.name: Tamales de Maíz Dulce Hondureño
regular:1008.desc: Tamales sweets of tender corn with cheese and cinnamon, the tamales dessert of Honduras.
hints: The tender corn ground is the base dough without any dried corn flour
Cinnamon and sugar give you the sweetness that makes them dessert
The dried cheese grated gives you the salty contrast inside the sweet dessert
They steam on corn leaf an hour like the tamales salted
Markets sell them especially during the season of fresh corn

regular:1009.name: Pinchos de Carne Hondureños
regular:1009.desc: Roast beef brochets marinated with vegetables, grilled to the embers in markets.
hints: The beef is cut into cubes and marinated with homemade Honduran adobo
Peppers, onion and tomato alternate with meat in the skewer
Roast in the embers and turn to brown evenly all sides
Popular markets in Tegucigalpa sell them as street food
Served with corn tortillas and freshly prepared tomato chimol

regular:1010.name: Licuado de Jocote
regular:1010.desc: Jocote shake — acid tropical fruit — with milk and sugar, Honduran school drink.
hints: Jocote is a small tropical fruit with very acidic and astringent flavor
It is blended with milk and sugar to soften the intense acidity of the fruit
It is the most popular drink of Honduran school pulperies at 10 am
Jocote in sugar — pickled in brown sugar — is the most popular sweet
It also eats green with salt and spicy chili as street candy

regular:1011.name: Arroz con Leche Hondureño
regular:1011.desc: Rice cooked in milk with cinnamon, clove and brown sugar, birthday dessert.
hints: The clove of smell gives it the spiced aroma that distinguishes it from other versions
Brown sugar gives you the color and taste deeper than white sugar
Cinnamon powder sprinkles on it generously when serving cold
It is the most common dessert on Honduran birthdays and family reunions
It is served very cold after several hours in the refrigerator always

regular:1012.name: Catrachitas Escolares
regular:1012.desc: Small toasted corn with beans, dry cheese and tanned, the Honduran school snack.
hints: They're smaller than the regular catrachitas to be the school snack
Refried beans are put in generous quantity on each tostadite
The dried cheese very dry and salty is grated above the beans
The tanning of acid cabbage is added above as a fresh auction
It's the 10:00 a.m. snack in Honduran schools across the country

regular:1013.name: Frijoles con Chicharrón
regular:1013.desc: Fried black beans served with crispy chicharrón and tortilla, Honduran rural breakfast.
hints: The beans are refried in butter until dry and concentrated in flavor
The very crunchy pork chicharrón is placed on top of the hot beans
The freshly made corn tortilla wraps the beans for the classic bite
It is the most popular breakfast in the Honduran countryside since dawn
The pork butter with which they are cooled gives it the flavor that butter does not give

regular:1014.name: Sopa de Albóndigas Nicaragüense
regular:1014.desc: Meatball beef broth with mint, potato and carrot, homemade nica dish.
hints: Meatballs are made with ground beef, raw rice and mint
They are cooked directly into the vegetable broth when boiled
Peppermint is the herb that gives the most Nicaraguan aroma to broth
Potato and carrot give the body and natural sweetness to broth
It is the soup of Wednesdays and Sundays in Nicaraguan homes

regular:1015.name: Gallopinto del Pacifico
regular:1015.desc: Rice with black beans sautéed with onion, garlic and sweet chili, Pacific version.
hints: Nicaragua’s Pacific has its own version of the gallo pinto national
The sweet pepper gives it the fruity aroma that distinguishes this regional version
Everything is skipped together until the rice is slightly crispy
It is more flavoured than the Caribbean coast version with its local spices
Managua and the Pacific consume this aromatic variant the most

regular:1016.name: Caldo Tlalpeño Nica
regular:1016.desc: Chicken broth with chayote, corn and mint, Central American version of the dish.
hints: Nicaragua has its version of this broth with local vegetables in the country
The chayote and the corn are the vegetables that characterize it most in the region
Weed is the most popular herb in Nicaraguan broths
The chicken with bone gives the most gelatinous and nutritious broth of the dish
It is served in the markets as breakfast or lunch economic and nutritious

regular:1017.name: Quesillo Nicaragüense
regular:1017.desc: Corn tortilla rolled with soft cheese, cream and pickled onion in vinegar.
hints: Nicaraguan quesillo is the coolest and softest cheese in the country
The tortilla is rolled with the shredded cheese and cream inside
The pickled onion in vinegar gives it the acidic touch that balances everything
Nagarote, in the West, has Nicaragua’s most famous stalls
Wrapped in transparent plastic sheet for serving and eating

regular:1018.name: Sopa de Mondongo Nica
regular:1018.desc: Mondongo beef with cassava, plantain and herb, soup from Managua markets.
hints: The mondongo —streets— is cleaned and cooked for hours in the broth
The cassava and the green banana give him the body that makes him so strong
Fresh mint gives you the fresh aroma that distinguishes the Nica version
Managua Markets Serve It On Fridays and Saturdays From Early
It is the most popular recovery dish on weekends in Nicaragua

regular:1019.name: Entamalado Nicaragüense
regular:1019.desc: Roasted green banana wrapped in plantain leaf with curd and cream, rural nica bite.
hints: The green banana roasts whole inside your leaf until softened
The curd — fresh pure cheese — is placed inside when opening the hot banana
The acidic cream completes the sweet-salted-creamy Nicaraguan bite
It is the snack of rural peoples in Nicaragua’s Pacific
It is simpler than tamal but equally nutritious and tasty for the countryside

regular:1020.name: Atol de Pinolillo
regular:1020.desc: A toasted corn drink ground with cocoa and cinnamon, the pinolillo cold or hot Nicaraguan.
hints: pinolillo is Nicaragua’s most identity drink, a national symbol
Roasted corn and cocoa are ground together to make the base powder
It is mixed with cold or hot water and sweetened with sugar to taste
Nicaraguans call themselves pinoleros for love of this historic drink
It has a darker and more intense flavor than similar Mexican champurrado

regular:1021.name: Chanfaina Nica
regular:1021.desc: Cheese of beef viscera with potato, tomato and spices, economic dish of the markets.
hints: Viscera — liver and mouth — are cooked in tomato sauce and onion
The Pope gives it consistency and the body that makes it more nutritious
Cumin and oregano are the spices that most aromatize it
Managua’s popular markets serve it from 7 a.m
It is the cheapest and most nutritious dish of market workers

regular:1022.name: Ayote en Dulce
regular:1022.desc: Pumpkin — ayote— cooked in panela syrup with cinnamon and clove, pure peasant dessert.
hints: The ayote —calabaza— is cut into pieces and cooked in dark panela syrup
The clove and cinnamon aromatize the syrup during all slow cooking
It is the most traditional dessert of rural peoples in the Nicaraguan Pacific
Cold served with acidic cream above for sweet-salted contrast
October and the Ayote season is when it consumes most in Nicaragua

regular:1023.name: Tortilla de Maíz Nica
regular:1023.desc: Thick corn tortilla cooked in comal with firewood, the base of Nicaraguan food.
hints: Nicaraguan tortilla is thicker and smaller than Mexican or Guatemalan tortilla
Cooked in a comal on wood stove giving a special smoky flavor
It accompanies absolutely all the dishes of Nicaraguan daily cuisine
Peasant women do it from 4 in the morning every day
No Nicaraguan food complete without corn tortilla on the table

regular:1024.name: Arroz a la Valenciana Nica
regular:1024.desc: Rice with chicken, vegetables and saffron, Nicaraguan version of Spanish festive rice.
hints: Nicaragua adopted this version of the festive rice of colonial Spanish cuisine
The chicken is cooked first and then cooked next to the rice with the broth
Saffron or bead gives intense yellow color to rice
It's the rice of weddings and important celebrations in Nicaragua
It differs from rice with chicken to bring more spices and saffron

regular:1025.name: Pozol Nica
regular:1025.desc: Corn drink fermented with water and salt, labor drink from the Nicaraguan countryside.
hints: Maize is cooked and fermented for several days until the acidic flavor is developed
It is mixed with cold water to make the field refreshing drink
It is more acidic and fermented than pinolillo for fermentation time
Rural areas in the Pacific and North consume it during agricultural work
It is carried in canteens to the countryside as the most nutritious and refreshing water

regular:1026.name: Sopa de Res Festiva Nica
regular:1026.desc: Queue soup and rib of beef with cassava, potato and güisquil, for weddings and big parties.
hints: It takes at least three kilos of meat to make this festive soup
The tail and rib give the most gelatinous and tasty broth of all parts
The cassava and the pope give her the body that makes her so forceful and special
Prepares for weddings, fifteen years and community celebrations
Nicaragua serves it in the early morning of the nighttime holidays

regular:1027.name: Guacho de Rabito
regular:1027.desc: Broth rice with pork, guandu and cilantro, dish of the Panamanian interior.
hints: Pork rabit gives you the most gelatinous broth and rich in collagen
Guandú —palo beans—is the most Panamanian ingredient in guacho
The broad-leaf cilantro gives it the scent that distinguishes any Panamanian guacho
The provinces of Herrera and Los Santos are famous for this version of the guacho
It is served very hot at breakfast in the popular markets of the interior

regular:1028.name: Tortilla Panameña
regular:1028.desc: Thick corn tortilla cooked in comal with butter, different from Central America.
hints: Panamanian tortilla is thicker and whiter than the rest of Central America
It rubs with generous butter while it's still hot from the griddle
Accompany any Panamanian breakfast next to the pastry and carimañola
The central provinces of Azuero have the largest and thickest tortillas
It is so important in Panamanian cuisine that it is made for all times

regular:1029.name: Sancocho Nacional Panameño
regular:1029.desc: The sancocho Panamanian chicken with otoe, yam and colantro, considered the national dish.
hints: The sancocho Panamanian is considered the most representative national dish in the country
The field hen is the one that gives you the most concentrated and authentic broth
Otoe and yam are typically Panamanian roots that cannot be missed
The cilantro—a wide leaf—gives the most Panamanian aroma of all ingredients
It is the dish of any celebration and favorite remedy for any discomfort

regular:1030.name: Pesada de Guandú Panameña
regular:1030.desc: Guandú beans in coconut milk with sugar and cinnamon, Christmas dessert of the interior.
hints: Guandú (green stick beans) is the most Panamanian legume that exists
It is cooked in coconut milk until very tender and sweet for sugar
Cinnamon and sugar give you the dessert profile instead of salty dish
It is the Christmas dessert of the provinces of Azuero and Herrera del interior
Penonomé and the interior consume it in the holidays of December mainly

regular:1031.name: Chicha de Maíz Panameña
regular:1031.desc: Refreshing corn drink cooked with pineapple and spices, unfermented, from the inside.
hints: This chicha Panamanian is not fermented unlike the Andean
The corn is boiled with pineapple and spices to make the base sweet and aromatic
It is served cold as a drink of the patron saintly celebrations of the interior of the country
Central provinces produce the best known chicha maize in Panama
It is the craft drink of Panamanian folk fairs and festivals

regular:1032.name: Guandú con Coco
regular:1032.desc: Rice cooked with sweet guandú and coconut milk, accompaniment of the Panamanian New Year.
hints: The tender green guandu has a different flavor to the dry guandu inside
Coconut milk gives you the creaminess and tropical flavor of the Caribbean
It is the New Year dish in many Panamanian families by tradition
The rice is dyed green by the tender guandu that is cooked together
Panama City has adopted it from Panamanian Caribbean tradition

regular:1033.name: Empanadas de Maíz Panameñas
regular:1033.desc: Maize pies stuffed with meat and cheese, fried until crispy.
hints: The yellow corn dough gives you the typical Panamanian texture and golden color
They are smaller than the carimañolas of yuca but just as popular
The filling of ground meat with sofrito Panamanian is the most traditional
They are served as breakfast next to the beans in the markets of the country
Panamanian white cheese can replace meat in the vegetarian version

regular:1034.name: Ceviche de Corvina Panameño
regular:1034.desc: Fresh Corvina marinated in lemon with cilantro, aji chombo and onion, ceviche tropical.
hints: The Panamanian Pacific Corvina is the most appreciated for the ceviche
The cilantro —a wide leaf— gives it the green aroma that distinguishes it from Peruvian
The very spicy chili pepper gives you the Caribbean heat that makes it so special
Panama City has open cevicherías from early on in the markets
It is different from the ceviche Peruvian in the use of cilantro and aji chombo

regular:1035.name: Sopa Borracha Panameña
regular:1035.desc: Orange cake bathed in rum syrup, Panama's most intoxicating dessert.
hints: The cake gets drunk in Panamanian rum syrup
Panamanian Seco Herrerano rum is the most traditional alcoholic ingredient
It is the dessert of weddings and large celebrations in the interior of the country
Herrera and Los Santos are the provinces best known for this recipe
The cake absorbs the rum syrup for hours before serving

regular:1036.name: Patacones con Guacamole Panameño
regular:1036.desc: Green banana toast with Panamanian guacamole, modern aperitif.
hints: The Panamanian guacamole carries broad-leaf cilantro instead of fine coriander
Tostones become the same as in all Central America with double frying
The combination is very popular in restaurants in Panama City
Spicy chili can be added to the guacamole for those who like spicy
It is one of the most popular appetizers in the bars of Casco Viejo Panamanian

regular:1037.name: Arroz con Pollo a la Panameña
regular:1037.desc: Rice with chicken and cilantro, the most cooked birthday dish in Panama.
hints: The broad-leaf cilantro gives you the flavor that distinguishes rice with Panamanian chicken
The chicken is cooked next to the rice from the beginning in the same hot pot
The achiote gives it the golden color and earthy flavor that characterizes it
It's the birthday dish and school parties all over the country
It differs from Venezuelan in the cilantro and Cuban in the most abundant achiote

regular:1038.name: Chipá So'o
regular:1038.desc: Chipa stuffed with ground meat and spices, the version with traditional chipa filling.
hints: So'o in Guarani means meat, hence the name of this special chipa
Seasoned ground meat is enclosed within the starch dough
Bake just like the normal chipa until browning the dough on the outside
It's stronger than the normal chip for meat filling inside
Asunción sells them in specialty bakeries especially on Saturdays

regular:1039.name: Mbaipy Paraguayo
regular:1039.desc: Paraguayan corn polenta cooked in milk with cheese, the soft and creamy version.
hints: It is the Paraguayan polenta but cooked in milk instead of water to be creamier
Fresh Paraguayan cheese gives the salty flavor that balances sweet milk
It's different from the sopa paraguaya in being more liquid and creamy, like puree
Served hot as a side dish or as a unique dish with meat next to it
The version with sugar and cinnamon is consumed as dessert in some regions

regular:1040.name: Guiso Carretero
regular:1040.desc: Dried beef stew with rice, onion and tomato, dish of the field truckers.
hints: Dried meat is rehydrated and shredded before mixing with rice
Truckers and drivers cooked it during trips around the countryside
Rice and dried meat are cooked together in a single pot with vegetables
It is very similar to Brazilian rice reel due to the same traveler origin
Asunción and the interior consume it as a midday economic dish

regular:1041.name: Borí Borí de Pollo
regular:1041.desc: Chicken soup with corn balls and cheese, the most classic version of borí borí.
hints: The chicken gives it a lighter and less fatty broth than the stew hen
Corn and cheese balls are the most characteristic element of the dish
They differ from the bori bori de res in the softest taste of chicken
It is the dish that most eats in urban households of Asunción
The consistency of the soup is thickened by the pellets that dissolve

regular:1042.name: Lampreado Paraguayo
regular:1042.desc: Manioc tortilla (yuca) fried with cheese and herbs, appetizer of the Paraguayan countryside.
hints: The cooked cassava is kneaded with cheese and herbs before frying in tortilla form
Fresh Paraguayan cheese melts inside when the tortilla is fried
It is the simplest and fastest appetizer in the Paraguayan countryside for visitors
Freshly fried hot served with an optional Paraguayan cane cup
It is different from the mbeju in the softest consistency and flattened shape

regular:1043.name: Arro Ko'ê Paraguayo
regular:1043.desc: Creamy rice cooked in broth with milk and cheese, the 'soup' of breakfast rice.
hints: Ko'ê means sunrise in Guaraní, it is the rice of Paraguayan breakfast
Rice is cooked in chicken broth until very creamy and soft
Milk and cheese are added at the end to make texture richer
It is the breakfast of cold winter days in indoor homes
It's different from lunch rice to be creamier and sweeter

regular:1044.name: Dulce de Mamón
regular:1044.desc: Papaya — mamón— cooked green in sugar syrup with cloves, Paraguayan artisan dessert.
hints: The green sucker is the young papaya before ripening, without natural sweetness
Cooked for hours in sugar syrup with clove until translucent
The clove of smell gives the spiced aroma to the dark and bright syrup
It is the sweet artisan most exported by Paraguay to Argentina and Brazil
Cold served with fresh Paraguayan cheese for sweet-salted contrast

regular:1045.name: Mbeju Salado
regular:1045.desc: Salty version of the mbeju with chicharrón and salt, more forceful than the simple version.
hints: The pork chicharrón is mixed directly into the starch dough
The result is fatter and saltier than the only cheese and starch bebeju
It is the version of the Paraguayan field for hard work breakfast
It is eaten especially in rural areas where chicharrón abounds
The fat of the chicharrón gives it the untuosity that makes it very satisfying

regular:1046.name: Chipa Guazú de Choclo
regular:1046.desc: Version of chipa guazú with choclo tender instead of dry, wet corn flour.
hints: The choclo tender grated gives you the moisture and sweetness that doesn't have dry corn
It's sweeter and juicy than the chipa Guazu of dehydrated corn flour
Bake in mold until spongy inside and golden on top
It's the favorite version of summer months when choclo is fresh
Asunción and the metropolitan area are where this variant is most consumed

regular:1047.name: Kivevé con Chicharrón
regular:1047.desc: Pumpkin puree with crispy chicharrón mixed inside, salty version of the kivevé.
hints: The pork chicharrón is incorporated into the sweet kivevé giving the salty flavor
The sweet contrast of the pumpkin with the chicharrón salt is unique
It is the strongest and most protein version of traditional Paraguayan kivevé
Rural areas of Eastern Paraguay consume it as a full lunch
It is a very fast and nutritious one-pot dish for the countryside

regular:1048.name: Arroz con Leche Guaraní
regular:1048.desc: Rice in milk with grated coconut and good grass, Paraguayan version with Guaraní aroma.
hints: The grated coconut gives the tropical flavor that distinguishes this Paraguayan version
The good weed — the good weeds — infused aromatize milk before cooking
It is the most aromatic and Guaraní version of rice with classic milk
The Paraguayan interior consumes it during family holidays and celebrations
It is served cold with cinnamon and additional coconut sprinkled above

regular:1049.name: Pupusa de Loroco con Queso
regular:1049.desc: Pupusa thick corn stuffed with parrot blossom and fresh cheese, the most Salvadoran.
hints: The parrot is an edible flower that only grows in El Salvador and Guatemala
The Loroco-cheese combination is definitely the favorite of Salvadorans
The dough is worked by hand until perfectly sealed and smooth
Cook in a griddle without oil until brown spots appear in the dough
Served with fermented cabbage tanning and homemade tomato sauce always

regular:1050.name: Tamale de Pollo Salvadoreño
regular:1050.desc: Tamal dough stuffed chicken in red errand, wrapped in steamed banana leaf.
hints: The banana leaf gives you the green aroma that wraps the whole dough
The red chile and tomato errand is the sauce that seasons chicken
It’s different from Nicaragua’s nacatamal in being smaller and drier
Sundays are the day of tamales in San Salvador markets
They bind in pairs and boil for two hours to fully cook

regular:1051.name: Sopa de Res Salvadoreña
regular:1051.desc: Broth of beef rib with güisquil, yucca, potato and fresh cilantro, the Sunday broth.
hints: Güisquil — chayote — and yucca are the most Salvadoran vegetables in the stock
The rib with bone gives the most gelatinous and nutritious broth
The fresh cilantro at the end gives it the most Central American scent possible
It is the most traditional Sunday lunch of Salvadoran families
Served with corn tortillas and pickled jalapeño spicy pepper

regular:1052.name: Enchiladas Salvadoreñas
regular:1052.desc: Maize toast with stewed meat, betabel, lettuce and dried grated cheese, different from Mexico.
hints: Salvadoran enchiladas are toasted, not tortillas with salsa like in Mexico
The grated betabel gives you the pink and earthy touch that visually distinguishes them
The meat stewed and shredded goes over the toast without red sauce
Dry hard cheese grates in abundance over all ingredients
They are the most popular snack or snack in San Salvador markets

regular:1053.name: Pan de Yema Salvadoreño
regular:1053.desc: Sweet bread made with egg yolks, sugar and sesame, the Salvadoran holy week bread.
hints: The abundant egg yolks give the intense golden color to the bread
The sesame on top distinguishes it from any other sweet bread in the region
It is the most expected bread of Easter in all Salvadoran cuisine
San Salvador's traditional bakeries have been doing so for generations
Purchased in dozens to share with family during the Week of Majority

regular:1054.name: Sopa de Frijoles con Chicharrón
regular:1054.desc: Cream of red beans with chopped chicharrón and acidic cream, the favorite soup of the week.
hints: The red beans are completely blended to make the cream thick
The crunchy chopped chicharrón is placed on top when serving so as not to lose the creak
The acidic cream contrasts with the intensity of liquefied red beans
It's the most consumed midweek soup in Salvadoran homes
Served with white rice and corn tortillas for full lunch

regular:1055.name: Caldo de Mariscos Salvadoreño
regular:1055.desc: Fresh Pacific seafood soup with yucca, banana and cilantro, coastal dish.
hints: The seafood of the Salvadoran Pacific are of high quality and very fresh
The cassava and the green banana give him the body that makes him so strong
The fresh cilantro at the end gives the Central American aromatic touch
La Libertad and Puerto El Triunfo are the best places for this broth
It is accompanied by corn tortillas and pickled jalapeno pepper always

regular:1056.name: Rellenitos de Frijol
regular:1056.desc: Mature banana chips stuffed with sweet black beans, shared with Guatemala.
hints: The crushed ripe banana covers the filling of black bean cooked with sugar
They are very similar to Guatemalan fillets because of their shared origin
They are fried in oil until golden browned and sprinkled with sugar and cinnamon
They are the most shared street dessert in San Salvador markets
The sweet black bean contrasts with the salty exterior of fried ripe banana

regular:1057.name: Atol Chuco
regular:1057.desc: Hot drink of black corn fermented with beans and chili, ancestral and nutritious.
hints: Fermented black corn gives it the acidic flavor and the characteristic greyish color
The ground beans give the thickness and protein to the hot drink
The chili gives it the mild itching that makes it a full hot breakfast
It is the oldest pre-Columbian drink that keeps alive in El Salvador
San Salvador sells it in street stalls from 4 a.m. daily

regular:1058.name: Pollo en Crema Salvadoreño
regular:1058.desc: Chicken in cream milk sauce with loroco and sweet chili, homemade festive dish.
hints: The parrot —flower— gives it the unique aroma that distinguishes the Salvadoran version
The cream of milk thickens the sauce until it becomes very smooth and smooth
The sweet green chili gives the flavor and fresh color to the creamy sauce
It is the favorite Sunday dish of well-off Salvadoran families
Served with white rice and cabbage salad with lemon and tomato

regular:1059.name: Nuégados de Yuca
regular:1059.desc: Yucca chips with cheese and anise bathed in panela honey, Easter dessert.
hints: The cooked cassava is mixed with cheese and anise before forming into balls
Fry in hot oil until golden on the outside
Hot panela honey with clove and cinnamon is poured over when serving
They are the most typical dessert of Easter in all markets of the country
Anise gives you the festive aroma that differentiates them from simple fritters

regular:1060.name: Sopa de Patas con Loroco
regular:1060.desc: Soup of leg of beef with parrot, corn and spices, version with the Salvadoran flower.
hints: The parrot gives it the unique aroma that makes this soup unmistakable Salvadorian
The legs of cooked beef hours gives you the most gelatinous and comforting broth
Grain corn gives sweetness and consistency to thick broth
San Salvador serves it in specialized restaurants from early on
It is the soup of Sunday celebration and special market days

regular:1061.name: Sopa Negra Tica
regular:1061.desc: Soup of black beans with poached egg, cheese and cilantro, rich and comforting breakfast.
hints: Black beans are cooked with onion, garlic and cilantro until softened
The egg is poached directly in the hot soup when serving
The tender cheese and the acidic cream are added over as final decoration
It is one of the most consumed soups in breakfasts of sodas
It differs from gallo pinto in being a liquid soup and not sautéed rice

regular:1062.name: Casado Tico
regular:1062.desc: Costa Rican day dish with rice, beans, meat, salad and banana, national lunch.
hints: The married man is the lunch par excellence of sodas — restaurants —
Rice and beans are the irreplaceable basis of any Costa Rican married man
Meat can be chicken, beef, pork or fish according to the preference of the day
Mature fried banana and fresh salad always complete the dish
The name comes from what you eat when you're married and have a home

regular:1063.name: Gallo Pinto de Arroz Negro
regular:1063.desc: Gallo pinto Costa Rican with Lizano sauce, the national breakfast of sodas.
hints: Lizano salsa is the exclusive signature of the Costa Rican gallo pinto
Without Lizano salsa is not authentic gallo pinto Costa Rica
The rice is sautéed with black beans until well mixed
Served with egg and Costa Rican acidic cream in full breakfast
Nicaragua disputes with Costa Rica which has the best gallo pinto in the region

regular:1064.name: Olla de Carne Completa
regular:1064.desc: Festive beef soup with all tubers: yampi, chayote, yucca, tiquizque and papa.
hints: Yampi and Tiquizque are specific tubers of Costa Rica
The Costa Rican chayote is the most emblematic vegetable of the meat pot
It is cooked with all tubers available on the farm during harvest
It's the dish of parties and big family events in the country
Served with white rice in a separate dish to absorb broth

regular:1065.name: Picadillo de Arracache Costarricense
regular:1065.desc: Arracache cooked with ground pork, onion, sweet chili and coriander, garnish tica.
hints: Arracache is a unique aromatic white tuber of Costa Rica and the Andes
The ground pork gives the salty flavor and protein to the vegetable picadillo
The broad-leaf cilantro gives you the most Costa Rican aroma of the dish
It is the most Costa Rican picadillo for the arracache that is only cultivated here
San José and the Central Valley consider it part of the national creole cuisine

regular:1066.name: Tamale de Navidad Tico
regular:1066.desc: Tamal Costa Rican dough with pork, rice, olives and raisins, Christmas on a leaf.
hints: The olives and raisins in Mexico differentiate it from the tamales
The dough carries lard and broth to be very soft and fluffy
Wrapped in banana leaf and cooked in pairs for two hours
It is the most laborious and expected Christmas dish in the whole family
Each family has its secret recipe passed from grandparents to grandchildren

regular:1067.name: Natilla Costarricense
regular:1067.desc: Natural acid cream very thick and dense, the most lactic dairy product of all.
hints: Natilla tica is the thickest acidic cream in the world, almost solid
It is produced in the dairy stores of the Central Valley with quality whole milk
Accompanied by gallo pinto, the tamales and any typical Costa Rican dish
It is so thick that you can cut it with a knife and not fall from the spoon
The acidic and creamy taste makes it irreplaceable on the breakfast table

regular:1068.name: Sopa de Frijoles con Albóndigas
regular:1068.desc: Soup of black beans with mini beef meatballs, the broth of the Ticos Mondays.
hints: Mini beef meatballs with rice are made very small for soup
Black beans cooked to soften form the thick base broth
The fresh cilantro and natilla are added when serving each individual dish
It is the dish of utilization of the gallo pinto surplus of the weekend
It is especially eaten on Mondays in the neighborhood sodas of San José

regular:1069.name: Arroz con Pollo Tico
regular:1069.desc: Rice with Costa Rican chicken with cilantro, Lizano sauce and colorful vegetables.
hints: The Lizano salsa gives the sweet and spicy flavor only to rice
The broad-leaf cilantro is the main aromatic of Costa Rican cuisine
Colorful vegetables — red pepper, green, corn — give you visual joy
It's the dish of school parties and birthdays all over the country
It differs from Nicaraguan in Lizano salsa that only exists in Costa Rica

regular:1070.name: Tortilla de Queso Tica
regular:1070.desc: Thick corn tortilla with melted turrialba cheese inside, Caribbean specialty.
hints: Turrialba cheese is Costa Rica's most famous, creamy and soft cheese
It gets inside the corn tortilla before sealing into the hot griddle
The Caribbean region — Limón — popularized it with the coolest cheese in the country
It is eaten hot directly from the griddle so that the cheese is melted
It is the Costa Rican version of quesadilla without wheat flour tortilla

regular:1071.name: Palmito con Natilla
regular:1071.desc: Heart of fresh palm in slices with acidic cream and lemon, Costa Rican salad.
hints: Costa Rica produces the best palm in Central America in the wet Caribbean
The fresh palm — not canned — has a crispy texture and unrivalled softness
Costa Rican creamy, acidic and thick gives creamy dressing
It is one of the few places where the palm is consumed fresh from the same day
It is especially consumed in Caribbean and Central Valley restaurants

regular:1072.name: Chifrijo Costarricense
regular:1072.desc: Cup of chicharrón and beans with rooster beak and tortilla chips, the food bar tico.
hints: The name comes from CHICharron + FRIJoles, the two main ingredients
Born in the bars of San Jose in the 90s as beer mouths
The tomato, cilantro and chili cock peak gives you the tropical freshness
The tortilla chips are placed around the glass to wet and accompany
It is the most popular bar aperitif in Costa Rica, typical of weekends

regular:1073.name: Mondongo Tico con Culantro
regular:1073.desc: mondongo soup with chickpeas, potato, cilantro and sweet chili, Sunday dish.
hints: The broad-leaf cilantro gives you the scent that distinguishes you from other mondongos
The chickpeas give consistency and extra protein to the broth
The sweet chili — pepper— gives the taste and fresh color to the dark broth

Dakar has the best thiéboudienne restaurants in the whole country
It is eaten shared in a large tray with everyone sitting around

sunday:54.name: Nasi Lemak
sunday:54.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk with fried anchovies, peanuts, egg and chili sambal.
hints: Rice is cooked in coconut milk with ginger and lemon grass
The sambal—fermented chili sauce—gives it the itching that identifies it
The crispy fried anchovies and roasted peanuts are the base garrison
Wrapped in banana leaf for Kuala Lumpur street breakfast
Malaysia considers it its national dish although Singapore also claims it

sunday:55.name: Varenyky
sunday:55.desc: Boiled dough empanadillas stuffed with potato and cheese or sour cherry, the Ukrainian pierogi.
hints: They are practically the same as Polish pierogi but with their own national recipes
The sweet version of sour cherry is the most popular dessert
Served with caramelized onion and butter in the classic salt version
Ukraine claims them with the same pride that Poland claims its pierogi
Poltava, in the center of the country, has the largest annual varenyky party

sunday:56.name: Stroopwafel
sunday:56.desc: Two fine biscuits joined together by a filling of molasses and cinnamon, put on the hot coffee to soften.
hints: It is placed on the cup of hot coffee so that steam heats the filling
The Dutch molasses—stroop—is the sweet, sticky filling that gives them their name
Gouda in the Netherlands is the city that invented them in the 19th century
They are the most recognizable snack of Dutch airports for tourists
The filling is made with dark molasses, butter, cinnamon and vanilla mixed

sunday:57.name: Köttbullar con Salsa
sunday:57.desc: Pork and veal meatballs in creamy cream sauce and broth, with red cranberry jam.
hints: Red blueberry jam is the most surprising and typical accompaniment
The sauce is made with meatball juice, beef broth and thick cream
Sweden claims them although the recipe came from Turkey with King Charles XII
IKEA popularized them globally in millions of people who eat in their restaurants
The mixture of ground pork and veal gives them the balanced texture and flavor

sunday:58.name: Fondue de Queso
sunday:58.desc: Gruyère and Emmental cheeses melted in white wine, with garlic and kirsch, to dip bread in casserole.
hints: Dry white wine creates emulsion with cheese so it doesn't get too thick
kirsch — cherry spirit — is added at the end to flavour and cut fat
The Swiss Alps have the oldest and most documented fondue tradition in Europe
It is served in a clay casserole—caquelon—on an alcohol stove
The rule says if you drop bread on the fondue, you have to pay for a round of drinks

sunday:59.name: Wiener Schnitzel
sunday:59.desc: Very thin beef fillet empanado in egg and breadcrumbs, fried in butter and oil until brown.
hints: It can only be called Wiener Schnitzel if it is made with beef, never pork
The overflow must not stick to the meat so that it will crack when frying
Vienna claims it as its most emblematic and identity dish in the country
Served with lemon slice and cucumber or potato salad
The clarified butter gives you the most authentic flavor of the historical version

sunday:60.name: Gaufre Belga
sunday:60.desc: Crispy waffle with vanilla levada dough, served with whipped cream, strawberries and chocolate.
hints: The dough carries yeast that gives it the spongy texture inside
Brussels and Liege have two different versions with different ingredients
The Brussels gaufe is rectangular and crisper than that of Liege
Sold in street stalls with Nutella, cream or only sugar icing
Belgium has more than 11 different regional varieties of waffle throughout the region

sunday:61.name: Irish Stew
sunday:61.desc: Lamb stew with potato, onion and parsley, Ireland's simplest and oldest stew.
hints: Potato is the most important ingredient in Irish famine history
The lamb of the Irish Aran Islands is most appreciated for stew
It cooks very slowly for hours with water and very little seasoning
The chopped fresh parsley is the only ornament served in the deep bowl
It is so simple that it only has four ingredients: lamb, potato, onion and water

sunday:62.name: Doubles
sunday:62.desc: Two bara — fried flour breads — stuffed with curry chickpeas, Trinidadian street snack.
hints: The bara — fried flat breads — are made of flour seasoned with turmeric
Channa — chickpeas— are cooked curry with spices from the Caribbean and India
The Indian influence in Trinidad is due to the workers arrived in the 19th century
They eat at breakfast on the way to work in Port of Spain
The pepper willow handle and the tamanind willow are added according to the taste of each

sunday:63.name: Pepperpot
sunday:63.desc: Dark beef stew with cassareep, casabe and chili, Christmas dish of the Guyanese Amerindians.
hints: Cassareep — concentrated juice of fermented yucca — gives it the intense black color
It is Guyana's most traditional Christmas dish, prepared on December 25th
It originates in Amerindian villages Arawak before European colonization
Meat is stored for days in the cassareep without cooling
Georgetown, capital of Guyana, serves it in every home on Christmas Day

sunday:64.name: Stew Chicken Beliceño
sunday:64.desc: Chicken stewed in dark red errand sauce, achiote and Mayan spices, daily dish of Belize.
hints: The red errand — achiote paste and Mayan spices — gives it the unique color and flavor
Belize shares with Guatemala the Mayan influence on its daily cuisine
Served with coconut rice and stewed beans in the most Belizean combination
Belize City has stew chicken restaurants since 7 a.m
Caramelized onion and garlic are the aromatic base of dark stew

sunday:65.name: Ghormeh Sabzi
sunday:65.desc: Persian stew of fresh green herbs with lamb, dried Persian lemons and red beans.
hints: Herbs — parsley, cilantro, alholva — are salted in oil before adding to the stew
Dehydrated Persian lemons —limu omani— give you the acidity that distinguishes it
It is the most beloved Persian dish and the one Iranians miss most in the diaspora
Cook for three hours until herbs darken and concentrate
Tehran consumes it especially on Fridays, holidays of Iran, family

sunday:66.name: Biryani Pakistaní
sunday:66.desc: Basmati rice with spicy lamb, saffron, fried onion and Karachi spices, more spicy than the Indian.
hints: Karachi has the most spicy and spicy biryani style of the entire subcontinent
Masala spice paste is different from Indian by the use of dried red chilies
The dum — steamed cooking capped — is the key technique of authentic biryani
Pakistan and India share the origin of biryani but have their own styles
The golden fried onion and mint leaves decorate the biryani when serving

sunday:67.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
sunday:67.desc: Chicken cooked in ginger and garlic broth, with rice cooked in the same broth, and three sauces.
hints: The chicken is soaked in ginger and garlic broth and cooked at low temperature
The rice is cooked in the same concentrated chicken broth to absorb flavor
Three sauces always accompany: chili, ginger and dark soy
Hawker centers in Singapore have the best and most awarded in the country
The origin is in Hainan, China, but Singapore adopted and perfected it

sunday:68.name: Nyama Choma
sunday:68.desc: Goat meat or beef roasted to the embers slowly, served with fresh ugali and kachumbari.
hints: The name literally means 'roasted meat' in Swahili, the most spoken language
The goat is the most popular meat for its more intense flavor and ease of raising
The ugali — corn polenta— is the irreplaceable accompaniment on each dish
Kachumbari — tomato salad and onion with chili — brings the final freshness
Nairobi has nyama choma joints open until late at night always

sunday:69.name: Groundnut Soup
sunday:69.desc: Thick soup of roasted peanuts ground with chicken, tomato and spices, Ghanaian ceremonial dish.
hints: Peanuts roast and grind to form the paste that thickens the soup
The roasted tomato and chili give it the red color and itching that balance the peanut
It is served with fufu —poached cassava ball— to soak in thick soup
It is the Sunday dish and important family ceremonies in Ghana
Accra has the best groundnut soup restaurants in the whole country

sunday:70.name: Mohinga
sunday:70.desc: Soup of rice noodles in catfish broth and lemon grass, with egg and crispy fried on top.
hints: It is Myanmar’s official national breakfast — formerly Burma — by decree
The broth is made with fresh catfish, lemon grass, onion and ginger
The crispy fried onion and chickpea paste go over when serving
It's been sold at Rangoon street stalls since 5 a.m
The name comes from the mixture of words mo — soft — and hin — stew — in Burmese

sunday:71.name: Hilsa al Curry
sunday:71.desc: Fish hilsa —the tarpon of the Ganges— in yellow mustard curry and turmeric, Bangladeshi identity dish.
hints: The hilsa —ish — is the national fish of Bangladesh and the most precious subcontinent
The mustard seed ground in yellow gives you the most Bangladeshi curry possible
Turmeric dyes intense yellow broth and gives it the earthy flavor
Dhaka and all of Bangladesh consume it especially in the monsoon season
The fish is cooked whole or in pieces with thorns to give more flavor to curry
